description: A transcriptional regulator primarily expressed in medullary thymic epithelial cells. It plays an important role in immunity by regulating the expression of a wide array of SELF-ANTIGENS and negative selection of autoreactive T-cells in the thymus. Deficiency in this protein induces a rare autosomal-recessive disease called AUTOIMMUNE POLYENDOCRINOPATHY-CANDIDIASIS-ECTODERMAL DYSTROPHY.

name: Treatment Effect Heterogeneity
description: The varying of responses to a given intervention or treatment that occurs across patients or patient subgroups.

name: Translesion DNA Synthesis
description: DNA damage tolerant, error-prone DNA replication by specialized DNA POLYMERASES that can accommodate damaged bases in their active sites and insert NUCLEOTIDES in the strand directly opposite the DNA DAMAGE.

name: Nudix Hydrolases
description: A group of Mg2+/Mn2+-dependent mainly pyrophosphohydrolases that hydrolyzes structures of NUcleoside DIphosphate linked to another moiety X to nucleoside monophosphate and X-Phosphate. Nudix hydrolases share conserved Nudix box (GX5EX7REUXEEXGU) and degrade variety of substrates including oxidized nucleotides (e.g., MutT) and metabolic intermediates (e.g., THIAMINE PYROPHOSPHATASE). In humans, Nudix superfamily proteins such as MutT proteins participate in DNA damage repairs. Mutations on a nudix hydrolase (NUDT15) are associated with a PURINE-PYRIMIDINE METABOLISM, INBORN ERRORS disorder called THPM2, and mutations in nudix hydrolase (NUDT2) are associated with IDDPN, a developmental intellectual disorder.

name: Brainwashing
description: A broad class of intense and often coercive tactics intended to produce profound changes in attitudes, beliefs, and emotions. Targets of such tactics have typically been prisoners of war and members of religious cults. (From https://dictionary.apa.org/brainwashing)

name: Workforce Diversity
description: Diversity encompasses the range of similarities and differences each individual brings to the workplace, including but not limited to national origin, language, race, color, disability, ethnicity, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, socioeconomic status, veteran status, and family structures. (hud.gov/program_offices/administration/admabout/diversity_inclusion/definitions#diversity)

name: Unvaccinated Persons
description: People who have not been vaccinated against a communicable disease.

name: Urea Transporters
description: Transmembrane carrier proteins responsible for urea movement across the cell membrane. Urea transporters are divided into renal tubular/testicular type (urea transporter 2 consisting of (UT) A1 to A5, encoded by SLC14A2 gene) and erythrocyte type (urea transporter 2 or UT-B1 encoded by the SLC14A1 gene). In humans mutations on the SLC14A1 gene determines KIDD BLOOD-GROUP SYSTEM.

name: Ginkgo Extract
description: Preparations of GINKGO BILOBA. They contain various ANTIOXIDANTS including FLAVONOIDS and TERPENES (e.g., XANTHOPHYLLS).

name: Calponins
description: A family of actin binding proteins mostly in smooth muscle. Calponins include most abundant alpha-calponin (h1 or basic); beta-calponin; neutral calponin (h2 calponin); acidic calponin, SM22, and transgelin. Calponin family members have N-terminal single Calponin Homology (CH) domain and multiple C-terminus 23-amino acids long calponin-like repeats called CLICK-23. Calponins participate in modulation of smooth muscle contraction by binding to ACTINS (F- and G-Actins), CALMODULIN and TROPOMYSIN.

name: Acetonitriles
description: Compounds in which a methyl group is attached to the cyano moiety.

name: Gap Junction beta-1 Protein
description: A GAP JUNCTION beta subunit containing four transmembrane domains expressed in myelinating SCHWANN CELLS and is localized to peripheral MYELIN (e.g., noncompact myelin in the paranode and Schmitt-Lanterman incisures). Mutations in the human gene GJB1 are associated with X-linked CHARCOT-MARIE-TOOTH DISEASE type 1 (CMT1X).

name: Gap Junction alpha-5 Protein
description: A GAP JUNCTION alpha subunit containing four transmembrane domains expressed in the atrial myocardium and ventricular HEART CONDUCTION SYSTEM including PURKINJE FIBERS. Mutations in the human gene GJA5 are associated with cardiac conduction abnormalities such as a familial ATRIAL FIBRILLATION.

name: Gap Junction delta-2 Protein
description: A GAP JUNCTION delta subunit containing four transmembrane domains expressed in the PANCREATIC BETA CELLS, retinal CONE PHOTORECEPTOR CELLS, hippocampal INTERNEURONS, and dendrites in the OLIVARY NUCLEUS and THALAMIC NUCLEI.

name: Gap Junction alpha-4 Protein
description: A GAP JUNCTION alpha subunit containing four transmembrane domains expressed in the adipose cells and myocardium. Mutations in the human gene GJA4 are risk factors for ATHEROSCLEROSIS and MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION.

name: Deltainfluenzavirus
description: A genus of the family ORTHOMYXOVIRIDAE comprising viruses similar to type C, lacking NEURAMINIDASE and using hemagglutinin-esterase fusion (HEF) protein for attachment. Unlike in other influenza virus genera viral NEP is not produced via alternatively spliced non-structural protein mRNA (NS1). Deltainfluenzavirus mostly infect nonhuman hosts, e.g., cattle and swine and in human causes acute febrile respiratory tract infection. Influenza D virus is the type species.

name: Acylphosphatase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of an acylphosphate and water to a carboxylate and phosphate.

name: Influenza A Virus, H5N6 Subtype
description: A subtype of INFLUENZA A VIRUS comprised of the surface proteins hemagglutinin 5 and neuraminidase 6. The H5N6 subtype, frequently referred to as the bird flu virus, is endemic in wild birds and very contagious among both domestic (POULTRY) and wild birds. H5N6 does not usually infect humans, but some cases have been reported with high mortality rate similar to another highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5) virus H5N1 AVIAN INFLUENZA VIRUS.

name: Treatment Interruption
description: A deliberate decision between the patient and health care provider to stop medication for a defined period of time and for a specific clinical purpose.

name: Interleukin-22
description: An interleukin that plays a critical role in modulating tissue responses during inflammation, and in WOUND HEALING.

name: Kir5.1 Channel
description: An inwardly-rectifying potassium channel that allows potassium to flow into rather than out of a cell. It selectively co-assembles with two other inward-rectifier type potassium channels, Kir4.1 or Kir4.2, to form heteromeric channels.

name: Bioenhancers
description: Agents that are used to increase the BIOAVAILABILITY and bioefficacy of a drug, without any therapeutic activity of its own.

name: Digital Health
description: Use of digital technologies in medicine and other health professions to manage illnesses and health risks and to promote wellness; includes the use of WEARABLE DEVICES; HEALTH INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY; ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS; TELEMEDICINE; and PERSONALIZED MEDICINE.

name: DNA Damage Tolerance
description: Strategies that cells use to continue DNA replication when replicative DNA polymerases stall at DNA damage-blocked replication forks. These DNA damage tolerant replication mechanisms bypass the DNA DAMAGE, which may be repaired subsequently by various DNA REPAIR mechanisms.

name: Rosmarinic Acid
description: A polyphenol compound that naturally occurs in rosemary with ANTIOXIDANT and anti-inflammatory properties.

name: Bothrops atrox
description: A species of venomous pit viper of the BOTHROPS genus. Bothrops atrox are found in the tropical lowlands of northern South America east of the Andes and Trinidad where it is called mapepire balsain. B. atrox is more commonly called common lancehead and fer-de-lance. BATROXOBIN is usually isolated from B. atrox venom.

name: Bothrops asper
description: A species of venomous pit viper of the BOTHROPS genus. Bothrops asper are found in Mexico, Central America and northern South America including Trinidad. B. asper is commonly called terciopelo.

name: Bungarus multicinctus
description: A venomous elapid snake species of BUNGARUS genus found in the marshlands of Southeast Asia and central and southern China. Its common name many-banded krait refers to the numerous white bands across its body. B. multicinctus venom is BUNGAEOTIXINS.

name: Bothrops jararaca
description: A species of venomous snakes of the BOTHROPS genus. Bothrops jararaca is found in South America and commonly called jararaca.

name: Bothrops jararaca Venom
description: Snake venoms isolated from BOTHROPS JARARACA. B. jararaca venoms contain a hemorrhagic metalloproteinase toxn jararhagin which binds to VON WILLEBRAND FACTOR.

name: Excision Repair
description: A major DNA repair mechanism in which defective regions in one strand are excised and resynthesized using the complementary base pairing information in the intact strand.

name: Community of Practice
description: Core concept of learning and knowledge management, a repository where knowledge is developed, maintained and reproduced. It is an important platform for knowledge sharing within an organization or among peers in other settings.

name: Narcissistic Personality Disorder
description: A pattern of grandiosity, need for admiration, and lack of empathy. (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK556001/)

name: Viperinae
description: A subfamily of snakes commonly known as true vipers or crotaline snakes in the family VIPERIDAE. They are distinguished from sister subfamily CROTALINAE or pit vipers by their lack the heat-sensing pit organs.

name: Echis
description: A genus of vipers found in Africa, Arabia and India. Echis snakes include venomous saw-scale viper and carpet viper.

name: Vipera
description: A genus of venomous and viviparous vipers in subfamily VIPERINAE. Vipera are found in Africa, Europe and Asia.

name: Bitis
description: A genus of Viperinae subfamily. Bitis snakes are found in Africa and Arabia. Bitis includes African puff adder (Bitis arietans) and horned adder (Bitis caudalis).

name: Cerastes
description: A genus of Viperinae found mostly in Africa, Arabia and India with characteristic horny scale over each eye. Cerastes genus includes Saharan sand viper (Cerastes vipera) and horned desert viper (Cerastes cerastes). A desert sidewinder Crotalus cerastes also has horny scale over its eyes but is a species in sister subfamily Crotalinae and found in Southwest American desert.

name: ATP-Binding Cassette Sub-Family B Member 4
description: An ATP-binding cassette, sub-family B protein that functions in translocating PHOSPHATIDYLCHOLINES from the inner to the outer leaflet of the canalicular membrane of the HEPATOCYTES.

name: Venomous Snakes
description: Snakes that produce SNAKE VENOMS. Venomous snakes are most often members of ELAPIDAE (e.g., cobras) including sea snakes in HYDROPHIINAE and VIPERIDAE (e.g., vipers).

name: Efferocytosis
description: Phagocytosis and clearance of apoptotic cells.

name: Ursolic Acid
description: A pentacyclic triterpene that co-occurs with its isomer OLEANOLIC ACID in several plant species, and occurs in large amounts in FRUITS (such as CRANBERRIES; PEARS; PLUMS; and OLIVES), MEDICINAL HERBS, and other plants.

name: Heloderma suspectum
description: Large nocturnal, venomous lizard found in the deserts of the Southwestern United States and northern Mexico. A synthetic version of Gila monster venom component exendin-4 is EXENATIDE.

name: Peptidyl-Prolyl Isomerase D
description: A cytoplasmic cyclophilin with molecular chaperoning properties. It is found along with other MOLECULAR CHAPERONES, in steroid aporeceptor complexes and plays a role in maintaining the nonnative folding-competent intermediate state of the steroid aporeceptors. The protein has the alias name cyclophilin D which is also the alias name for the related protein Peptidyl-Prolyl Isomerase F.

name: Edible Seaweeds
description: Various seaweeds either wild-harvested or cultured (AQUACULTURE) for direct human consumption.

name: CD68 Molecule
description: A single-pass type 1 transmembrane glycoprotein that localizes to LYSOSOMES; ENDOSOMES; and cell surface CELL MEMBRANES. It is a member of the lysosomal associated membrane glycoprotein family and the scavenger receptor family. The highly glycosylated extracellular domain binds to tissue- and organ-specific LECTINS or SELECTINS.

name: Centrosomal Associated Proteins
description: Proteins that are localized in the CENTROSOME. They help with processes such as MITOSIS and CELL MOTILITY.

name: Peroxidasin
description: A peroxidase originally isolated from DROSOPHILA that catalyzes the oxidation of bromide by hydrogen peroxide and generates hypobromite as a reactive intermediate. Its functions include a role in EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX assembly of COLLAGEN TYPE IV; LAMININ; and FIBRONECTIN.

name: Amphidinolides
description: Complex macrolides produced by marine dinoflagellates such as AMPHIDINIUM. Many amphidinolides and related iriomoteolides are cytotoxic which disturb MICROTUBULE activities.

name: DNA Polymerase theta
description: A specialized DNA polymerase that in humans is encoded by the POLQ gene. It is involved in DNA repair pathways, including DNA END-JOINING REPAIR and RECOMBINATIONAL DNA REPAIR.

name: Bioactive Peptides, Dietary
description: Peptides that are derived from dietary protein and which can modulate physiological functions.

name: delta-1-Pyrroline-5-Carboxylate Reductase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the last step in proline biosynthesis, which catalyzes the NADPH-dependent reduction of delta-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate to L-Proline.

name: Neuroserpin
description: An inhibitory serpin that inhibits PLASMINOGEN ACTIVATORS (tPA) in the brain.

name: Myrmecophytes
description: Plants that host ANTS by providing shelter in specialized nesting structures or domatia (e.g., Beltian or Mullerian bodies) and sometimes provide food (e.g., food and pearl bodies; and EXTRAFLORAL NECTARS). Ant colony in turn provides the host plant with defense against encroaching foliage, nutrients via waste by-product and help with SEED DISPERSAL.

name: Hemosiderosis, Pulmonary
description: Iron deposition within the lung. Primary pulmonary hemosiderosis is characterized by HEMOPTYSIS; IRON-DEFICIENCY ANEMIA, and diffuse pulmonary hemorrhage as seen as transient pulmonary infiltrates on RADIOGRAPHY. Even though large amounts of iron are laid down in the lung, with normal or increased total body iron, anemia occurs because of inability of the erythron to use iron sequestered in pulmonary MACROPHAGES.

name: Tibiofemoral Joint
description: The articulation between the articular surfaces of the TIBIA and the FEMUR.

name: Cardio-Oncology
description: The study, diagnosis, and treatment of CARDIOTOXICITY in patients who undergo treatment for cancer.

name: Chelidonium majus
description: A plant species of the family PAPAVERACEAE. The common name greater celandine is similar to lesser celandine (Ficaria verna), and celandine poppy (Stylophorum diphyllum). It has been used in folk medicine and its latex contains biologically active compounds including BENZOPHENANTHRIDINES alkaloids (e.g., Chelerythrine).

name: Iodothyronine Deiodinase Type II
description: An enzyme responsible for T4 (3,5,3',5'-tetraiodothyronine) to T3 (3,5,3'-TRIIODOTHYRONINE) conversion. May contribute to increasing T3 THYROID HORMONE production in patients with GRAVES DISEASE.

name: Cyclophanes
description: Hydrocarbons consisting of aromatic unit(s) and cross-linked ansa chain(s), derived from two nonadjacent positions of the aromatic ring(s), e.g., p-cyclophane and m-cyclophane.

name: Pleuromutilins
description: A tricyclic diterpene natural product isolated from Pleurotus mutilus (now referred to as Clitopilus scyphoides). Possesses modest antibacterial activity against primarily gram-positive bacterial organisms.

name: Matrix Gla Protein
description: A 79-residue, vitamin K-dependent protein containing a single disulfide bond & 4.8 gamma-carboxyglutamate (Gla) residues.

name: Cefpirome
description: A fourth-generation cephalosporin antibacterial agent. Appears to be more active in vitro against Staphylococci, some Enterococci, some ENTEROBACTERIACEAE, and PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA.Cefpirome has a pyridinium group attached to C-3 position of its cephalosporin core.

name: Red Fluorescent Protein
description: Protein analogs and derivatives of the Disocosoma red fluorescent protein that emit a red-orange light (FLUORESCENCE) when excited with ULTRAVIOLET RAYS. They are used as REPORTER GENES and FLUORESCENT PROBES for MICROSCOPY of living cells and organisms.

name: Eukaryotic Translation Initiation Factor 5A
description: A component of eukaryotic initiation factor 5A that is involved in the elongation, termination, and stimulation of peptide bond formation. This factor is essential for cell proliferation

name: Homeobox Protein PITX2
description: A homeodomain transcription factor involved in cardiac development.

name: Fire Ants
description: Two members of ant genus Solenopsis in the family Formicidae, order Hymenoptera, accidentally introduced into the United States at Mobile, Alabama. Fire ants are now found in many states from California to Florida. Fire ant bites typically cause a burning sensation, welts and blisters but can cause systemic or life-threatening reactions.

name: Ceftaroline
description: A fifth-generation cephalosporin antibacterial agent that is used to treat skin infections caused by bacteria in adults and newborns. Ceftaroline has a 1,3-thiazolidine ring attached to the C-7 position of its cephalosporin core.

name: DNA Methyltransferase 3B
description: A DNA (cytosine 5) Methyltransferase that has an essential role in the establishment of DNA methylation patterns during development.

name: SS-B Antigen
description: Nuclear autoantigens implicated in nascent RNA protection. It is a target of AUTOANTIBODIES in patients with SJOGREN'S SYNDROME.

name: Cefozopran
description: A fourth-generation cephalosporin antibacterial agent with a broad spectrum of activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Cefozopran has a 1-methyltetrazolethiol (MTT) moiety at C-3 of its cephalosporin core.

name: Sterol O-Acyltransferase 2
description: A sterol O-acyltransferase that catalyzes reaction of Acyl-CoA and cholesterol into CoA and cholesterol ester. It is a distinct enzyme from Acetyl-CoA C-Acetyltransferase 2, which is also referred to as ACAT2.

name: Cefiderocol
description: A siderophore cephalosporin with enhanced activity against GRAM-NEGATIVE AEROBIC BACTERIA.

name: Dyrk Kinases
description: PROTEIN KINASES that can phosphorylate aromatic amino acid residue TYROSINE as well as aliphatic amino acid residues SERINE and THREONINE.

name: Ficolins
description: Soluble oligomeric defense proteins with lectin-like activity. They initiate the LECTIN pathway of COMPLEMENT ACTIVATION through attached serine proteases and a primitive OPSONIZATION.

name: Sigma-1 Receptor
description: A sigma receptor that regulates neuroinflammation, neurotransmitters, neurogenesis, ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM stress and MITOCHONDRIA function.

name: Exportin 1 Protein
description: A karyopherin that functions in nuclear export of proteins and several classes of RNAs.

name: Homeobox Protein SIX3
description: A homeodomain protein that functions in embryonic eye and forebrain development.

name: UDP Xylose-Protein Xylosyltransferase
description: A pentosyltransferase that initiates a series of post-translational modifications necessary for transport and secretion of proteoglycans. It is a key enzyme for glycosylation of the proteoglycan core.

name: Haemaphysalis longicornis
description: A species of tick (TICKS) in the family IXODIDAE, distributed in AUSTRALASIA but establishing in the Eastern UNITED STATES. It is an aggressive biter and can cause severe infestations in livestock. It is also a known/suspected vector of various livestock and human diseases.

name: Cefpodoxime
description: A third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic. Cefpodoxime contains a methoxy group at C-3 of its cephalosporin core.

name: Rabphilin-3A
description: A putative target protein for RAB3A GTP-BINDING PROTEIN. Implicated in regulated secretion, particularly in neurotransmitter release.

name: HLA-E Antigens
description: Class I human histocompatibility (HLA) antigens encoded by genes at the E locus on chromosome 6. They bind a restricted subset of peptides derived from the leader peptides of other class I molecules. They primarily are involved with down-regulating cytolytic activity of NK CELLS and restricting non-canonical CD8-POSITIVE T LYMPHOCYTES.

name: Cefpodoxime Proxetil
description: A prodrug of its active metabolite CEFPODOXIME.

name: Chemokine Receptor D6
description: A broad-specificity receptor for inflammatory CC CHEMOKINE.

name: Nociceptin
description: A pronociceptive peptide that acts as a specific endogenous agonist to the NOCICEPTIN RECEPTOR.

name: Inosine Triphosphatase
description: A pyrophosphatase that catalyzes the conversion of inosine triphosphate and deoxy-inosine triphosphate to inosine monophosphate and deoxy-inosine monophosphate, respectively.

name: Galactoside 2-alpha-L-fucosyltransferase
description: Catalyzes the transfer of L-fucose to the terminal galactose residue of glycoconjugates through an alpha-(1,2) linkage leading to H antigen synthesis.

name: GADD45 Proteins
description: Nuclear proteins that act as critical stress sensors that mediate various cellular responses, including DNA REPAIR; CELL CYCLE ARREST; and APOPTOSIS.

name: Dexpramipexole
description: The (R)-(+) enantiomer of PRAMIPEXOLE. Dexpramipexole has lower affinity for DOPAMINE RECEPTORS than pramipexole.

name: Lobesia botrana
description: A species of tortrix or leafroller moths of the family Tortricidae. These insects cause significant agricultural damage throughout the world feeding on the flower or fruit of host plants, most often grapes (VITIS VINIFERA).

name: Lymantria dispar
description: Moths of genus Lymantria in the family Erebidae, order Lepidoptera. European-origin subspecies Lymantria dispar dispar was formerly known as gypsy moth and accidentally released in Medford, Massachusetts. Now they are called spongy moths and have spread to many states from Virginia to Michigan and pockets of California. Spongy moth caterpillars cause severe defoliation of oaks and other trees and shrubs. LYMANTRIA DISPAR is a group of related Asian-origin subspecies moths known to cause more extensive damage in its native range because its females are active fliers unlike spongy moths of European origin. FSMC includes Lymantria dispar asiatica, L. d. japonica, L. albescens, L. umbrosa, and L. postalba.

name: Helicoverpa armigera
description: Widely distributed old world bollworm which bore into the wide variety of host’s flowers and fruit and feed within the plant. Old world bollworm was detected in Puerto Rico in 2014 and Florida in 2015 but now eradicated in the United States.

name: Polyamine Oxidase
description: An FAD-dependent enzyme in the polyamine catabolism pathway that generates hydrogen peroxide. Present with high activity in most tissues of vertebrate organisms.

name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa Exotoxin A
description: An NAD-dependent ADP-ribosyltransferase that catalyzes the transfer of the ADP ribosyl moiety of oxidized NAD onto elongation factor 2 (EF-2) thus arresting protein synthesis. Commonly used as the toxin in immunotoxins.

name: Dammaranes
description: Tetracyclic triterpenes named after dammar resin, a natural resin first isolated from tropical trees of the DIPTEROCARPACEAE family.

name: Cefprozil
description: A second-generation cephalosporin antibacterial agent. Cefprozil has a phenyl ring at the C-3 position of its cephalosporin core.

name: Lamin B Receptor
description: A 58 kDa membrane protein and delta(14)-sterol reductase that is found in the NUCLEAR ENVELOPE. Deficiencies of this receptor cause PELGER-HUET ANOMALY.

name: Poison Frogs
description: Frogs that sequester and secrete POISONS (e.g., BATRACHOTOXINS). Poison frogs include Australian Pseudophryne, Central and South American Dendrobates, Epipedobates, and Phyllobates and Madagascan Mantella. Melanophyrniscus is a poison toad in the family of Bufonidae. All poison dart frogs are from rain forest of western Colombia and are members of Phyllobates.

name: Cohesins
description: Protein complex constituents that bind chromosomes from late G1 until the metaphase - anaphase transition. The cohesin complex regulates sister chromatid cohesion, HOMOLOGOUS RECOMBINATION and DNA looping.

name: Myokines
description: Signaling proteins that are synthesized and released by muscle fibers in response to exercise or other forms of physical activity.

name: Patient-Ventilator Asynchrony
description: A time mismatch between patient's inspiratory effort and MECHANICAL VENTILATOR's inspiratory time.

name: Parthenium hysterophorus
description: An annual species in the family ASTERACEA, genus Parthenium which sometimes is referred to as feverfew, not to be confused with the medicinal herb often cultivated in the garden, TANACETUM PARTHENIUM. Parthenium hysterophorus is an invasive allelopathic weed indigenous to the Caribbean, Central and South America and has similar rosette stage structures as COMMON RAGWEED. It contains sesquiterpene lactones including parthenin which is poisonous to grazing animals and allergenic and irritant, causing Parthenium dermatitis in humans.

name: Polypeptide N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase
description: Family of enzymes that catalyze the formation of GalNAcAlpha1-serine/threonine linkages in glycoproteins.

name: ETS Translocation Variant 6 Protein
description: A transcriptional repressor in the ETS transcription factor family. Contains a unique ETS domain and HLH domain that can interfere with protein-protein interactions.

name: RAC2 GTP-Binding Protein
description: A small rac GTP-binding protein that forms one of the components of the NADPH oxidase enzyme system.

name: Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase Kinase Kinase 11
description: A MAP kinase kinase kinase that activates the SAPK/JNK and p38/ERK SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION pathways. It has multiple interaction domains, including a Cdc42 binding motif.

name: Retinoic Acid Receptor gamma
description: A retinoic acid receptor that regulates transcriptional activity by heterodimerizing with nuclear RETINOID X RECEPTORS.

name: Puberty Inhibitors
description: Agents that are used to temporarily suppress puberty in adolescents.

name: NF-kappaB-Inducing Kinase
description: A protein serine-threonine kinase that catalyzes the activation of canonical and non-canonical NF-kappaB pathways.

name: Altmetrics
description: Non-traditional journal impact measures that include tracking of downloads; mentions in SOCIAL MEDIA, NEWS reports, BLOGS, and online ENCYCLOPEDIAS; links in bookmarking services and online reference managers; and crowd-based reviews.

name: Metabolic Reprogramming
description: Various cellular responses cells undergo in order to sustain energy production under cellular METABOLIC STRESS. Oncogenic metabolic reprogramming is one of the hallmarks of cancer progression and metastasis.

name: Soft Computing
description: Computing that deals with approximate models and gives solutions to complex real-life problems. Has greater tolerance for imprecision, uncertainty, partial truth, and approximations. Based on techniques such as FUZZY LOGIC, genetic algorithms, NEURAL NETWORKS, COMPUTER, MACHINE LEARNING, and EXPERT SYSTEMS.

name: Incarceration
description: The state of being imprisoned or confined.

name: Academia
description: The environment concerned with the pursuit of research, education, and scholarship.

name: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists
description: Compounds that stimulate the activity of GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1 RECEPTOR. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists are used to treat TYPE 2 DIABETES and OBESITY.

name: Secreted Aspartic Proteases
description: Enzymes that are produced and secreted by organisms, including bacterial and fungi.They are involved in a variety of biological processes, such as nutrient acquisition, pathogenesis of candida, and host tissue invasion.

name: Degrons
description: Minimal elements within a protein that are sufficient for recognition and degradation by a proteolytic apparatus. Inherent degrons are comprised of short linear amino acid sequences and secondary protein structural features that increase the affinity to E3 LIGASE; and are involved in regulating the specificity and timing of PROTEIN DEGRADATION. Acquired degrons are mostly transient and conferred by post-translational modifications of specific amino acids within proteins. (From Mol Cell. 2016 Sep 15;63(6):1055-65)

name: Tissue Inhibitor of Metalloproteinase-4
description: An inhibitor of matrix metalloproteinases involved in regulation of PLATELET AGGREGATION and recruitment.

name: Legumins
description: CASEIN-like globular storage proteins from leguminous seeds such as peas.

name: Kalinin
description: An epithelium-specific basement membrane adhesion molecule that is a component of anchoring filaments. Consists of 3 subunits (A, B2, & B1).

name: ATPase Inhibitory Protein
description: CA(2+) MG(2+)-ATPASE inhibitor found in membranes of mammalian ERYTHROCYTES.

name: Nucleolin
description: Phosphoprotein found in nucleoli, on the cell membrane, and in cytoplasm of all higher eukaryotes. They act as a receptor for some viruses, bacteria, and toxins.

name: Glyphosate
description: Active compound in herbicidal formulations that inhibits 3-PHOSPHOSHIKIMATE 1-CARBOXYVINYLTRANSFERASE.

name: Food Loss and Waste
description: Reductions in edible FOOD post-harvesting anywhere along the food supply chain, e.g., due to spoilage, improper storage, excessive food preparation, resulting in REFUSE DISPOSAL of potentially useful food mass.

name: CD83 Antigen
description: A glycoprotein member of the immunoglobulin superfamily that is primarily expressed on the surface of DENDRITIC CELLS. It is believed to play a role in ANTIGEN PRESENTATION and CELL-TO-CELL INTERACTION following LYMPHOCYTE ACTIVATION.

name: Ganglionic Eminence
description: A transitory embryonic structure that appears during the 5th week post-fertilization. The ganglionic eminence plays an important in the development of the nervous system by guiding tangential cell and axon migration during embryonic development and give rise to BASAL GANGLIA and cortical GABAergic and thalamic and olfactory INTERNEURONS.

name: Collagen Type XVII
description: A 220 kDa non-fibrillar collagen and basement membrane component. It is involved in healing wounds of the EPITHELIUM, CORNEAL.

name: GluK2 Kainate Receptor
description: A high-affinity KAINATE and GLUTAMATE receptor that functions as ligand-gated ion channel in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSYEM and plays an essential role in NEURONAL PLASTICITY.

name: GluK3 Kainate Receptor
description: A high-affinity KAINATE and GLUTAMATE receptor that functions as ligand-gated ion channel in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSYEM and modulates excitatory synaptic transmission.

name: Transcription Factor MTF-1
description: A zinc dependent transcription factor involved in the regulation of intracellular signaling pathways. Regulates the expression of two streams of genes functioning in metal homeostasis and anti-oxidative response.

name: Thyroid Hormone-Binding Proteins
description: Membrane-bound proteins found in the ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM of CULTURED CELLS and NEOPLASMS. They were identified originally based on their capacity to bind THYROID HORMONE.

name: Carbohydrate Sulfotransferases
description: Transmembrane enzymes of the Golgi network that recognize glycans attached to LIPIDS and PROTEINS passing through the secretory pathway.

name: Psychological Growth
description: A process of actively learning and adapting to new ways to function following a challenging life crisis.

name: Coping Skills
description: Various techniques for actively managing a stressful event or situation.

name: Job Security
description: The extent to which job separations are involuntary. The primary measure of job security is the rate of job loss (https://www.bls.gov/osmr/research-papers/2002/pdf/ec020050.pdf).

name: Emotional Exhaustion
description: A state of feeling emotionally overextended and drained.

name: Media Exposure
description: The extent to which individuals encounter messages and content via COMMUNICATION MEDIA.

name: Role Conflict
description: A state of tension or distress that occurs when fulfilling roles of one status making it difficult to fulfill the roles of another.

name: Medical Neglect
description: Failure to seek timely and appropriate care or allow such care for medical, dental or psychological needs by family members, legal guardian and other caregivers. Negligence by professionals is PROFESSIONAL NEGLIGENCE.

name: Social Genomics
description: Field of genetics studying correlates between variations in SOCIOLOGICAL FACTORS and differences in GENOME-wide GENE EXPRESSION REGULATION.

name: Stemona Alkaloids
description: Structurally related ALKALOIDS derived from the plants of the monocotyledonous family STEMONACEAE, characterized by the presence of a pyrrolo(1,2-a)azepine or a pyrido(1,2-a)azepine nucleus.

name: Subjective Stress
description: Perceptions of PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS based on the individual's own personal values, beliefs and past and current experiences and circumstances.

name: Protein Phosphatase Inhibitory Proteins
description: A group of proteins that control the activity of PROTEIN PHOSPHATASES.

name: Indolosesquiterpenes
description: Sesquiterpene compounds that contain an INDOLE.

name: UK Biobank
description: A biomedical database and research resource that contains genetic and health data on participants aged 40-69 years with a roughly even number of men and women recruited between 2006 and 2010 throughout the UK.

name: Extravillous Trophoblasts
description: Differentiated trophoblast cells originally from trophoblastic cell columns of anchoring CHORIONIC VILLI of the DECIDUA basalis of the PLACENTA. Extravillous trophoblasts invade into the uterine structures, attaching the placenta to the UTERUS. They are also found in chorionic plate, MYOMETRIUM, and spiral arteries.

name: Ectodermal Placodes
description: A series of thickened ECTODERM patches in the developing cranial region that appears during week 4 in human embryo. Ectodermal placodes are the primordium of many ectodermal sensory systems including the INNER EAR, the EYE LENS, the OLFACTORY EPITHELIUM, as well as the PITUITARY GLAND and THYROID GLAND.

name: Undertreatment
description: Remedial treatment or preventive procedures of a disease which is done too infrequently or not enough to control disease diagnosis or treatment. Many factors contribute to medical undertreatment including lack of ACCESS TO HEALTH SERVICES and PATIENT PREFERENCE.

name: Polo-like Kinases
description: Protein serine-threonine kinases which regulate entry into M phase, spindle pole biogenesis and function, mitotic chromosome dynamics, mitotic exit, and cytokinesis. They contain a characteristic Polo-box protein interaction domain.

name: Polo-Like Kinase 1
description: Plays a crucial role in the regulation of proliferative activity of normal and malignant cells. Proposed as a new target for antineoplastic treatment strategies.

name: Solute Carrier Family 44, Member 2 Protein
description: A mitochondrion and plasma membrane protein that enables choline transmembrane transporter activity.

name: beta Lactam Antibiotics
description: Bactericidal agents that contain a beta-lactam ring in their chemical structure. They inhibit bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to PENICILLIN-BINDING PROTEINS, preventing the synthesis of peptidoglycan in bacterial cell walls.

name: Two-Pore Channels
description: Ligand-gated cation-selective ION CHANNELS located in ENDOSOMES and LYSOSOMES of plant and animal cells.

name: First Generation Cephalosporins
description: CEPHALOSPORIN agents with excellent coverage against gram-positive cocci, such as STAPHYLOCOCCUS and STREPTOCOCCUS. They have some activity against the gram-negative bacteria, but in general, gram-negative activity is decreased compared to 2nd, 3rd, and 4th generation cephalosporins.

name: Roundabout Proteins
description: A family of single-pass transmembrane receptors that act as the cognate receptors for the secreted guidance factor Slit emanating from central nervous system midlines.

name: RNA Methylation
description: The addition of a methyl group to one of the NITROGEN atoms on a NUCLEOTIDE base in an RNA molecule.

name: Mass Shooting Events
description: A mass killing by firearm that consists of 3 or more killings in a single incident (H.R.2076 – 112th U.S. Congress (2011-2012): Investigative Assistance for Violent Crimes Act of 2012).

name: Retrograde Ejaculation
description: The flow of SEMINAL FLUID, from the posterior URETHRA, backwards into the BLADDER. Causes include injuries such as from SPINAL CORD INJURIES; DIABETIC NEUROPATHIES; surgeries in adjacent tissues such as AORTIC ANEURYSM surgeries and transurethral bladder neck incisions; or drug side effects.

name: Second Generation Cephalosporins
description: Agents with less activity against gram-positive cocci than FIRST GENERATION CEPHALOSPORINS but have increased activity against gram-negative bacilli.

name: Ejaculatory Dysfunction
description: The inability in males to ejaculate, or to have a normal time to EJACULATION.

name: Third Generation Cephalosporins
description: Agents that are structurally similar to other CEPHALOSPORINS but have a broader spectrum of activity against bacteria than the first and second generation cephalosporins. These agents cover more resistant STREPTOCOCCUS, STAPHYLOCOCCUS, gram-positive anaerobes, and more resistant strains of HAEMOPHILUS, NEISSERIA, PROTEUS, ESCHERICHIA COLI, and KLEBSIELLA (HNPEK).

name: Toll-Like Receptor Agonists
description: Agents that stimulate TOLL-LIKE RECEPTOR signaling, and the activity of both the INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE and ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY.

name: Paraptosis
description: A type of programmed cell death resembling NECROSIS, with mitochondrial and ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM swelling and accumulation of CYTOPLASMIC VACUOLES. Distinctive morphological changes to the CELL NUCLEUS are absent.

name: Hearing Loss, Hidden
description: Hearing loss that is difficult to diagnose by standard hearing tests as it most often pertains to difficulties in hearing only in certain situations such as in noisy environments.

name: Gender-Affirming Care
description: A supportive healthcare, consisting of medical, surgical, mental health, and non-medical services for TRANSGENDER PERSONS and GENDER-NONCONFORMING PERSONS. Medical and psychosocial gender affirming healthcare practices may lower rates of adverse mental health outcomes, build SELF ESTEEM, and improve overall QUALITY OF LIFE for transgender and gender diverse youth (https://opa.hhs.gov/sites/default/files/2022-03/gender-affirming-care-young-people-march-2022.pdf).

name: ERRalpha Estrogen-Related Receptor
description: An orphan nuclear receptor that belongs to the ERR subfamily. It has enriched expression in tissues with high oxidative metabolic capacity.

name: Acetophenones
description: Derivatives of the simplest aromatic ketone acetophenone (of general formula C6H5C(O)CH3).

name: Time Pressure
description: Sense of time urgency to complete a task. This sense of time urgency creates psychological pressure affecting performance (https://www.nrc.gov/docs/ML2112/ML21127A272.pdf).

name: Lacrosse
description: A version of the game of baggataway, in which two teams of players use long-handled, racketlike implements (crosses) to catch, carry, or throw a ball down the field or into the opponents’ goal. The goal is defined by uprights and a crossbar framing a loose net. The distinctive feature of the game is the crosse (lacrosse stick), the implement used by the players to carry, catch, and pass the ball. The crosse is sharply bent at the top to form a hook from the end of which a thong is drawn and fastened to the shaft about 2 or 3 feet from the end of the handle, forming an oval triangle that is woven with a loose network of leather, nylon, or gut to form the pocket with which the ball is handled.(from https://www.britannica.com/sports/lacrosse)

name: Agroecology
description: The design, development and management of sustainable agroecosystems based on the application of ecological principles while considering existing social, cultural, and economic factors of farming communities. (From https://lod.nal.usda.gov/nalt/5505)

name: Quantum Mechanics
description: The field of physics that explains how extremely small objects simultaneously have the characteristics of both particles (tiny pieces of matter) and waves (a disturbance or variation that transfers energy).

name: Plain Language Summaries
description: Short summaries of research articles written in clear, easy-to-understand language, intended to be a useful way of communicating health research to a non-expert reader.

name: Cognitive Flexibility
description: The ability to effectively adapt one's cognitive and behavioral strategies in response to changing task or environmental demands. (from Clinical Psychology Review August 2021,102061).

name: Athletic Trainers
description: Health care professionals who render service or treatment, under the direction of or in collaboration with a physician, in accordance with their education and training and State statutes, rules and regulations. Services provided are related to injury and illness prevention, wellness promotion and education, emergent care, examination and clinical diagnosis, therapeutic intervention, and rehabilitation of injuries and medical conditions. (from https://www.bocatc.org/)

name: Large Language Models
description: Computational designs that apply DEEP LEARNING methods on extremely large data sets as a basis for predicting and constructing natural-sounding text.

name: Street Food
description: Ready-to-eat foods and beverages prepared and/or sold by vendors or hawkers especially in the streets and other similar places. They represent a significant part of urban food consumption for millions of low-and-middle-income consumers, in urban areas on a daily basis. (USDA)

name: Price Transparency
description: Healthcare pricing information provided in advance of receiving care and publicizing how and from whom patients can obtain price estimates. Hospitals operating in the United States are required to make public a list of standard charges for items and services they provide. (Federal Register 84 FR 65524)

name: Human Challenge Trials
description: Trials in which participants are intentionally challenged (whether or not they have been vaccinated) with exposure to an infectious disease organism.

name: Emotional Eating
description: Eating behaviors caused by PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS; ANXIETY; BOREDOM; or other negative emotions rather than physical HUNGER.

name: Autonomous Robots
description: Machines that are engineered to learn about their environment and make decisions to complete tasks with little to no human intervention. These robots may be designed to complete tasks such as patient intervention, remote monitoring, inventory transportation, among many others.

name: Intelligent Systems
description: Technological systems that perform automated tasks within specific environments enabled by artificial intelligence.

name: Boosting Machine Learning Algorithms
description: A form of ensemble learning methods which combines weak learners to create strong ones, which reduces training errors and bias in the training models. There are different types of boosting such as gradient boosting, XGBoost, and Adaboost.

name: Ensemble Learning
description: A method in machine learning where several base learners are combined to create an optimal learning model. This can be used for a variety of models including forecasting, classification, or function approximation.

name: Federated Learning
description: A method of training machine learning models whereby multiple devices train their own copy of the artificial intelligence model using decentralized local data. These locally trained model results are then aggregated by a central server to update the global model without accessing local data.

name: Reinforcement Machine Learning
description: A machine learning training method in which an agent in an uncertain environment is rewarded for optimal behaviors and punished for undesired behaviors, allowing the agent to learn from trial-and-error.

name: Representation Machine Learning
description: A class of machine learning approaches that allow a system to discover the representations required for feature detection or classification from raw data. The requirement for manual feature engineering is reduced by allowing a machine to learn the features and apply them to a given activity.

name: Transfer Machine Learning
description: Process of training a new learning network by beginning with previously trained for a related problem, leading to less time and energy required for training the new learning network.

name: Prediction Methods, Machine
description: Methods of making prediction about a new measurement based on calculations of previous data.

name: Predictive Learning Models
description: Machine learning models which are trained to analyze historical data to find patterns and trends, allowing it to predict future outcomes.

name: Particle Swarm Optimization
description: A heuristic computational algorithm designed to find optimal solutions in a random search space. Particle swarm optimization measures swarm intelligence which is a computation measurement inspired by behaviors of self-organized swarming animals.

name: Pattern Analysis, Machine
description: The process of recognizing and extracting meaningful information from patterns in data. Pattern analysis in machine learning is often used for predictions and forecasting.

name: Convolutional Neural Networks
description: Artificial neural networks designed to automatically learn features through the use of sequence of layers which transform one volume to the next. Convolutional neural networks initially produce a feature map by use of convolution layers consisting of a set of learnable filters convolved with input, i.e., having smaller widths and heights and the same depth as that of input volume.

name: Long Short Term Memory
description: A form of recurrent computer neural networks which allows for important information to be retained and less important information to be erased. These kinds of networks are used for tasks such as language translation, anomaly detection, speech and handwriting recognition, and time series prediction.

name: Cellular Neural Networks, Computer
description: A type of neural network that consists of a large number of processing elements called cells arranged in a grid-like structure that interact with each other and neighboring cells through a set of predefined rules to perform complex computations.

name: Feedforward Neural Networks
description: A network where information is only passed in one direction. This is the opposite of a recurrent neural network, in which information is processed in a cycle.

name: Extreme Learning Machines
description: A feedforward neural network designed with a single layer hidden node where the weights between inputs and hidden nodes are randomly assigned. Extreme learning machines can be trained fast and used for the data clustering, grouping, regression, prediction, and forecasting.

name: Multilayer Perceptrons
description: A feedforward neural network with multiple layers, an input layer, at least three hidden layers, and an output layer, generally used for pattern recognition and classification.

name: Graph Neural Networks
description: Neural networks designed to process signals supported on graphs.

name: Radial Basis Function Networks
description: A three-layer neural network made of an input layer, hidden layer, and output layer. Radial basis function networks are used for function approximation, interpolation, classification, and time series prediction.

name: Recurrent Neural Networks
description: A type of neural network where the output from the previous step is fed as input to the current step with the help of a hidden layer which tracks data sequences. Recurrent neural network is often used when the data is sequential, and weights need to be treated same across all the layers such as in time series data and speech recognition. Variation of recurrent neural network include bidirectional neural network and long short-term memory.

name: Hopfield Neural Networks
description: Fully interconnected, single layer neural network, which can be used for associative memory and optimization tasks.

name: Adaptive Algorithms
description: Algorithms designed to solve a problem by modifying their behaviors when faced with an unseen task with limited data during training.

name: Generative Adversarial Networks
description: An unsupervised learning network which is composed of two separate networks, a generator which produces content and a discriminator which works to identify real content from the generated content. Over time, generative adversarial networks create data that increasingly resembles the input data.

name: Backtracking Algorithms
description: A general algorithmic technique that considers solutions one option at a time backtracking to get the desired solution. This allows searching every possible option recursively.

name: Classification Algorithms
description: A class of algorithms that predicts into which category an observation belongs based on training data.

name: Clustering Algorithms
description: Algorithms designed to find groups of similar data points (called clusters) in the dataset. Clustering is often used for feature engineering or pattern discovery in unsupervised machine learning.

name: Compression Algorithms
description: A class of algorithms which both reduces and restores the size of files to increase their portability. Compression algorithms can be lossy or lossless.

name: Detection Algorithms
description: Algorithms designed to find or localize the objects in images and assign the objects (affordances).

name: Dynamic Programming
description: Dynamic programming is an optimization technique where smaller portions of problems are broken down, solved, and remembered, in order to solve a larger and more complex problem.

name: Genetic Algorithms
description: Heuristic search algorithms which direct the random searches to the area of better performance or fitness function by computationally creating the conditions inspired by NATURAL SELECTION. They are commonly used to generate solutions for optimization problems.

name: Machine Learning Algorithms
description: A class of algorithms which enables a computer to learn as it goes, thereby accomplishing its goal without being explicitly programmed to do so.

name: Parallel Algorithms
description: Algorithms that can execute several instructions simultaneously on different processing devices and then combine all the individual outputs to produce the final result.

name: Prediction Algorithms
description: A class of algorithms which are designed to forecast unseen data. Prediction Algorithms can discover patterns, perform classification tasks, and identify trends.

name: Autoencoder
description: An unsupervised learning technique where the machine learns patterns in unlabeled data sets, makes compressed representations and reconstructs the input as output at minimum loss of features from the input. Autoencoders are useful in denoising images, DIMENSIONALITY REDUCTION and feature extraction.

name: Multiple-Instance Learning Algorithms
description: Weakly supervised learning algorithms where training set is arranged in a labeled bag of instances, and a single class label is assigned to a bag.

name: Claustrophobia
description: Persistent and irrational fear of enclosed places (e.g., elevators, closets, tunnels) or of being confined (e.g., in an airplane or the backseat of a car). Situations where enclosure or confinement may be encountered are often avoided or else endured with intense anxiety or distress. The focus of fear is typically on panic symptoms triggered in these situations, such as feelings of being unable to breathe, choking, sweating, and fears of losing control. (From APA Dictionary of Psychology, accessed 11/8/2023)

name: Phobia, School
description: Overwhelming and persistent reluctance to go to school, which usually occurs during the primary school years and is often a symptom of an educational, social, or emotional problem. (From APA Dictionary of Psychology)

name: Ethical Dilemmas
description: Situations in which two moral principles conflict with one another. Fictional or hypothetical dilemmas of this kind are used to assess the moral beliefs or moral reasoning skills of individuals. (From APA Dictionary of Psychology, https://dictionary.apa.org/)

name: Remote Patient Monitoring
description: A type of TELEMEDICINE in which healthcare providers monitor patients using digital medical devices. Data collected from these devices are then electronically transferred to providers for care management and has been used to measure symptoms of chronic conditions, such as cardiac diseases, diabetes, and asthma. Benefits include patient engagement, patient adherence to their treatment plan, and the ability to expand physician reach and easily provide care to patients without the need for patients in person encounters. (From https://psnet.ahrq.gov/perspective/remote-patient-monitoring. Accessed 11 Nov 2023)

name: Body Satisfaction
description: The subjective perception and evaluation of one’s own body in terms of different aspects such as size, shape, musculature or muscle tone, weight, and fitness.

name: Psychologists
description: Professionals trained in the study of mental processes and behavior in man and animals.

name: Emergency Use Authorization
description: Authorization allowing the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to strengthen public health protections against chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats including infectious diseases, by facilitating the availability and use of medical countermeasures needed during public health emergencies. Under section 564 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, FDA may authorize unapproved medical products or unapproved uses of approved medical products to be used in an emergency to diagnose, treat, or prevent serious or life-threatening diseases or agents when certain criteria are met, including there are no adequate, approved, and available alternatives.(From fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/emergency-use-authorization-medical-products-and-related-authorities)

name: Coccidioidal Meningitis
description: Meningitis caused by a fungus of the genus COCCIDIOIDES, endemic to the SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES, south-central Washington State, and parts of Mexico and Central and South America.

name: Congenital Portosystemic Shunt
description: Congenital vascular malformation where the portal venous system blood (PORTAL SYSTEM) bypasses the liver sinusoids and drains into the systemic vein through a shunt.

name: Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease
description: A disease in which serum antibodies are directed against MYELIN-OLIGODENDROCYTE GLYCOPROTEIN. MOGAD is typically associated with ACUTE DISSEMINATED ENCEPHALOMYELITIS; NEUROMYELITIS OPTICA; or TRANSVERSE MYELITIS.

name: Lucilia Blowflies
description: A genus of the family Calliphoridae in the order Diptera. Members include common green bottle fly whose maggots are used in MAGGOT THERAPY and sheep blowflies causing MYIASIS. Several member species are blowflies of interest to FORENSIC ENTOMOLOGY.

name: Interleukin-21
description: INTERLEUKINS that affect the differentiation and function of LYMPHOCYTES and MYELOID CELLS and regulate both IMMUNITY, INNATE and ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY. They are also involved in the expansion of NK CELLS.

name: Structural Maintenance of Chromosome Protein 1
description: A central component of the COHESIN PROTEIN COMPLEX involved in the cohesion of sister chromatids after DNA REPLICATION and in DNA REPAIR.

name: Prospero-Related Homeobox 1 Protein
description: TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR involved in developmental processes like CELL DIFFERENTIATION and regulating GENETIC TRANSCRIPTION and STEM CELLS. It plays a critical role in embryonic development and functions as a key regulatory protein in neurogenesis and organ development.

name: Slit Homolog 2 Protein
description: A secreted protein containing four LEUCINE-rich repeats, followed by six EGF repeats, an ALPS domain, three additional EGF repeats, and a CYSTEINE-rich carboxy-terminal region. It functions in CELL MIGRATION and neuron guidance during brain and nervous system development.

name: Nicotinate-Nucleotide Diphosphorylase (Carboxylating)
description: A Pentosyltransferase involved in the catabolism of QUINOLINIC ACID, NAD+ biosynthesis, and APOPTOSIS.

name: Lucilia sericata
description: A blowfly species in the genus Lucilia. Lucilia sericata is the most often used species for MAGGOT THERAPY and is responsible for sheep blowfly strike (MYIASIS) in northern Europe. Can form hybrids with Australian sheep blowfly, LUCILIA CUPRINA.

name: Lucilia cuprina
description: A blowfly species in the genus Lucilia. Lucilia cuprina is responsible for sheep blowfly strike (MYIASIS) in Australia. Can form hybrids with LUCILIA SERICATA.

name: mRNA Guanylyltransferases
description: Enzymes that catalyze the transfer of GMP residue from GTP to 5' end of RNA to form a cap structure identified as G(5')pppN. They can also modify synthetic poly(A) & poly(G) to form m7G(5')pppAn & m7G(5')pppGn.

name: Periodization
description: A systematic training calendar designed to provide variations in performance targeting, while maximizing results and reducing the potential for overtraining. Term only applies to EXERCISE.

name: Mesolimbic System
description: One of the main brain dopaminergic circuits, which connects the MIDBRAIN with the LIMBIC SYSTEM, going from the VENTRAL TEGMENTAL AREA to the NUCLEUS ACCUMBENS, connecting with other structures such as the AMYGDALA and the PREFRONTAL CORTEX.

name: Disulfidptosis
description: A form of disulfide stress-induced CELL DEATH triggered under glucose starvation conditions and overexpression of AMINO ACID TRANSPORT SYSTEM Y+ proteins.

name: Personal Trainers
description: Fitness professionals who work with people to identify and achieve their personal fitness and health goals. They create exercise programs and motivate clients through feedback and accountability.

name: Seven in Absentia Proteins
description: Members of the E3 ubiquitin ligase family that contain a RING-finger protein motif. They play critical roles in CELL PROLIFERATION; PROTEOSTASIS; DNA DAMAGE; and HYPOXIA response.

name: Kiribati
description: The Gilbert Islands were granted self-rule by the UK in 1971 and complete independence in 1979 under the new name of Kiribati.

name: Medical Debt
description: Debt related to, in whole or in part, transactions, accounts, or balances arising from the receipt of medical services, products, or devices.

name: Scoping Review
description: Review to identify knowledge gaps, scope a body of literature, clarify concepts or to investigate research conduct.

name: Scoping Reviews as Topic
description: Works about a review to identify knowledge gaps, scope of a body of literature, clarify concepts, or investigate research conduct.

name: Gene Therapy Agents
description: A functional gene designed for targeted delivery to specific tissues within the body for correcting or repairing a gene that may be defective.

name: Digital Media
description: Information or entertainment in digital form, especially online via the Internet. Examples of digital media include online news sources, video games, blogs, and social media. The term may also be used to describe online content, especially content that is interactive; on-demand media that is accessible through a range of devices; and media that is responded to or shared in real time. It is sometimes used to refer to content that is created, published, or distributed by individuals or non-traditional publishers, such as bloggers.

name: Vaso-Occlusive Crises
description: A common complication of SICKLE CELL DISEASE arises when MICROVESSELS become obstructed by sickled red blood cells, leading to tissue and organ oxygen deprivation, resulting in acute episodes of pain.

name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
description: Uncontrolled anxiety or excessive worry that exceeds the realistic scope of life situations and endures for at least a month or longer.

name: Guttate Psoriasis
description: A skin condition, typically emerges suddenly and frequently occurs after an infection such as STREPTOCOCCAL INFECTION. While prevalent among children, it can also manifest in young adults. Its defining feature is the eruption of small, red, scaly patches that typically appear on the arms, legs, and torso.

name: Nociplastic Pain
description: Pain originating from the disrupted function of pain-related sensory pathways in both the peripheral and central nervous system (CNS), leading to heightened sensitivity.

name: Vasodilator-Stimulated Phosphoprotein
description: An actin-associated protein expressed in platelets and various cells and tissues. It is also recognized as a substrate for CYCLIC GMP-DEPENDENT PROTEIN KINASES and CYCLIC AMP-DEPENDENT PROTEIN KINASES. It plays a role in various processes, including platelet activation and cell migration.

name: Steroidogenic Acute Regulatory Protein
description: A mitochondrial protein found in the ADRENAL GLANDS and GONADS. It plays an important role in the transfer of cholesterol from the outer to the inner mitochondrial membrane.

name: Bisphenols
description: A class of phenolic compounds that are derived from DIPHENYLMETHANE, 4,4'-dihydroxy-2,2-diphenylpropane, DIPHENYL SULFONE, and their related compounds with similar structures. They are commonly used in the production of POLYMERS.

name: Taste Receptors, Type 2
description: G-protein coupled receptors that sense bitter TASTE.

name: Frontline Workers
description: Employees whose primary responsibilities are to provide or maintain essential services, or involve direct engagement with customers, patients, or the public.

name: Ferroportin
description: An iron exporter protein that transports iron from inside of a cell to the outside.

name: Diphenyl Sulfone Compounds
description: Compounds that include two phenyl groups joined by the sulfur atom of Sulfur Dioxide

name: Men's Health Services
description: Organized services to provide health care for men.

name: T-bet Transcription Factor
description: A transcription factor of the T-box family of transcription factors, functions in immune system regulation, particularly in T-cell differentiation. It also is involved in the development of Th1 cells and the regulation of CXCR3 expression.

name: Oxysterol Binding Proteins
description: Family of steroid receptors that transport CHOLESTEROL and PHOSPHOLIPIDS. They act as a sensor or transporter of these ligands at contact sites of two different cellular membranes where they function as lipid exchangers, mediating counter-directional transport of two different lipid ligands.

name: Bisphenol A Compounds
description: Compounds that include structure of or are derivatives of 2,2-Bis(4-hydroxyphenyl)propane.

name: Polycarbonates
description: Polymeric substances that include repeating carbonate molecules in their structure.

name: Paternal Death
description: Death of the male parent.

name: AICDA (Activation-Induced Cytidine Deaminase)
description: A CYTIDINE DEAMINASE required for several crucial steps of B Cell terminal differentiation.

name: Bisphenol S Compounds
description: Compounds that are derived from, or include the structure of 4,4'-sulfonyldiphenol.

name: Transcription Factor TFIIIC
description: TFIII transcription factor that consists of TFIIIC1 (MW appx 200 kDA) and TFIIIC2 (MW 400-500 kDa) subunits. TFIIIC2 contains the TFIIIC90 subunit, which has HISTONE ACETYLTRANSFERASE activity.

name: Bisphenol F Compounds
description: Compounds that include the structure of, or are derivatives of 4,4'-Dihydroxydiphenylmethane.

name: Generative Artificial Intelligence
description: An artificial intelligence (AI) technique that generates synthetic artifacts by analyzing training examples; learning their patterns and distribution; and then creating realistic facsimiles. It uses generative modeling and advances in deep learning to produce diverse content at scale by utilizing existing media such as text, graphics, audio, and video. (From Association for Computing Machinery, https://doi.org/10.1145/3626110)

name: Ubiquitin-Conjugating Enzyme UBC9
description: An enzyme that facilitates the conjugation of SUMO PROTEIN to target substrate.

name: Developmental Origins of Health and Disease
description: Concept that the origins of lifestyle-related disease is formed at the time of fertilization, embryonic, fetal, and neonatal stages by the interrelation between genes and the environments (nutrition, stress, or environmental chemicals). (J Cardiol 2020 Jul;76(1):14-17)...

name: Battered Men
description: Men who are physically and or mentally abused.

name: Unaccompanied Minors
description: A child or adolescent without the presence of a legal guardian.

name: Polymorphic Catecholaminergic Ventricular Tachycardia
description: An arrhythmogenic disorder of the heart characterized by irregular heart rhythms in response to physical activity, stress, or catecholamine infusion, often transitioning into VENTRICULAR FIBRILLATION.

name: Carboranes
description: Molecules that include CARBON, BORON and HYDROGEN and typically form into a polygonal structure.

name: Polyether Compounds
description: Organic polymers that consist of molecules that are joined together by single bonded oxygen atoms.

name: Podoplanin
description: A cell-surface mucin-like glycoprotein that is encoded by the PDPN gene and is commonly found in the PULMONARY ALVEOLI, HEART, and endothelium of lymphatic vessels. It interacts with the C-type lectin-like receptor 2 (CLEC-2), expressed on BLOOD PLATELETS. It may also function in TUMOR development and progression.

name: Kcnj10 Channel
description: An Inwardly rectifying potassium channel expressed by GLIAL CELLS of the brain and in cells of the DISTAL KIDNEY TUBULES. Mutations in the KCNJ10 gene can cause SESAME SYNDROME.

name: Collapsin Response Mediator Protein 1
description: Nerve tissue protein which is necessary for signaling by class 3 SEMAPHORINS and subsequent remodeling of the CYTOSKELETON. It plays a role in AXON GUIDANCE during development of the NERVOUS SYSTEM.

name: Cronkhite-Canada Syndrome
description: A nonfamilial polyposis syndrome that is characterized by the presence of diffuse gastrointestinal polyposis, skin hyperpigmentation, ALOPECIA; DIARRHEA, and PROTEIN-LOSING ENTEROPATHY. It was first reported by Cronkhite and Canada in 1955.

name: Long-Chain-Fatty-Acid-CoA Ligase
description: Coenzyme A ligase that catalyzes the activation of fatty acids in LIPOGENESIS and membrane remodeling. Activity is independent of PHOSPHATIDYLCHOLINES.

name: Tirzepatide
description: An analog of GASTRIC INHIBITORY POLYPEPTIDE and agonist of GLUCOSE-DEPENDENT INSULINOTROPIC POLYPEPTIDE RECEPTOR and GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1 RECEPTOR used to enhance glycemic control of TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS.

name: T Lineage-Specific Activation Antigen 1
description: A T-lymphocyte differentiation antigen recognized by the DX11 MONOCLONAL ANTIBODY and expressed on the majority of peripheral blood T-LYMPHOCYTES where it is involved in their cytolytic function and SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION.

name: Cocaine- and Amphetamine-Regulated Transcript Protein
description: Neuropeptide that functions with NEUROPEPTIDE Y and LEPTIN in the regulation of APPETITE. It also plays a role in neural development and is involved in the regulation of energy homeostasis and stress control.

name: CD163 Antigen
description: Scavenger receptor that functions in clearance of HEMOGLOBIN-HAPTOGLOBIN COMPLEX upon hemolysis of red blood cells by MACROPHAGES and may protect tissues from hemoglobin-mediated OXIDATIVE STRESS.

name: Skin Microbiome
description: All of the microbial organisms that naturally exist upon the EPIDERMIS.

name: Seashore
description: ECOSYSTEM or ground next to the water between the high tide point and the low tide point.

name: R-Spondins
description: Types of THROMBOSPONDINS that regulate the WNT SIGNALING PATHWAY.

name: Brachyury Protein
description: A T-box transcription factor which regulates the expression of genes required for MESODERM formation and differentiation.

name: Bisphenol B Compounds
description: Compounds that include structure of or are derivatives of 2,2-Bis(4-hydroxyphenyl)butane.

name: Uveal Melanoma
description: A rare, malignant MELANOMA arising from the melanocytes of the UVEA.

name: Gaelic Football
description: A form of EUROPEAN FOOTBALL derived from traditional Irish ball games. It has similarities to, but is distinct from, SOCCER and RUGBY.

name: Forced Labor, Employment
description: Forced labor occurs when individuals are compelled against their will to provide work or service through the use of force, fraud, or coercion. (https://www.dhs.gov/blue-campaign/forced-labor)

name: Grief Therapy
description: Treatment that helps a person work through a greater than normal reaction to a loss, such as the death of a loved one. Therapy may be individual or group therapy.

name: Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome
description: Disease that affects linguistic, VISUAL SPATIAL PROCESSING; EXECUTIVE FUNCTION, and MOOD regulation. Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome is associated with acquired lesions in the CEREBELLUM particularly in the posterior lobe and the vermis.

name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
description: Infection of the lungs in a patient who is not hospitalized or who has not resided in a long-term care facility for 14 days prior to the onset of symptoms. It is associated with some signs and symptoms of acute infection and is accompanied by the presence of an acute infiltrate on chest radiograph.(US Pharm. 2007;32(10):44-5 https://www.uspharmacist.com/article/community-acquired-pneumonia)

name: Data Analytics
description: The collection, transformation, and organization of data in order to draw conclusions, make predictions, and drive informed decision making. The process deduces logical sets and patterns by filtering and applying required transformations and models of raw data.

name: Fluorescent Chemosensor Compounds
description: Molecular probes that respond to specific chemical interactions by altering the degree or frequency of their fluorescence. They are used to provide direct visualization of chemical changes within cells.

name: Emphysematous Pyelonephritis
description: Acute often necrotizing pyelonephritis characterized by accumulation of gas within and around renal parenchyma. Emphysematous pyelonephritis is typically associated with bacterial infection in DIABETES MELLITUS and IMMUNOCOMPROMISED PATIENT.

name: Fetus-in-Fetu
description: Rare abnormality where a fetal part of an identical twin that stopped developing during gestation is found within a normally developing fetus. It is considered a TWIN PREGNANCY complication.

name: Acetoxyacetylaminofluorene
description: An alkylating agent that forms DNA ADDUCTS at the C-8 position in GUANINE, resulting in single strand breaks. It has demonstrated carcinogenic action.

name: Historically Black Colleges and Universities
description: The Higher Education Act of 1965, as amended, defines an HBCU as: “…any historically black college or university that was established prior to 1964, whose principal mission was, and is, the education of black Americans, and that is accredited by a nationally recognized accrediting agency or association determined by the Secretary [of Education] to be a reliable authority as to the quality of training offered or is, according to such an agency or association, making reasonable progress toward accreditation.” (https://sites.ed.gov/whhbcu/one-hundred-and-five-historically-black-colleges-and-universities/

name: Chemsex
description: The use of drugs to enhance or sustain sexual activity primarily but not exclusively by men who have sex with men.

name: Cloacal Exstrophy
description: A rare congenital malformation that affects the development of the urinary, digestive, and REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEMS due to CLOACA malformations. In this condition, the large intestine develops outside the abdominal cavity, with the bladder connected to it. Due to this abnormal connection between the colon and the bladder, urine and stool can mix, and there is often no anus.

name: Opticians
description: Technicians who follow prescriptions for visual correction, order lenses, and dispense eyeglasses and contact lenses.

name: RNA Damage
description: Injuries to RNA molecules, leading to changes in their structure or function.

name: Sense of Agency
description: Perception or feeling of control over one's own actions thereby influencing the course of events and outcomes. SELF-EFFICACY on the other hand is beliefs or expectations in self-ability to achieve intended goals or to produce a given effect in specific tasks.

name: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction
description: A therapeutic intervention designed to improve PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING through reduced ANXIETY; PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS; DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS; DISTRESS and improved mood by increased mindfulness.

name: Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy
description: A therapeutic intervention designed to treat people with DEPRESSION through use of elements of MINDFULNESS-BASED STRESS REDUCTION and other cognitive behavioral therapy.

name: Climate Anxiety
description: Persistent and difficult to control psychological distress over CLIMATE CHANGE.

name: Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine
description: The practice of medicine concerned with conditions in individuals resulting from exposure to environments where the ambient pressure is increased, such as the undersea environment.

name: CRF Receptor, Type 1
description: Corticotropin Releasing Hormone Receptor 1 is a G protein coupled receptor that binds corticotropin-releasing hormone, a peptide that plays a key role in activating signal transduction pathways involved in the stress response.

name: Histidine-Rich Glycoprotein
description: A multifunctional protein primarily found in the PLASMA with His/Pro-Rich (HRR) region which contains approximately 12 tandem internal repeats of the 5-residue G[H/P][H/P]PH consensus sequence. Histidine-rich glycoprotein has a diverse range of ligands that are involved in many biological processes, including COAGULATION; IMMUNE RESPONSE; ANGIOGENESIS, and WOUND HEALING.

name: Exostosin Glycosyltransferase Family
description: Glycosyltransferases involved in the elongation of HEPARAN SULFATE chains. Mutations in exostosin genes are associated with HEREDITARY MULTIPLE EXOSTOSES.

name: Outcome Expectations
description: Believed or anticipated consequences of a person’s behavior.

name: Chronic Care Model
description: A healthcare framework that typically integrates clinical information systems to improve CLINICAL DECISION-MAKING, support for COMMUNITY RESOURCES and SELF-MANAGEMENT and improvement of care continuity through better delivery system design and organization.

name: Exostosin 1
description: A bifunctional glycosyltransferase involved in transferring GLUCURONIC ACID and N-ACETYLGLUCOSAMINE in the elongation of HEPARAN SULFATE chains. Mutations in the gene EXT1, coding for this protein (as well as mutations in other genes), are responsible for defects in heparan sulfate synthesis resulting in HEREDITARY MULTIPLE EXOSTOSES. Exostosin-1, along with EXOSTOSIN-2, is a component of heparan sulfate polymerase.

name: Adherence Interventions
description: Various interventions designed to improve treatment adherence and compliance.

name: OEIS Complex
description: A combination of defects comprising OMPHALOCELE, exstrophy of the cloaca, ANUS IMPERFORATE, and spinal defects. This rare complex is thought to represent the most severe end of a spectrum of birth defects, the exstrophy-epispadias sequence, which, in order of increasing severity, includes phallic separation with EPISPADIAS, pubic diastasis, EXSTROPHY OF THE BLADDER, and CLOACAL EXSTROPHY. (From OMIM 258040)

name: Exostosin 2
description: A bifunctional glycosyltransferase involved in transferring GLUCURONIC ACID and N-ACETYLGLUCOSAMINE in the elongation of HEPARAN SULFATE chains. Mutations in the gene EXT2, coding for this protein (as well as mutations in other genes), are responsible for defects in heparan sulfate synthesis resulting in chromosome 11-linked HEREDITARY MULTIPLE EXOSTOSES. Exostosin 2, along with EXOSTOSIN 1, is a component of heparan sulfate polymerase.

name: Atrophic Maxilla
description: Loss of the MAXILLA bone mass and/or height due to natural edentulous maxilla (JAW, EDENTULOUS) or previous dental extractions. It may require a reconstruction via BONE TRANSPLANTATION and/or ALVEOLOPLASTY prior to a DENTAL IMPLANTATION.

name: Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm
description: A rare and aggressive hematologic malignancy derived from the precursors of PLASMACYTOID DENDRITIC CELLS. Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasms affect bone marrow and blood in addition to the lymph nodes, spleen, central nervous system, and skin.

name: Foveomacular Retinitis
description: A photochemical injury to retina tissues, usually at the RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM. It is commonly associated with sungazing, eclipse viewing, welding, or using a laser pointer without proper eye protection resulting in subjective visual disturbances (e.g., floaters) and reduced VISUAL ACUITY.

name: Oral Allergy Syndrome
description: Allergic reaction to certain foods, including fresh fruits, vegetables and nuts which share CROSS REACTIONS to allergens from trees, grass or pollens. Oral allergy syndrome is limited to itchy lips, mouth, and throat without severe ANAPHYLAXIS and is often associated with chronic EOSINOPHILIC ESOPHAGITIS.

name: Return of Individual Research Results
description: The return of individual results involves the return of information specific to the research subject. It encompasses information that is linked to the identity of a research subject and pertains to that subject and the focus of the study. Individual results can be obtained in clinical, social behavioral, and other types of research is not limited to clinical research (https://www.hhs.gov/ohrp/sachrp-committee/recommendations/attachment-b-return-individual-research-results/index.html).

name: Diabesity
description: Co-occurrence of DIABETES MELLITUS and OBESITY largely due to diabetic complication from HYPERGLYCEMIA. Diabesity is also associated with faster deterioration of diabetic symptoms and complications.

name: Politicization
