description: Generally an issue or an institution emerging into the sphere of politics such as making previously unpolitical matters political. (Tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/13501763.2019.1619188)

name: Social Prescribing
description: A way of referring people to non-clinical local services (for example, sports activities, arts, group learning, community-based activities, cookery and gardening), with the sole aim of ensuring human contact, followed by support and care.

name: Biosurfactants
description: Surface-active substances produced by plants and microorganisms, such as bacteria, fungi, and yeast. They have the ability to reduce surface and INTERFACIAL TENSION, making them useful in a variety of applications.

name: Functional Medicine
description: The clinical application of SYSTEMS BIOLOGY, that focuses on identifying the underlying drivers of a patient's disease and addressing, through personalized therapeutic interventions, those root causes of the disease.

name: RNA, Z-Form
description: A left-handed conformation of double stranded RNA that is similar in structure to Z-DNA.

name: Specialized Pro-Resolving Mediators
description: Lipid mediators derived from derivatives of POLYUNSATURATED FATTY ACIDS which tends to limit inflammation. They include resolvins, PROTECTIN, maresins, and LIPOXINS.

name: Non-Fungible Tokens
description: Digital certificates, in the form of data recorded on a BLOCKCHAIN, that signify ownership of associated digital items, such as images, music, or videos, not contained in the certificate data itself.

name: Advanced Maternal Age
description: Pregnancy in women at least 35 years old at the time of delivery. This was formerly known as geriatric pregnancy.

name: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy
description: A rare form of dilated cardiomyopathy which causes heart enlargement and weakness during the last month of pregnancy or within five months of delivery.

name: Medical Interpreting
description: The facilitation of verbal communication to assist in the healthcare process, by converting a message in one language to the same message in another language.

name: Drinking Establishments
description: Places where alcoholic beverages are served.

name: Aging in Place
description: To continue to live in one's home safely, independently, and comfortably in a familiar environment..

name: Network Meta-Analysis
description: Works consisting of meta-analysis of randomized trials in which estimates of comparative treatment effects are visualized and interpreted from a network of interventions that may or may not have been evaluated directly against each other. Common considerations in network meta-analysis include conceptual and statistical heterogeneity and incoherence.

name: Personal Care Products
description: Products used to maintain hygiene, health, and appearance.

name: Aerogels
description: A synthetic porous ultralight solid material is created from a gel through a supercritical drying process, in which the gel's liquid component is replaced with gas.

name: Vestibular Migraine
description: Vertigo or major dizziness associated with abnormal brain activity in migraine affecting the VESTIBULAR SYSTEM.

name: Sex Differences
description: A physical characteristic of an organism's sex that is not directly related to its REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEM.

name: Cortisol Awakening Response
description: A physiological response to awakening. It is a discreet and distinct component of the CORTISOL circadian cycle, with characteristics unrelated to cortisol secretion throughout the rest of the day (Wilhelm et al., 2007; Fries et al., 2009).

name: Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness
description: A chronic functional disorder with vertigo, dizziness and unsteadiness triggered by vestibular episode and psychological stress. Unlike in BENIGN PAROXYSMAL POSITIONAL VERTIGO, the otoliths on the OTOLITHIC MEMBRANE are not involved in pathology of persistent postural-perceptual dizziness.

name: Perilymphatic Fistula
description: An abnormal connection between inner ear and the surrounding structures, resulting in a leakage of the PERILYMPH. It is most common in a whiplash-type head trauma injury. Perilymph or labyrinthine fistulas may result in dizziness and/or intermittent hearing loss.

name: Autoimmune Inner Ear Disease
description: Inner ear diseases caused by autoimmune reaction, characterized by audiovestibular dysfunction including TINNITUS; VERTIGO and progressive SENSORINEURAL HEARING LOSS. Autoimmune inner ear disease may coexist with other systemic autoimmune diseases (e.g., COGAN SYNDROME).

name: Cervical Dizziness
description: Presence of vestibular symptoms such as light-headedness, dizziness or unsteadiness associated with injuries and pathologies of the CERVICAL VERTEBRAE. Cervicogenic dizziness are often associated with a whiplash-type injury and neck pain.

name: Immunoediting, Cancer
description: The reduction of the immunogenicity of a population of tumor cells over time, under the GENETIC SELECTION pressure of IMMUNOLOGIC SURVEILLANCE, leading to TUMOR IMMUNE EVASION.

name: Dual-Task Tests
description: Tests in which two tasks are performed simultaneously. Dual-Task Exercises can be used to show the performance differences of subjects in MULTITASKING BEHAVIOR.

name: Carbon Nanomaterials
description: Materials produced from CARBON with a unit size typically between 1 and 100 nanometers.

name: Carbon Quantum Dots
description: Spherical carbon materials typically less than 10 nanometers in size and possessing fluorescence emission properties.

name: Bioisosterism
description: A strategy used in PHARMACEUTIC CHEMISTRY where one part of a molecule is replaced with a different one that has similar physical or chemical properties, but with the aim of enhancing the biological activity, stability, or safety of the molecule.

name: Integrated Stress Response
description: A signaling pathway that enables cells to adapt to various stressors by modulating protein synthesis. It is initiated by the activation of specific PROTEIN KINASES (e.g., PERK, GCN2, PKR, and HRI) in response to distinct stress signals, including amino acid deprivation, VIRAL INFECTIONS, and OXIDATIVE STRESS.

name: Auditory Acuity
description: The ability to hear and distinguish one SOUND from another. These are typically assessed using whisper tests, tuning fork tests, or BONE CONDUCTION tests.

name: Epitranscriptome
description: The altered pattern of GENE EXPRESSION related to RNA METHYLATION.

name: Glycobiology
description: The study of the structure, function, and biology of carbohydrates (sugars) and carbohydrate-containing molecules, known as glycans, in biological systems.

name: Respiratory Therapists
description: A healthcare professional specializing in evaluating and treating patients with airway and breathing problems.

name: Blood-Spinal Cord Barrier
description: A specialized transport barrier between the PARENCHYMAL TISSUE of the SPINAL CORD and the surrounding BLOOD VESSELS.

name: Infographic
description: Graphic visual representations of educational content. It is used to deliver complex information, such as RESEARCH results.

name: Perineuronal Nets
description: Meshwork of extracellular matrix containing CHONDROITIN SULFATE PROTEOGLYCANS structures interposed among glial processes. Perineuronal nets (PNN) surround the soma and dendrites of certain neuronal cell types, e.g., inhibitory GABAergic PARVALBUMIN-positive INTERNEURONS. PNN plays a role in NEURONAL PLASTICITY and may modulate memory.

name: Carotid Webs
description: The presence of one or more thin flap-like membranes arising from the posterior wall of the INTERNAL CAROTID ARTERY bulb. While carotid webs can be asymptomatic, they may also be associated with TRANSIENT ISCHEMIC ATTACKS, and STROKE.

name: Reverse Vaccinology
description: A process where the genome of a pathogen is studied to find genes that may code for antigen proteins. If found, the putative antigen genes are then cloned, expressed in bacteria, and used to vaccinate experimental animals. If the expressed protein is shown to induce protective immunity it then becomes a candidate for further studies as a vaccine to be used to prevent infection.

name: DNA Nanostructures
description: Nanostructures formed from DNA. They are used as a scaffold for complex structures due to programmable assembly and control of size, shape, and function.

name: Plant-based Milk
description: MILK SUBSTITUITES derived from PLANTS.

name: Thermal Comfort
description: Maintaining comfortable temperature for living in general, and more specifically for patients in hospitals.

name: Autoimmune-Inflammatory Syndrome Induced by Adjuvants
description: An immune disease that is triggered by a variety of ADJUVANTS. It results in a spectrum of autoimmune and inflammatory responses that lead to significant health challenges.

name: Vascular Health
description: The state of the VASCULAR SYSTEM when functioning optimally without evidence of disease, disorders, or deficiencies.

name: UGT1A1 Enzyme
description: Glucuronosyltransferase encoded by UGT1 complex which encodes human bilirubin, phenol, and other UDP-glucuronosyltransferase isozymes with identical carboxyl termini. It catalyzes reactions where lipophilic substrates are conjugated with glucuronic acid to increase the metabolite's water solubility and excretion into either urine or bile. UGT1A1enzyme is essential for elimination and detoxification of drugs, xenobiotics and metabolites.

name: Ezrin
description: A cytoskeletal protein and PROTEIN-TYROSINE KINASE substrate that links cytoskeletal structures to the PLASMA MEMBRANE. In EPITHELIAL CELLS, it is essential for the formation of MICROVILLI and membrane ruffles on the apical pole and is also required for macropinocytosis (see PINOCYTOSIS) along with the GUANINE NUCLEOTIDE EXCHANGE FACTOR PLEKHG6.

name: Receptor, Farnesoid X-Activated
description: An ORPHAN NUCLEAR RECEPTOR that is activated by farnesol metabolites in bile acid; Increases insulin production and sensitivity.

name: MAP Kinase Kinase Kinase 7
description: MAP kinase kinase kinase which plays a critical role in cellular responses to environmental stimuli and CYTOKINES.

name: Cadherin 5
description: A classical cadherin which plays a critical role in maintaining permeability of the ENDOTHELIUM.

name: Pentraxins
description: A family of ACUTE PHASE PROTEINS characterized by a shared pentraxin PROTEIN DOMAIN. They include C-reactive protein and serum amyloid P component and function in the regulation of INNATE IMMUNITY and INFLAMMATION.

name: Picornavirales
description: Viruses with a monopartitite or bipartite positive-strand RNA genome that share the following properties: auto-proteolytically processed polyprotein(s), a common three-domain replication block (Hel-Pro-Pol domain consisting of a superfamily III helicase, a proteinase with a chymotrypsin-like structure and a superfamily I RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) and non-enveloped icosahedral virions approximately 30 nm in diameter with a pseudo-T=3 symmetry.

name: Superoxide Dismutase 2
description: A superoxide dismutase that processes REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES generated by mitochondrial respiration. It protects tissues from damage during disease progression.

name: Sphingosine Kinase
description: The catalyst to phosphorylate SPHINGOSINE into sphingosine-1-phosphate; Important in ANGIOGENESIS, CELL SURVIVAL, and CELL MIGRATION

name: Proteoglycan 4
description: A proteoglycan involved in joint surface lubrication and encoded by the PRG4 gene. Altered expression occurs in some forms of ARTHRITIS.

name: Tacrolimus Binding Protein 5
description: A tacrolimus binding protein with peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase activity that interacts with PROGESTERONE RECEPTOR complexes and HSP90 HEAT-SHOCK PROTEINS.

name: LexA Repressor Protein
description: A bacterial repressor protein that has serine endopeptidase activity. LexA represses transcription of genes involved in the SOS RESPONSE to DNA DAMAGE.

name: Kcnj11 Channel
description: An inwardly-rectifying potassium channel that forms the pore of KATP CHANNELS. It regulates potassium permeability as a function of cytoplasmic ATP and ADP concentrations in many different cell types.

name: Endothelial PAS Domain-Containing Protein 1
description: A basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor that regulates expression of genes in response to oxygen, including VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR. It plays a role in the development of blood vessels (NEOVASCULARIZATION, PHYSIOLOGIC) and lung tissue.

name: Myosin Binding Protein C
description: A myosin-binding protein found in the SARCOMERES of STRIATED MUSCLE. Iit has slow and fast paralogs. Myosin-binding protein C regulates systolic and diastolic activity in MYOCARDIUM and muscle contraction in SKELETAL MUSCLE.

name: Force Potentiation
description: A phenomenon where a muscle's force output is temporarily enhanced due to its previous contraction history.

name: Polyacrylamides
description: Synthetic, water-soluble acrylic polymers with the formula -CH2CHCONH2-.

name: Fibroblast Activation Protein Alpha
description: A large, gelatin-degrading membrane SERINE ENDOPEPTIDASE complex expressed by stromal FIBROBLASTS of epithelial cancers; it is a biomarker for MELANOMA cell invasiveness.

name: Fos-Related Antigen 1
description: A component of TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR AP-1; do not confuse with fibrinogen-related antigen (FRA antigen)

name: Bis(5'-adenosyl)triphosphatase
description: A dinucleoside triphosphate hydrolase that has a critical role in regulating the expression of genes essential for CELL PROLIFERATION; CELL SURVIVAL, and modulating APOPTOSIS.

name: Natural Resistance-associated Macrophage Protein 1
description: A cation transport protein that shares structural homology with prokaryotic and eukaryotic transport proteins. In mammals, it is a MACROPHAGE-specific antiporter, transporting metal ions in either direction against a proton gradient, and localizes to membranes of late ENDOSOMES and LYSOSOMES, where it may contribute to antimicrobial activity.

name: Pigment Epithelium-Derived Factor
description: A neurotrophic protein and serpin that induces CELL DIFFERENTIATION in RETINOBLASTOMA cells and also functions as an ANGIOGENESIS INHIBITOR in the mammalian eye.

name: Heparanase
description: A mammalian endoglucuronidase which degrades HEPARAN SULFATE glycosaminoglycans into short 5-6 kDa pieces.

name: Noggin Protein
description: A protein that binds to certain BONE MORPHOGENIC PROTEINS to regulate their activity. In Xenopus embryos, this is a dorsalizing factor localized to the SPEMANN ORGANIZER. Mutations in this protein may occur in NOG-RELATED-SYMPHALANGISM SPECTRUM DISORDER.

name: Tsg101 Protein
description: A ubiquitin regulator which encodes a coiled-coil domain that interacts with STATHMIN and is involved in endosomal protein sorting

name: Retinoid Isomerohydrolase
description: A cis-trans isomerase that catalyzes the isomerization of all trans-retinol to 11-cis-retinol (VITAMIN A) in the dark. It is expressed in the RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM and also converts ALL-TRANS-RETINYL ESTERS to 11-cis-retinol.

name: Myocilin
description: A secreted glycoprotein that controls activation of signaling pathways in adjacent cells (PARACRINE COMMUNICATION) for processes that include CELL ADHESION; CELL MIGRATION; and organization of the CYTOSKELETON. It is primarily expressed in the RETINA and variants in the myocillin gene cause GLAUCOMA 1, OPEN ANGLE, A.

name: Interleukin-24
description: An interleukin that suppresses MELANOMA cell growth and colony formation. ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM STRESS activates its expression.

name: Dectin-1
description: A C-type lectin that functions as a pattern recognition receptor on DENDRITIC CELLS and other immune cells. It is specific for beta-1,-linked and beta 1,6-linked GLUCANS that constitute the CELL WALL of pathogenic bacteria and fungi, and is essential for the TOLL-LIKE RECEPTOR 2 INNATE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE and activation of NF-KAPPA-B.

name: Phosphoinositide 5-Phosphatases
description: Phosphoric monoester hydrolases that dephosphorylate PHOSPHATIDYLINOSITOLS to regulate CELL SIGNALING.

name: Sortilin
description: A component of TRANSPORT VESICLES that contain GLUT4 PROTEIN. It functions in the transport and processing of LDL RECEPTORS.

name: Serum-Glucocorticoid Regulated Kinases
description: Serine-threonine-protein kinases that regulates a variety of ION CHANNELS and MEMBRANE TRANSPORT PROTEINS, as well as cellular processes that include neuronal excitability, CELL PROLIFERATION; CELL SURVIVAL; and APOPTOSIS. They also have important roles in the cellular stress response (STRESS, PHYSIOLOGICAL), renal sodium retention and potassium elimination.

name: Interferon Regulatory Factor-8
description: An interferon regulatory factor regulated by INTERFERON-GAMMA that binds the interferon-inducible ENHANCER ELEMENTS of HISTOCOMPATIBILITY ANTIGENS CLASS I genes.

name: Histone Deacetylase 3
description: A histone deacetylase that catalyzes the deacetylation of the core HISTONES (H2A, H2B,H3, and H4) as well as other cellular proteins. It functions in the CELL NUCLEUS as part of the nuclear-receptor corepressor complex to regulate the GENETIC TRANSCRIPTION of NUCLEAR RECEPTORS.

name: Major Vault Protein
description: The major structural protein of vault ribonucleoprotein particles, which function in NUCLEOCYTOPLASMIC TRANSPORT and SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION.

name: Alternative Oxidase
description: The terminal OXIDOREDUCTASE in the plant mitochondrial electron transport chain utilized in the alternative pathway of respiration. It limits REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES production and bypasses ELECTRON TRANSPORT COMPLEX III and ELECTRON TRANSPORT COMPLEX IV to keep metabolic homeostasis during PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS.

name: Lysophospholipase D
description: A lysophospholipase that catalyzes the hydrolysis of GLYCEROPHOSPHOLIPIDS to produce LYSOPHOSPHATIDIC ACIDS and corresponding AMINES. Autotaxin is secreted lysophospholipase D and produces lysophosphatidic acid in EXTRACELLULAR FLUID.

name: MAP-Kinase-Activated Kinase 2
description: A serine-threonine protein kinase that functions in many different processes including the cellular response to PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS, production of CYTOKINES; ENDOCYTOSIS; CYTOSKELETON dynamics, CELL MIGRATION; and CELL PROLIFERATION. It is phosphorylated by MAPK14 in response to stress, and in turn phosphorylates substrates at a SERINE that is preceded by a large hydrophobic amino acid.

name: CD69 Antigens
description: An activation antigen and C-type lectin that is rapidly induced and phosphorylated after IL-2 stimulation of NK CELLS and a subset of low buoyant density T-LYMPHOCYTES.

name: rab11 GTP-Binding Proteins
description: Rab GTP-binding proteins that function primarily in regulating intracellular PROTEIN TRANSPORT among membrane-bound ORGANELLES and in ENDOCYTOSIS. They also participate in the establishment of CELL POLARITY in EPITHELIAL CELLS.

name: Semaglutide
description: A glucagon-like peptide and GLP-1 agonist used to enhance glycemic control of TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS, and for OBESITY MANAGEMENT.

name: cGAS-STING Signaling Pathway
description: A signal transduction pathway that involves cGMP-AMP synthase (cGAS), stimulator of interferon genes (STING), and downstream signaling adaptors. This pathway plays an essential role in the innate immune system by activating immune defenses, particularly against invading pathogens or harmful damage.

name: STING Protein
description: A membrane protein that functions in INNATE IMMUNITY and INFLAMMATION through the CGAS-STING SIGNALING PATHWAY. It acts as a sensor of cytosolic DNA from bacteria and viruses and promotes the production of INTERFERON TYPE I.

name: Scaffold Protein ILK
description: A scaffold protein originally thought to function as a SERINE-THREONINE PROTEIN KINASE. It lacks kinase activity and regulates a variety of cellular processes that include CELL ADHESION; CELL MIGRATION; and assembly of FOCAL ADHESIONS.

name: Thymosin beta(4)
description: A thymosin that functions to regulate organization of the CYTOSKELETON. It binds to and sequesters ACTIN monomers to inhibit POLYMERIZATION and also inhibits CELL DIFFERENTIATION of some STEM CELLS.

name: PTEN-Induced Putative Kinase
description: A serine-threonine-protein kinase which senses damaged MITOCHONDRIA and protects against mitochondrial dysfunction caused by PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS. It phosphorylates proteins on the OUTER MITOCHONDRIAL MEMBRANE to coordinate quality control mechanisms that remove and replace dysfunctional mitochondrial components. Mutations in the PINK1 gene, which encodes PTEN-induced putative kinase, are associated with PARKINSON DISEASE.

name: Neurodevelopment
description: A developmental process in which NEURONS extend and form SYNAPSES.

name: SS-A Antigen
description: A cytoplasmic autoantigen and ribonucleoprotein implicated in nascent RNA protection. It is a target of AUTOANTIBODIES in patients with SJOGREN'S SYNDROME.

name: TRIM21 Protein
description: A ubiquitin-protein ligase that supports INNATE IMMUNITY by binding to the invariant chain of antibody-virus complexes. It prevents expression of viral genes.

name: Sodium-Iodide Symporters
description: Proteins that cotransport sodium ions and iodide ions across cellular membranes. They function in the biosynthesis of TRIIODOTHYRONINE and THYROXINE.

name: Melanopsin
description: A G-PROTEIN-COUPLED RECEPTOR found in RETINAL GANGLION CELLS that regulates non-image forming visual functions like CIRCADIAN RHYTHM responses and pupil dilation.

name: Phospholamban
description: A regulatory membrane peptide of SARCOPLASMIC RETICULUM CALCIUM-TRANSPORTING ATPASES. Its phosphorylation by CYCLIC AMP-DEPENDENT PROTEIN KINASES allows protein kinase-induced stimulation of calcium transport.

name: Retinol-Binding Proteins, Interstitial
description: A subclass of retinol-binding proteins that take part in the transport of RETINOL between the ROD CELL OUTER SEGMENT and RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM. Do not confuse with inverted repeat binding protein (also known as IRBP).

name: DC-Specific ICAM-3 Grabbing Nonintegrin
description: A pathogen pattern recognition receptor and C-type lectin expressed on the surface of immature DENDRITIC CELLS (DCs). It also functions as a high-affinity receptor for intercellular adhesion molecules ICAM-2 and ICAM-3 to initiate the primary IMMUNE RESPONSE.

name: Chondroitin Sulfate Proteoglycan 4
description: Transmembrane proteoglycans expressed in OLIGODENDROCYTE PRECURSOR CELLS; NEUROGLIA: and PERICYTES. It is a biomarker and treatment target for MELANOMA.

name: Cuproptosis
description: A type of regulated cell death that is triggered by the accumulation of COPPER in MITOCHONDRIA.

name: Interferon Regulatory Factor-4
description: An interferon regulatory factor that is key in immune CELL DIFFERENTIATION, LYMPHOCYTE ACTIVATION, and generating ANTIBODY-PRODUCING CELLS. They play a key role in the development of DENDRITIC CELLS.

name: Royal Jelly
description: A secretion produced by honey BEES that consists of water, protein, MONOSACCHARIDES; and FATTY ACIDS that include 10-hydroxy-2-decenoic acid, sebacic acid, 10-hydroxydecanoic acid, and 9-oxo-2-decanoic acid. It also contains trace amounts of MINERALS; ANTI-BACTERIAL COMPOUNDS; B VITAMINS; and VITAMIN C.

name: Protein Kinase C zeta
description: A serine-threonine protein kinase that induces phosphorylation & inactivation of NF-KAPPAB INHIBITOR ALPHA in vitro.

name: betaIG-H3 Protein
description: An extracellular matrix protein that binds FIBRILLAR COLLAGENS and functions in CELL ADHESION; CELL MIGRATION; and CELL PROLIFERATION. In humans, the TGFBI gene encodes beta IG-H3 protein, and mutations in TGFBI cause CORNEAL DYSTROPHIES, HEREDITARY.

name: p300-CBP-Associated Factor
description: A p300-CBP transcription factor with intrinsic HISTONE ACETYLASE activity that functions to promote TRANSCRIPTIONAL ACTIVATION. Among its functions is suppression of the CELL CYCLE where it competes with ADENOVIRUS E1A PROTEINS.

name: Dolutegravir
description: An HIV integrase inhibitor that is used in the treatment of HIV INFECTIONS in combination with other ANTI-HIV AGENTS.

name: Abacavir
description: A carbocyclic nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor with potent and selective anti-HIV activity.

name: Diamine N-Acetyltransferase
description: An acetyltransferase that transfers an acetyl group to SPERMIDINE as it is converted into PUTRESCINE. It occurs in two types: the cytosolic N1-acetyltransferse (cSAT) and the nuclear N8-acetyltransferase (nSAT).

name: RE1-Silencing Transcription Factor
description: A repressor protein that restricts neuronal gene transcription in non-neuronal cells.

name: Lipopolysaccharide-Binding Protein
description: An acute-phase protein that binds to the lipid a moiety of bacterial LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDES, a glycolipid present in the outer membrane of all GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA. The Lipopolysaccharide-Binding Proteins/Lipopolysaccharide complex may be involved in immune response by interacting with the CD14 ANTIGEN

name: Proto-Oncogene Protein Spi-1
description: An ETS MOTIF - containing trans-activator that functions in HEMATOPOIESIS. It activates transcription of critical genes by making genomic regions within HETEROCHROMATIN accessible to other key transcription factors.

name: Monocarboxylate Transport Protein 1
description: A bi-directional monocarboxylic acid transporter that occurs in many different tissues, including MYOCARDIUM; LYMPHOCYTES; and MONOCYTES. It catalyzes transport across the PLASMA MEMBRANE of monocarboxylates such as LACTATE; PYRUVATE; ACETATE; and KETONE BODIES.

name: Cyclic Guanosine Monophosphate-Adenosine Monophosphate Synthase
description: A nucleotidyltransferase that catalyzes the formation of cyclic GMP-AMP in mammals. This activates the STING1 PROTEIN through the CGAS-STING SIGNALING PATHWAY, which triggers the production of INTERFERON TYPE I and other CYTOKINES.

name: Solute Carrier Family 11, Member 2
description: A cation transport protein that is important in metal transport, particularly iron, in MACROPHAGES. It is important in intestinal iron absorption and supplying iron for ERYTHROCYTES.

name: UDP-Galactose Translocators
description: Monosaccharide transport proteins that move cytosolic URIDINE DIPHOSPHATE GALACTOSE into the Golgi apparatus by exchanging it for URIDINE MONOPHOSPHATE. They can also transport URIDINE DIPHOSPHATE N-ACETYLGALACTOSAMINE.

name: Drug Dispensaries
description: Facilities other than traditional PHARMACIES that provide medicinal products to people in a hospital setting, or at a retail location.

name: Asparaginyl Endopeptidase
description: A cysteine endopeptidase that occurs in LYSOSOMES of MACROPHAGES where it hydrolyzes molecules containing ASPARAGINE. It plays a critical role in ANTIGEN PRESENTATION.

name: Atrial Natriuretic Factor Receptor B
description: An atrial natriuretic factor receptor that regulates cardiac growth. It has a binding preference for NATRIURETIC PEPTIDE, C-TYPE.

name: Pseudobulbar Affect
description: A condition that is characterized by episodes of sudden uncontrollable and inappropriate laughing or crying. It can result from certain neurological conditions or injuries that may impact the way the brain controls emotions.

name: Omphalocele
description: A congenital defect with major fissure in the ABDOMINAL WALL at the UMBILICUS resulting in the extrusion of VISCERA through the UMBILICUS. Unlike GASTROSCHISIS, omphalocele is covered with PERITONEUM but without overlying SKIN.

name: Cucurbit(n)urils
description: A group of barrel-shaped imidazolines composed of (n) glycoluril monomers linked by methylene bridges and are often abbreviated CB[n] or CB*[n]. They have a high binding affinity to CATIONS and neutral molecules.

name: Taurine Transporters
description: An amino acid transport protein that acts as a SYMPORTER transporting taurine with sodium across the CELL MEMBRANE. It plays a role in the metabolism of NEUROTRANSMITTER AGENTS.

name: S100 Calcium Binding Protein A10
description: A member of the S100 family of calcium-binding proteins that binds BCL-XL PROTEIN. It acts as a PLASMINOGEN receptor that mediates plasminogen activation and is considered both a LIGAND for and a subunit of ANNEXIN A2.

name: Proteoglycan Link Protein
description: An extracellular matrix protein that interacts with proteoglycan monomers to form aggregate structures. It is involved in stabilizing the interaction between the proteoglycan subunit and HYALURONIC ACID in CARTILAGE.

name: DNA Excision Repair Protein ERCC-5
description: A DNA helicase that performs EXCISION REPAIR functions following UV damage. In humans, mutations in the ERCC5 gene can cause XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM, COMPLEMENTATION GROUP G and increase susceptibility to SKIN CANCER.

name: Myocardin
description: A transcriptional coactivator protein highly expressed in SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS and CARDIOMYOCYTES. It functions as a cofactor for SERUM RESPONSE FACTOR and regulates smooth muscle contraction, smooth muscle CELL DIFFERENTIATION, and cardiac muscle development.

name: Fatty Acid Amide Hydrolases
description: Amidohydrolases that catalyze the hydrolysis of endogenous amidated lipids such as OLEYLAMIDE and ANANDAMIDE to FATTY ACIDS, resulting in changes to their roles in SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION.

name: Trans-Activation Responsive RNA-Binding Protein
description: An RNA binding protein that binds to the HIV LONG TERMINAL REPEAT. An infected organism will produce it as RNA INTERFERENCE to prevent HIV from repressing host EIF-2 KINASE expression.

name: Organic Cation Transporter 3
description: A potential-sensitive organic cation transporter protein that mediates the transport of a wide spectrum of organic CATIONS. It plays a role in the uptake of monoamine NEUROTRANSMITTER AGENTS.

name: Growth Arrest-Specific Protein 6
description: A ligand for RECEPTOR PROTEIN-TYROSINE KINASES AXL, TYRO3 and MERTK through which it regulates cell growth and survival of ENDOTHELIAL CELLS; CELL ADHESION; and CELL MIGRATION. GAS6 also has critical roles in the development of NATURAL KILLER CELLS and PLATELET ACTIVATION.

name: Infographics as Topic
description: Works about graphic visual representations of educational content.

name: Meiotic Recombination Protein SPO11
description: An endodeoxyribonuclease that functions as part of a DNA TOPOISOMERASE II complex to create DOUBLE-STRAND DNA BREAKS for initiating HOMOLOGOUS RECOMBINATION in MEIOSIS.

name: N-myc Downstream-Regulated Gene 1 Protein
description: A cell cycle protein required for activating TUMOR SUPPRESSOR PROTEIN P53 -mediated CASPASES and APOPTOSIS. It is up-regulated during colon epithelial cell differentiation and down-regulated in COLORECTAL NEOPLASMS.

name: Empty Spiracles Homeobox Proteins
description: Transcription factors that play a role in the development of NEURONS. They contain a homeodomain homologous to that of the Drosophila empty spiracles head gap gene product (ems).

name: Homeobox A1 Protein
description: A homeodomain protein that plays a role in the proliferation and differentiation of HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS. It is activated by TRETINOIN.

name: Thrombospondin 2
description: A thrombospondin that mediates CELL-TO-CELL INTERACTION and cell - EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX interactions. It may also function as an ANGIOGENESIS INHIBITOR through its interaction with CD36 ANTIGENS.

name: Connexin 50
description: A connexin which forms the structural component of GAP JUNCTIONS in the EYE LENS. In humans, variants in the GJA8 gene cause multiple types of CATARACT.

name: Engrailed 2 Protein
description: A homeodomain protein that influences the development and neuroprotection of DOPAMINERGIC NEURONS in the MESENCEPHALON. It is implicated in several types of cancer.

name: Pseudothrombocytopenia
description: A laboratory phenomenon where a low platelet count is observed due to the action of ANTICOAGULANTS such as EDTA causing platelet AGGLUTINATION.

name: Extrachromosomal DNA
description: DNA that occurs outside of CHROMOSOMES in prokaryotic or eukaryotic cells.

name: Y-Family DNA Polymerases
description: A family of DNA polymerases that have the capability to carry out TRANSLESION DNA SYNTHESIS and have low replication fidelity on undamaged DNA.

name: Prostasin
description: A serine endopeptidase that has a similar cleavage specificity to TRYPSIN, favoring substrates with poly-basic amino acid sequences. Prostasin plays a critical role in activating EPITHELIAL SODIUM CHANNELS through cleavage of the ENAC gamma subunit.

name: Replisomes
description: A multienzyme complex that carries out DNA REPLICATION. Replisomes consist of DNA HELICASES; REPLICATION FACTOR C; PROLIFERATING CELL NUCLEAR ANTIGEN; DNA GYRASE; DNA TOPOISOMERASES; DNA LIGASES; and RIBONUCLEASE H.

name: Neurabins
description: Neuronal proteins that bind to F-ACTIN and modulate the morphology of DENDRITIC SPINES, as well as excitatory SYNAPTIC TRANSMISSION through their regulatory effects on PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE 1.

name: Frizzled-Related Proteins
description: Membrane proteins which share sequence similarity with FRIZZLED RECEPTORS and participate in a variety of CELL SIGNALING activities that regulate CELL GROWTH PROCESSES and MORPHOGENESIS.

name: Avapritinib
description: A tyrosine kinase receptor inhibitor that targets mutants of PROTO-ONCOGENE PROTEIN KIT and PLATELET-DERIVED GROWTH FACTOR ALPHA RECEPTOR.

name: Evidence Synthesis
description: Evidence synthesis refers to any method that combines data and insights from multiple sources to summarize existing literature and support informed decisions, often in health, social care, or policy contexts.

name: Adducins
description: Membrane and cytoskeletal-associated proteins that bind CALMODULIN and promote assembly of SPECTRIN and ACTIN FILAMENTS into MACROMOLECULAR PROTEIN COMPLEXES.

name: Protein Kinase C-lambda
description: A calcium- and diacylglycerol-independent protein kinase C that protects against APOPTOSIS and functions in NF-KAPPA B signaling, CELL DIFFERENTIATION and CELL POLARITY.

name: Polyoxometalates
description: Anionic polyelectrolytes that contain metal-oxo clusters. They are often used in CATALYSIS due to their structural variation and versatility.

name: Formyltetrahydrofolate Dehydrogenase
description: An oxidoreductase that metabolizes 10-formyltertahydrofolate into tetrahydrofolate.

name: Tuberculosis Disease
description: An advanced form of TUBERCULOSIS that is not being controlled by the IMMUNE SYSTEM. It requires prompt and effective treatment to prevent medical complications and transmission of the disease to other people.

name: Serine Racemase
description: A RACEMASE which catalyzes the conversion of L-Serine to D-Serine.

name: Hydroxyacylglutathione Hydrolase
description: A thiolesterase that catalyzes the production of GLUTATHIONE and D-LACTIC ACID from the hydrolysis of S-D-lactoyl-glutathione. In vertebrates, only one gene that encodes hydroxyacylglutathione hydrolase is known to occur. In yeast and higher plants, separate genes encode the cytosolic and mitochondrial forms of this enzyme.

name: Nursing Home Residents
description: Persons who reside in NURSING HOMES.

name: Dentin Sialophosphoprotein
description: An extracellular matrix protein that is highly expressed in ODONTOBLASTS. It is cleaved into 2 chains: dentin sialoprotein and dentin phosphoprotein. Mutations in the human DSPP gene, which encodes dentin sialophosphoprotein, can cause DENTINOGENESIS IMPERFECTA.

name: Non-Melanoma Skin Neoplasms
description: Skin neoplasms that are not MELANOMA.

name: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma
description: A non-melanoma skin neoplasm that is one of the three principal types of skin cancer. It often presents as a hard lump or ulcer and is more likely to metastasize than BASAL CELL CARCINOMA.

name: Hippo Kinases
description: Protein serine-threonine kinases that regulate cell growth and CELL PROLIFERATION in the HIPPO SIGNALING PATHWAY. They control mammalian cell and organ size.

name: Acetrizoic Acid
description: An iodinated radiographic contrast medium used as acetrizoate sodium in HYSTEROSALPINGOGRAPHY.

name: Acetyl-CoA C-Acetyltransferase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the formation of acetoacetyl-CoA from two molecules of ACETYL COA. Some enzymes called thiolase or thiolase-I have referred to this activity or to the activity of ACETYL-COA C-ACYLTRANSFERASE.

name: Acetyl-CoA C-Acyltransferase
description: Enzyme that catalyzes the final step of fatty acid oxidation in which ACETYL COA is released and the CoA ester of a fatty acid two carbons shorter is formed.

name: Acetyl-CoA Carboxylase
description: A carboxylating enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of ATP, acetyl-CoA, and HCO3- to ADP, orthophosphate, and malonyl-CoA. It is a biotinyl-protein that also catalyzes transcarboxylation. The plant enzyme also carboxylates propanoyl-CoA and butanoyl-CoA (From Enzyme Nomenclature, 1992) EC 6.4.1.2.

name: Acetyl-CoA Hydrolase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes reversibly the hydrolysis of acetyl-CoA to yield CoA and acetate. The enzyme is involved in the oxidation of fatty acids. EC 3.1.2.1.

name: Acetyl Coenzyme A
description: Acetyl CoA participates in the biosynthesis of fatty acids and sterols, in the oxidation of fatty acids and in the metabolism of many amino acids. It also acts as a biological acetylating agent.

name: Acetate-CoA Ligase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the formation of CoA derivatives from ATP, acetate, and CoA to form AMP, pyrophosphate, and acetyl CoA. It acts also on propionates and acrylates. EC 6.2.1.1.

name: Acetylation
description: Formation of an acetyl derivative. (Stedman, 25th ed)

name: Acetylcarnitine
description: An acetic acid ester of CARNITINE that facilitates movement of ACETYL COA into the matrices of mammalian MITOCHONDRIA during the oxidation of FATTY ACIDS.

name: Acetylcholine
description: A neurotransmitter found at neuromuscular junctions, autonomic ganglia, parasympathetic effector junctions, a subset of sympathetic effector junctions, and at many sites in the central nervous system.

name: Acetylcholinesterase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of ACETYLCHOLINE to CHOLINE and acetate. In the CNS, this enzyme plays a role in the function of peripheral neuromuscular junctions. EC 3.1.1.7.

name: Acetylcysteine
description: The N-acetyl derivative of CYSTEINE. It is used as a mucolytic agent to reduce the viscosity of mucous secretions. It has also been shown to have antiviral effects in patients with HIV due to inhibition of viral stimulation by reactive oxygen intermediates.

name: Acetyldigitoxins
description: Cardioactive derivatives of lanatoside A or of DIGITOXIN. They are used for fast digitalization in congestive heart failure.

name: Acetyldigoxins
description: Alpha- or beta-acetyl derivatives of DIGOXIN or lanatoside C from Digitalis lanata. They are better absorbed and longer acting than digoxin and are used in congestive heart failure.

name: Acetylene
description: The simplest two carbon alkyne with the formula HCCH.

name: Acetylesterase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of acetate esters and water to alcohols and acetate. EC 3.1.1.6.

name: Acetylgalactosamine
description: The N-acetyl derivative of galactosamine.

name: Acetylglucosamine
description: The N-acetyl derivative of glucosamine.

name: Acetylglucosaminidase
description: A beta-N-Acetylhexosaminidase that catalyzes the hydrolysis of terminal, non-reducing 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-beta-glucose residues in chitobiose and higher analogs as well as in glycoproteins. Has been used widely in structural studies on bacterial cell walls and in the study of diseases such as MUCOLIPIDOSIS and various inflammatory disorders of muscle and connective tissue.

name: Acetylmuramyl-Alanyl-Isoglutamine
description: Peptidoglycan immunoadjuvant originally isolated from bacterial cell wall fragments; also acts as pyrogen and may cause arthritis; stimulates both humoral and cellular immunity.

name: Acecainide
description: A major metabolite of PROCAINAMIDE. Its anti-arrhythmic action may cause cardiac toxicity in kidney failure.

name: Acetylserotonin O-Methyltransferase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of a methyl group from S-adenosylmethionine to N-acetylserotonin to form N-acetyl-5-methoxytryptamine (MELATONIN).

name: Acetylthiocholine
description: An agent used as a substrate in assays for cholinesterases, especially to discriminate among enzyme types.

name: Acetyltransferases
description: Enzymes catalyzing the transfer of an acetyl group, usually from acetyl coenzyme A, to another compound. EC 2.3.1.

name: Achievement
description: Success in bringing an effort to the desired end; the degree or level of success attained in some specified area (esp. scholastic) or in general.

name: Achilles Tendon
description: Tendon that connects the muscles in the back of the calf to the HEEL BONE.

name: Achlorhydria
description: A lack of HYDROCHLORIC ACID in GASTRIC JUICE despite stimulation of gastric secretion.

name: Acholeplasma
description: A genus of gram-negative organisms including saprophytic and parasitic or pathogenic species.

name: Acholeplasma laidlawii
description: An organism originally isolated from sewage, manure, humus, and soil, but recently found as a parasite in mammals and birds.

name: Acholeplasmataceae
description: Gram-negative organisms including apparently free-living saphrophytes as well as mammalian and avian parasites, and possibly pathogens.

name: Achondroplasia
description: An autosomal dominant disorder that is the most frequent form of short-limb dwarfism. Affected individuals exhibit short stature caused by rhizomelic shortening of the limbs, characteristic facies with frontal bossing and mid-face hypoplasia, exaggerated lumbar lordosis, limitation of elbow extension, GENU VARUM, and trident hand. (Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man, http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Omim, MIM#100800, April 20, 2001)

name: Acid Phosphatase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of an orthophosphoric monoester and water to an alcohol and orthophosphate. EC 3.1.3.2.

name: Acid-Base Equilibrium
description: The balance between acids and bases in the BODY FLUIDS. The pH (HYDROGEN-ION CONCENTRATION) of the arterial BLOOD provides an index for the total body acid-base balance.

name: Acid-Base Imbalance
description: Disturbances in the ACID-BASE EQUILIBRIUM of the body.

name: Acidosis
description: A pathologic condition of acid accumulation or depletion of base in the body. The two main types are RESPIRATORY ACIDOSIS and metabolic acidosis, due to metabolic acid build up.

name: Acidosis, Lactic
description: Acidosis caused by accumulation of lactic acid more rapidly than it can be metabolized. It may occur spontaneously or in association with diseases such as DIABETES MELLITUS; LEUKEMIA; or LIVER FAILURE.

name: Acidosis, Renal Tubular
description: A group of genetic disorders of the KIDNEY TUBULES characterized by the accumulation of metabolically produced acids with elevated plasma chloride, hyperchloremic metabolic ACIDOSIS. Defective renal acidification of URINE (proximal tubules) or low renal acid excretion (distal tubules) can lead to complications such as HYPOKALEMIA, hypercalcinuria with NEPHROLITHIASIS and NEPHROCALCINOSIS, and RICKETS.

name: Acidosis, Respiratory
description: Respiratory retention of carbon dioxide. It may be chronic or acute.

name: Acids
description: Chemical compounds which yield hydrogen ions or protons when dissolved in water, whose hydrogen can be replaced by metals or basic radicals, or which react with bases to form salts and water (neutralization). An extension of the term includes substances dissolved in media other than water. (Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

name: Acids, Acyclic
description: Carboxylic acids that have open-chain molecular structures as opposed to ring-shaped structures.

name: Acids, Aldehydic
description: Dicarboxylic acids in which one of the carboxyl groups (-COOH) has been replaced by an aldehyde group (-CHO).

name: Acids, Carbocyclic
description: Carboxylic acids that have a homocyclic ring structure in which all the ring atoms are carbon.

name: Acids, Heterocyclic
description: A class of acids containing a ring structure in which at least one atom other than CARBON is incorporated.

name: Acids, Noncarboxylic
description: Inorganic acids with a non metal, other than carbon, attached to hydrogen, or an acid radical containing no carbon.

name: Acidulated Phosphate Fluoride
description: A sodium fluoride solution, paste or powder, which has been acidulated to pH 3 to 4 and buffered with a phosphate. It is used in the prevention of dental caries.

name: Acinetobacter
description: A genus of gram-negative bacteria of the family MORAXELLACEAE, found in soil and water and of uncertain pathogenicity.

name: Acinetobacter Infections
description: Infections with bacteria of the genus ACINETOBACTER.

name: Acne Vulgaris
description: A chronic disorder of the pilosebaceous apparatus associated with an increase in sebum secretion. It is characterized by open comedones (blackheads), closed comedones (whiteheads), and pustular nodules. The cause is unknown, but heredity and age are predisposing factors.

name: Acne Keloid
description: A type of acneiform disorder in which secondary pyogenic infection in and around pilosebaceous structures ends in keloidal scarring. It manifests as persistent folliculitis of the back of the neck associated with occlusion of the follicular orifices. It is most often encountered in black or Asian men.

name: Aconitate Hydratase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the reversible hydration of cis-aconitate to yield citrate or isocitrate. It is one of the citric acid cycle enzymes. EC 4.2.1.3.

name: Aconitic Acid
description: A tricarboxylic acid with the formula (COOH)-CH2-C(COOH)=CH-COOH.

name: Aconitine
description: A C19 norditerpenoid alkaloid (DITERPENES) from the root of ACONITUM; DELPHINIUM and larkspurs. It activates VOLTAGE-GATED SODIUM CHANNELS. It has been used to induce ARRHYTHMIAS in experimental animals and it has anti-inflammatory and anti-neuralgic properties.

name: Vestibulocochlear Nerve
description: The 8th cranial nerve. The vestibulocochlear nerve has a cochlear part (COCHLEAR NERVE) which is concerned with hearing and a vestibular part (VESTIBULAR NERVE) which mediates the sense of balance and head position. The fibers of the cochlear nerve originate from neurons of the SPIRAL GANGLION and project to the cochlear nuclei (COCHLEAR NUCLEUS). The fibers of the vestibular nerve arise from neurons of Scarpa's ganglion and project to the VESTIBULAR NUCLEI.

name: Vestibulocochlear Nerve Diseases
description: Pathological processes of the VESTIBULOCOCHLEAR NERVE, including the branches of COCHLEAR NERVE and VESTIBULAR NERVE. Common examples are VESTIBULAR NEURITIS, cochlear neuritis, and ACOUSTIC NEUROMA. Clinical signs are varying degree of HEARING LOSS; VERTIGO; and TINNITUS.

name: Acoustics
description: The branch of physics that deals with sound and sound waves. In medicine it is often applied in procedures in speech and hearing studies. With regard to the environment, it refers to the characteristics of a room, auditorium, theatre, building, etc. that determines the audibility or fidelity of sounds in it. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

name: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome
description: An acquired defect of cellular immunity associated with infection by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), a CD4-positive T-lymphocyte count under 200 cells/microliter or less than 14% of total lymphocytes, and increased susceptibility to opportunistic infections and malignant neoplasms. Clinical manifestations also include emaciation (wasting) and dementia. These elements reflect criteria for AIDS as defined by the CDC in 1993.

name: Acremonium
description: A mitosporic fungal genus with many reported ascomycetous teleomorphs. Cephalosporin antibiotics are derived from this genus.

name: Acridine Orange
description: A cationic cytochemical stain specific for cell nuclei, especially DNA. It is used as a supravital stain and in fluorescence cytochemistry. It may cause mutations in microorganisms.

name: Acridines
description: Compounds that include the structure of acridine.

name: Acriflavine
description: 3,6-Diamino-10-methylacridinium chloride mixt. with 3,6-acridinediamine. Fluorescent dye used as a local antiseptic and also as a biological stain. It intercalates into nucleic acids thereby inhibiting bacterial and viral replication.

name: Acrocephalosyndactylia
description: Congenital craniostenosis with syndactyly.

name: Acrodermatitis
description: Inflammation involving the skin of the extremities, especially the hands and feet. Several forms are known, some idiopathic and some hereditary. The infantile form is called Gianotti-Crosti syndrome.

name: Acrodynia
description: A condition seen primarily in childhood, most often resulting from chronic exposure to MERCURY COMPOUNDS which may result in encephalopathy and POLYNEUROPATHY. Clinical features include pain, swelling and pinkish discoloration of the fingers and toes, weakness in the extremities, extreme irritability, HYPERESTHESIA, and alterations in level of consciousness. (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p603)

name: Acrolein
description: Unsaturated three-carbon aldehyde.

name: Acromegaly
description: A condition caused by prolonged exposure to excessive HUMAN GROWTH HORMONE in adults. It is characterized by bony enlargement of the FACE; lower jaw (PROGNATHISM); hands; FEET; HEAD; and THORAX. The most common etiology is a GROWTH HORMONE-SECRETING PITUITARY ADENOMA. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1992, Ch36, pp79-80)

name: Acromioclavicular Joint
description: The gliding joint formed by the outer extremity of the CLAVICLE and the inner margin of the ACROMION PROCESS of the SCAPULA.

name: Acromion
description: The lateral extension of the spine of the SCAPULA and the highest point of the SHOULDER.

name: Acronine
description: A pyrano-acridone alkaloid found in RUTACEAE plants.

name: Acrosin
description: A trypsin-like enzyme of spermatozoa which is not inhibited by alpha 1 antitrypsin.

name: Acrosome
description: The cap-like structure covering the anterior portion of SPERM HEAD. Acrosome, derived from LYSOSOMES, is a membrane-bound organelle that contains the required hydrolytic and proteolytic enzymes necessary for sperm penetration of the egg in FERTILIZATION.

name: Acrylamides
description: Colorless, odorless crystals that are used extensively in research laboratories for the preparation of polyacrylamide gels for electrophoresis and in organic synthesis, and polymerization. Some of its polymers are used in sewage and wastewater treatment, permanent press fabrics, and as soil conditioning agents.

name: Acrylates
description: Derivatives of acrylic acid (the structural formula CH2=CHCO2H), including its salts and esters.

name: Acrylic Resins
description: Polymers of high molecular weight which are derived from acrylic acid, methacrylic acid or other related compounds and are capable of being molded and then hardened to form useful components.

name: Acrylonitrile
description: A highly poisonous compound used widely in the manufacture of plastics, adhesives and synthetic rubber.

name: ACTH Syndrome, Ectopic
description: Symptom complex due to ACTH production by non-pituitary neoplasms.

name: Actihaemyl
description: An extract from calf blood containing inorganic salts, amino acids, polypeptides and purines, but no proteins nor antigenic substances or blood group characteristics. Its exact composition is unknown. It has been proposed as a radiation-protective agent.

name: Acting Out
description: Expressing unconscious emotional conflicts or feelings, often of hostility or love, through overt behavior.

name: Actinin
description: A protein factor that regulates the length of R-actin. It is chemically similar, but immunochemically distinguishable from actin.

name: Actinium
description: A trivalent radioactive element and the prototypical member of the actinide family. It has the atomic symbol Ac, and atomic number 89. Its principal isotope is 227 and it decays primarily by beta-emission.

name: Actinobacillosis
description: A disease characterized by suppurative and granulomatous lesions in the respiratory tract, upper alimentary tract, skin, kidneys, joints, and other tissues. Actinobacillus lignieresii infects cattle and sheep while A. equuli infects horses and pigs.

name: Actinobacillus
description: A genus of PASTEURELLACEAE described as gram-negative, nonsporeforming, nonmotile, facultative anaerobes. Most members are found both as pathogens and commensal organisms in the respiratory, alimentary, and genital tracts of animals.

name: Actinobacillus Infections
description: Infections with bacteria of the genus ACTINOBACILLUS.

name: Actinomyces
description: A genus of gram-positive, rod-shaped bacteria whose organisms are nonmotile. Filaments that may be present in certain species are either straight or wavy and may have swollen or clubbed heads.

name: Actinomycetaceae
description: A family of bacteria including numerous parasitic and pathogenic forms.

name: Actinomycetales
description: An order of gram-positive, primarily aerobic BACTERIA that tend to form branching filaments.

name: Actinomycetales Infections
description: Infections with bacteria of the order ACTINOMYCETALES.

name: Actinomycosis
description: Infections with bacteria of the genus ACTINOMYCES.

name: Actinomycosis, Cervicofacial
description: A form of ACTINOMYCOSIS characterized by slow-growing inflammatory lesions of the lymph nodes that drain the mouth (lumpy jaw), reddening of the overlying skin, and intraperitoneal abscesses.

name: Spectinomycin
description: An antibiotic produced by Streptomyces spectabilis. It is active against gram-negative bacteria and used for the treatment of GONORRHEA.

name: Actins
description: Filamentous proteins that are the main constituent of the thin filaments of muscle fibers. The filaments (known also as filamentous or F-actin) can be dissociated into their globular subunits; each subunit is composed of a single polypeptide 375 amino acids long. This is known as globular or G-actin. In conjunction with MYOSINS, actin is responsible for the contraction and relaxation of muscle.

name: Action Potentials
description: Abrupt changes in the membrane potential that sweep along the CELL MEMBRANE of excitable cells in response to excitation stimuli.

name: Activity Cycles
description: Bouts of physical irritability or movement alternating with periods of quiescence. It includes biochemical activity and hormonal activity which may be cellular. These cycles are shorter than 24 hours and include sleep-wakefulness cycles and the periodic activation of the digestive system.

name: Actomyosin
description: A protein complex of actin and MYOSINS occurring in muscle. It is the essential contractile substance of muscle.

name: Acute Disease
description: Disease having a short and relatively severe course.

name: Acute-Phase Proteins
description: Proteins that are secreted into the blood in increased or decreased quantities by hepatocytes in response to trauma, inflammation, or disease. These proteins can serve as inhibitors or mediators of the inflammatory processes. Certain acute-phase proteins have been used to diagnose and follow the course of diseases or as tumor markers.

name: Acute-Phase Reaction
description: An early local inflammatory reaction to insult or injury that consists of fever, an increase in inflammatory humoral factors, and an increased synthesis by hepatocytes of a number of proteins or glycoproteins usually found in the plasma.

name: Acyclovir
description: A GUANOSINE analog that acts as an antimetabolite. Viruses are especially susceptible. Used especially against herpes.

name: Acyl Carrier Protein
description: Consists of a polypeptide chain and 4'-phosphopantetheine linked to a serine residue by a phosphodiester bond. Acyl groups are bound as thiol esters to the pantothenyl group. Acyl carrier protein is involved in every step of fatty acid synthesis by the cytoplasmic system.

name: Acyl Coenzyme A
description: S-Acyl coenzyme A. Fatty acid coenzyme A derivatives that are involved in the biosynthesis and oxidation of fatty acids as well as in ceramide formation.

name: Acylation
description: The addition of an organic acid radical into a molecule.

name: N-Acylneuraminate Cytidylyltransferase
description: An enzyme that forms CMP-acylneuraminic acids, which donate the N-acylneuraminic acid residues to the terminal sugar residue of a ganglioside or glycoprotein. EC 2.7.7.43.

name: Acyltransferases
description: Enzymes from the transferase class that catalyze the transfer of acyl groups from donor to acceptor, forming either esters or amides. (From Enzyme Nomenclature 1992) EC 2.3.

name: Adamantane
description: A tricyclo bridged hydrocarbon.

name: Adams-Stokes Syndrome
description: A condition of fainting spells caused by heart block, often an atrioventricular block, that leads to BRADYCARDIA and drop in CARDIAC OUTPUT. When the cardiac output becomes too low, the patient faints (SYNCOPE). In some cases, the syncope attacks are transient and in others cases repetitive and persistent.

name: Adaptation, Biological
description: Changes in biological features that help an organism cope with its ENVIRONMENT. These changes include physiological (ADAPTATION, PHYSIOLOGICAL), phenotypic and genetic changes.

name: Adaptation, Ocular
description: The adjustment of the eye to variations in the intensity of light. Light adaptation is the adjustment of the eye when the light threshold is increased; DARK ADAPTATION when the light is greatly reduced. (From Cline et al., Dictionary of Visual Science, 4th ed)

name: Adaptation, Physiological
description: The non-genetic biological changes of an organism in response to challenges in its ENVIRONMENT.

name: Adaptation, Psychological
description: A state of harmony between internal needs and external demands and the processes used in achieving this condition. (From APA Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed).

name: Addison Disease
description: An adrenal disease characterized by the progressive destruction of the ADRENAL CORTEX, resulting in insufficient production of ALDOSTERONE and HYDROCORTISONE. Clinical symptoms include ANOREXIA; NAUSEA; WEIGHT LOSS; MUSCLE WEAKNESS; and HYPERPIGMENTATION of the SKIN due to increase in circulating levels of ACTH precursor hormone which stimulates MELANOCYTES.

name: Adenine
description: A purine base and a fundamental unit of ADENINE NUCLEOTIDES.

name: Mitochondrial ADP, ATP Translocases
description: A class of nucleotide translocases found abundantly in mitochondria that function as integral components of the inner mitochondrial membrane. They facilitate the exchange of ADP and ATP between the cytosol and the mitochondria, thereby linking the subcellular compartments of ATP production to those of ATP utilization.

name: Adenine Phosphoribosyltransferase
description: An enzyme catalyzing the formation of AMP from adenine and phosphoribosylpyrophosphate. It can act as a salvage enzyme for recycling of adenine into nucleic acids. EC 2.4.2.7.

name: Dependovirus
description: A genus of the family PARVOVIRIDAE, subfamily PARVOVIRINAE, which are dependent on a coinfection with helper adenoviruses or herpesviruses for their efficient replication. The type species is Adeno-associated virus 2.

name: Adenocarcinoma
description: A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization.

name: Adenocarcinoma, Papillary
description: An adenocarcinoma containing finger-like processes of vascular connective tissue covered by neoplastic epithelium, projecting into cysts or the cavity of glands or follicles. It occurs most frequently in the ovary and thyroid gland. (Stedman, 25th ed)

name: Adenofibroma
description: A benign neoplasm composed of glandular and fibrous tissues, with a relatively large proportion of glands. (Stedman, 25th ed)

name: Adenoids
description: A collection of lymphoid nodules on the posterior wall and roof of the NASOPHARYNX.

name: Adenolymphoma
description: A benign tumor characterized histologically by tall columnar epithelium within a lymphoid tissue stroma. It is usually found in the salivary glands, especially the parotid.

name: Adenoma
description: A benign epithelial tumor with a glandular organization.

name: Adenoma, Basophil
description: A small tumor of the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland whose cells stain with basic dyes. It may give rise to excessive secretion of ACTH, resulting in CUSHING SYNDROME. (Dorland, 27th ed)

name: Adenoma, Chromophobe
description: A benign tumor of the anterior pituitary in which the cells do not stain with acidic or basic dyes.

name: Adenoma, Acidophil
description: A benign tumor, usually found in the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland, whose cells stain with acid dyes. Such pituitary tumors may give rise to excessive secretion of growth hormone, resulting in gigantism or acromegaly. A specific type of acidophil adenoma may give rise to nonpuerperal galactorrhea. (Dorland, 27th ed)

name: Adenosine
description: A nucleoside that is composed of ADENINE and D-RIBOSE. Adenosine or adenosine derivatives play many important biological roles in addition to being components of DNA and RNA. Adenosine itself is a neurotransmitter.

name: Cyclic AMP
description: An adenine nucleotide containing one phosphate group which is esterified to both the 3'- and 5'-positions of the sugar moiety. It is a second messenger and a key intracellular regulator, functioning as a mediator of activity for a number of hormones, including epinephrine, glucagon, and ACTH.

name: Adenosine Deaminase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of ADENOSINE to INOSINE with the elimination of AMMONIA.

name: Adenosine Diphosphate
description: Adenosine 5'-(trihydrogen diphosphate). An adenine nucleotide containing two phosphate groups esterified to the sugar moiety at the 5'-position.

name: Adenosine Diphosphate Glucose
description: Serves as the glycosyl donor for formation of bacterial glycogen, amylose in green algae, and amylopectin in higher plants.

name: Adenosine Diphosphate Ribose
description: An ester formed between the aldehydic carbon of RIBOSE and the terminal phosphate of ADENOSINE DIPHOSPHATE. It is produced by the hydrolysis of nicotinamide-adenine dinucleotide (NAD) by a variety of enzymes, some of which transfer an ADP-ribosyl group to target proteins.

name: Adenosine Diphosphate Sugars
description: Esters formed between the aldehydic carbon of sugars and the terminal phosphate of adenosine diphosphate.

name: Adenosine Kinase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the formation of ADP plus AMP from adenosine plus ATP. It can serve as a salvage mechanism for returning adenosine to nucleic acids. EC 2.7.1.20.

name: Adenosine Monophosphate
description: Adenine nucleotide containing one phosphate group esterified to the sugar moiety in the 2'-, 3'-, or 5'-position.

name: Adenosine Phosphosulfate
description: 5'-Adenylic acid, monoanhydride with sulfuric acid. The initial compound formed by the action of ATP sulfurylase on sulfate ions after sulfate uptake. Synonyms: adenosine sulfatophosphate; APS.

name: Adenosine Triphosphatases
description: A group of enzymes which catalyze the hydrolysis of ATP. The hydrolysis reaction is usually coupled with another function such as transporting Ca(2+) across a membrane. These enzymes may be dependent on Ca(2+), Mg(2+), anions, H+, or DNA.

name: Calcium-Transporting ATPases
description: Cation-transporting proteins that utilize the energy of ATP hydrolysis for the transport of CALCIUM. They differ from CALCIUM CHANNELS which allow calcium to pass through a membrane without the use of energy.

name: Sodium-Potassium-Exchanging ATPase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the active transport system of sodium and potassium ions across the cell wall. Sodium and potassium ions are closely coupled with membrane ATPase which undergoes phosphorylation and dephosphorylation, thereby providing energy for transport of these ions against concentration gradients.

name: Adenosine Triphosphate
description: An adenine nucleotide containing three phosphate groups esterified to the sugar moiety. In addition to its crucial roles in metabolism adenosine triphosphate is a neurotransmitter.

name: Adenoviridae
description: A family of non-enveloped viruses infecting mammals (MASTADENOVIRUS) and birds (AVIADENOVIRUS) or both (ATADENOVIRUS). Infections may be asymptomatic or result in a variety of diseases.

name: Adenoviridae Infections
description: Virus diseases caused by the ADENOVIRIDAE.

name: Adenovirus Infections, Human
description: Respiratory and conjunctival infections caused by 33 identified serotypes of human adenoviruses.

name: Aviadenovirus
description: A genus of ADENOVIRIDAE that infects birds. The type species is FOWL ADENOVIRUS A.

name: Adenoviruses, Human
description: Species of the genus MASTADENOVIRUS, causing a wide range of diseases in humans. Infections are mostly asymptomatic, but can be associated with diseases of the respiratory, ocular, and gastrointestinal systems. Serotypes (named with Arabic numbers) have been grouped into species designated Human adenovirus A-G.

name: Adenoviruses, Simian
description: Species of the genus MASTADENOVIRUS associated with respiratory and enteric infections in primate hosts.

name: Adenylyl Cyclases
description: Enzymes of the lyase class that catalyze the formation of CYCLIC AMP and pyrophosphate from ATP.

name: Adenylate Kinase
description: An enzyme that catalyzes the phosphorylation of AMP to ADP in the presence of ATP or inorganic triphosphate. EC 2.7.4.3.

name: Adenylosuccinate Lyase
description: An enzyme that, in the course of purine ribonucleotide biosynthesis, catalyzes the conversion of 5'-phosphoribosyl-4-(N-succinocarboxamide)-5-aminoimidazole to 5'-phosphoribosyl-4-carboxamide-5-aminoimidazole and the conversion of adenylosuccinic acid to AMP. EC 4.3.2.2.

name: Adenylosuccinate Synthase
description: A carbon-nitrogen ligase. During purine ribonucleotide biosynthesis, this enzyme catalyzes the synthesis of adenylosuccinate from GTP; IMP; and aspartate with the formation of orthophosphate and GDP. EC 6.3.4.4.

name: Adenylyl Imidodiphosphate
description: 5'-Adenylic acid, monoanhydride with imidodiphosphoric acid. An analog of ATP, in which the oxygen atom bridging the beta to the gamma phosphate is replaced by a nitrogen atom. It is a potent competitive inhibitor of soluble and membrane-bound mitochondrial ATPase and also inhibits ATP-dependent reactions of oxidative phosphorylation.

name: Tissue Adhesions
description: Pathological processes consisting of the union of the opposing surfaces of a wound.

name: Adhesiveness
description: A property of the surface of an object that makes it stick to another surface.

name: Adhesives
description: Substances that cause the adherence of two surfaces. They include glues (properly collagen-derived adhesives), mucilages, sticky pastes, gums, resins, or latex.

name: Adie Syndrome
description: A syndrome characterized by a TONIC PUPIL that occurs in combination with decreased lower extremity reflexes. The affected pupil will respond more briskly to accommodation than to light (light-near dissociation) and is supersensitive to dilute pilocarpine eye drops, which induce pupillary constriction. Pathologic features include degeneration of the ciliary ganglion and postganglionic parasympathetic fibers that innervate the pupillary constrictor muscle. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p279)

name: Adipates
description: Derivatives of adipic acid. Included under this heading are a broad variety of acid forms, salts, esters, and amides that contain a 1,6-carboxy terminated aliphatic structure.

name: Adipose Tissue
description: Specialized connective tissue composed of fat cells (ADIPOCYTES). It is the site of stored FATS, usually in the form of TRIGLYCERIDES. In mammals, there are two types of adipose tissue, the WHITE FAT and the BROWN FAT. Their relative distributions vary in different species with most adipose tissue being white.

name: Adiposis Dolorosa
description: A rare disease characterized by multiple tumor-like fatty deposits that press on nerves in various sites causing pain and weakness. Often these lipoma-like structures are located on the trunk and limbs but not on the face and hands.

name: Adjustment Disorders
description: Maladaptive reactions to identifiable psychosocial stressors occurring within a short time after onset of the stressor. They are manifested by either impairment in social or occupational functioning or by symptoms (depression, anxiety, etc.) that are in excess of a normal and expected reaction to the stressor.

name: Adjuvants, Immunologic
description: Substances that augment, stimulate, activate, potentiate, or modulate the immune response at either the cellular or humoral level. The classical agents (Freund's adjuvant, BCG, Corynebacterium parvum, et al.) contain bacterial antigens. Some are endogenous (e.g., histamine, interferon, transfer factor, tuftsin, interleukin-1). Their mode of action is either non-specific, resulting in increased immune responsiveness to a wide variety of antigens, or antigen-specific, i.e., affecting a restricted type of immune response to a narrow group of antigens. The therapeutic efficacy of many biological response modifiers is related to their antigen-specific immunoadjuvanticity.

name: Adjuvants, Pharmaceutic
description: Agents that aid or increase the action of the principle drug (DRUG SYNERGISM) or that affect the absorption, mechanism of action, metabolism, or excretion of the primary drug (PHARMACOKINETICS) in such a way as to enhance its effects.

name: Administrative Personnel
description: Individuals responsible for the development of policy and supervision of the execution of plans and functional operations.

name: Admitting Department, Hospital
description: Hospital department responsible for the flow of patients and the processing of admissions, discharges, transfers, and also most procedures to be carried out in the event of a patient's death.

name: Adnexa Uteri
description: Appendages of the UTERUS which include the FALLOPIAN TUBES, the OVARY, and the supporting ligaments of the uterus (BROAD LIGAMENT; ROUND LIGAMENT).

name: Adnexal Diseases
description: Diseases of the uterine appendages (ADNEXA UTERI) including diseases involving the OVARY, the FALLOPIAN TUBES, and ligaments of the uterus (BROAD LIGAMENT; ROUND LIGAMENT).

name: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease
description: A spectrum of inflammation involving the female upper genital tract and the supporting tissues. It is usually caused by an ascending infection of organisms from the endocervix. Infection may be confined to the uterus (ENDOMETRITIS), the FALLOPIAN TUBES; (SALPINGITIS); the ovaries (OOPHORITIS), the supporting ligaments (PARAMETRITIS), or may involve several of the above uterine appendages. Such inflammation can lead to functional impairment and infertility.

name: Adolescent
description: A person 13 to 18 years of age.

name: Adolescent Behavior
description: Any observable response or action of an adolescent.

name: Adolescent Medicine
description: A branch of medicine pertaining to the diagnosis and treatment of diseases occurring during the period of ADOLESCENCE.

name: Adolescent Psychiatry
description: The medical science that deals with the origin, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of mental disorders in individuals 13-18 years.

name: Psychology, Adolescent
description: Field of psychology involving the study of normal and abnormal behavior of adolescents. It includes mental processes as well as observable responses.

name: Adolescent, Hospitalized
description: Adolescent hospitalized for short term care.

name: Adolescent, Institutionalized
description: An adolescent who is receiving long-term in-patient services or who resides in an institutional setting.

name: Adoption
description: Voluntary acceptance of a child of other parents to be as one's own child, usually with legal confirmation.

name: Adosterol
description: A sterol usually substituted with radioactive iodine. It is an adrenal cortex scanning agent with demonstrated high adrenal concentration and superior adrenal imaging.

name: Adrenal Cortex
description: The outer layer of the adrenal gland. It is derived from MESODERM and comprised of three zones (outer ZONA GLOMERULOSA, middle ZONA FASCICULATA, and inner ZONA RETICULARIS) with each producing various steroids preferentially, such as ALDOSTERONE; HYDROCORTISONE; DEHYDROEPIANDROSTERONE; and ANDROSTENEDIONE. Adrenal cortex function is regulated by pituitary ADRENOCORTICOTROPIN.

name: Adrenal Cortex Diseases
description: Pathological processes of the ADRENAL CORTEX.

name: Adrenal Cortex Hormones
description: HORMONES produced by the ADRENAL CORTEX, including both steroid and peptide hormones. The major hormones produced are HYDROCORTISONE and ALDOSTERONE.

name: Adrenal Cortex Neoplasms
description: Tumors or cancers of the ADRENAL CORTEX.

name: Adrenal Gland Diseases
description: Pathological processes of the ADRENAL GLANDS.

name: Adrenocortical Hyperfunction
description: Excess production of ADRENAL CORTEX HORMONES such as ALDOSTERONE; HYDROCORTISONE; DEHYDROEPIANDROSTERONE; and/or ANDROSTENEDIONE. Hyperadrenal syndromes include CUSHING SYNDROME; HYPERALDOSTERONISM; and VIRILISM.

name: Adrenal Insufficiency
description: Conditions in which the production of adrenal CORTICOSTEROIDS falls below the requirement of the body. Adrenal insufficiency can be caused by defects in the ADRENAL GLANDS, the PITUITARY GLAND, or the HYPOTHALAMUS.

name: Adrenal Gland Neoplasms
description: Tumors or cancer of the ADRENAL GLANDS.

name: Adrenal Glands
description: A pair of glands located at the cranial pole of each of the two KIDNEYS. Each adrenal gland is composed of two distinct endocrine tissues with separate embryonic origins, the ADRENAL CORTEX producing STEROIDS and the ADRENAL MEDULLA producing NEUROTRANSMITTERS.

name: Adrenal Hyperplasia, Congenital
description: A group of inherited disorders of the ADRENAL GLANDS, caused by enzyme defects in the synthesis of cortisol (HYDROCORTISONE) and/or ALDOSTERONE leading to accumulation of precursors for ANDROGENS. Depending on the hormone imbalance, congenital adrenal hyperplasia can be classified as salt-wasting, hypertensive, virilizing, or feminizing. Defects in STEROID 21-HYDROXYLASE; STEROID 11-BETA-HYDROXYLASE; STEROID 17-ALPHA-HYDROXYLASE; 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (3-HYDROXYSTEROID DEHYDROGENASES); TESTOSTERONE 5-ALPHA-REDUCTASE; or steroidogenic acute regulatory protein; among others, underlie these disorders.

name: Adrenal Medulla
description: The inner portion of the adrenal gland. Derived from ECTODERM, adrenal medulla consists mainly of CHROMAFFIN CELLS that produces and stores a number of NEUROTRANSMITTERS, mainly adrenaline (EPINEPHRINE) and NOREPINEPHRINE. The activity of the adrenal medulla is regulated by the SYMPATHETIC NERVOUS SYSTEM.

name: Adrenal Rest Tumor
description: Neoplasm derived from displaced cells (rest cells) of the primordial ADRENAL GLANDS, generally in patients with CONGENITAL ADRENAL HYPERPLASIA. Adrenal rest tumors have been identified in TESTES; LIVER; and other tissues. They are dependent on ADRENOCORTICOTROPIN for growth and adrenal steroid secretion.

name: Adrenergic alpha-Agonists
description: Drugs that selectively bind to and activate alpha adrenergic receptors.

name: Adrenergic alpha-Antagonists
description: Drugs that bind to but do not activate alpha-adrenergic receptors thereby blocking the actions of endogenous or exogenous adrenergic agonists. Adrenergic alpha-antagonists are used in the treatment of hypertension, vasospasm, peripheral vascular disease, shock, and pheochromocytoma.

name: Adrenergic beta-Agonists
description: Drugs that selectively bind to and activate beta-adrenergic receptors.

name: Adrenergic beta-Antagonists
description: Drugs that bind to but do not activate beta-adrenergic receptors thereby blocking the actions of beta-adrenergic agonists. Adrenergic beta-antagonists are used for treatment of hypertension, cardiac arrhythmias, angina pectoris, glaucoma, migraine headaches, and anxiety.

name: Adrenergic Fibers
description: Nerve fibers liberating catecholamines at a synapse after an impulse.

name: Adrenergic Agonists
description: Drugs that bind to and activate adrenergic receptors.

name: Adrenochrome
description: Pigment obtained by the oxidation of epinephrine.

name: Adrenocorticotropic Hormone
description: An anterior pituitary hormone that stimulates the ADRENAL CORTEX and its production of CORTICOSTEROIDS. ACTH is a 39-amino acid polypeptide of which the N-terminal 24-amino acid segment is identical in all species and contains the adrenocorticotrophic activity. Upon further tissue-specific processing, ACTH can yield ALPHA-MSH and corticotrophin-like intermediate lobe peptide (CLIP).

name: Adrenodoxin
description: An iron-sulfur protein which serves as an electron carrier in enzymatic steroid hydroxylation reactions in adrenal cortex mitochondria. The electron transport system which catalyzes this reaction consists of adrenodoxin reductase, NADP, adrenodoxin, and cytochrome P-450.

name: Adrenoleukodystrophy
description: An X-linked recessive disorder characterized by the accumulation of saturated very long chain fatty acids in the LYSOSOMES of ADRENAL CORTEX and the white matter of CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. This disease occurs almost exclusively in the males. Clinical features include the childhood onset of ATAXIA; NEUROBEHAVIORAL MANIFESTATIONS; HYPERPIGMENTATION; ADRENAL INSUFFICIENCY; SEIZURES; MUSCLE SPASTICITY; and DEMENTIA. The slowly progressive adult form is called adrenomyeloneuropathy. The defective gene ABCD1 is located at Xq28, and encodes the adrenoleukodystrophy protein (ATP-BINDING CASSETTE TRANSPORTERS).

name: Adsorption
description: The adhesion of gases, liquids, or dissolved solids onto a surface. It includes adsorptive phenomena of bacteria and viruses onto surfaces as well. ABSORPTION into the substance may follow but not necessarily.

name: Adult
description: A person having attained full growth or maturity. Adults are of 19 through 44 years of age. For a person between 19 and 24 years of age, YOUNG ADULT is available.

name: Advertising
description: Works about the act or practice of calling public attention to a product, service, need, etc., especially by paid announcements in newspapers, magazines, on radio, or on television. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

name: Aedes
description: A genus of mosquitoes (CULICIDAE) frequently found in tropical and subtropical regions. YELLOW FEVER and DENGUE are two of the diseases that can be transmitted by species of this genus.

name: Aequorin
description: A photoprotein isolated from the bioluminescent jellyfish Aequorea. It emits visible light by an intramolecular reaction when a trace amount of calcium ion is added.
