description: A plant genus of the family CELASTRACEAE that contains insecticidal sesquiterpenoids and celastrus oil.

name: Salsola
description: A plant genus of the family CHENOPODIACEAE. The extract may be called lochein. Tumbleweed may occasionally refer to AMARANTHUS.

name: Erdheim-Chester Disease
description: A rare form of non-Langerhans-cell histiocytosis (HISTIOCYTOSIS, NON-LANGERHANS-CELL) with onset in middle age. The systemic disease is characterized by infiltration of lipid-laden macrophages, multinucleated giant cells, an inflammatory infiltrate of lymphocytes and histiocytes in the bone marrow, and a generalized sclerosis of the long bones.

name: Clethraceae
description: A plant family of the order Ericales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida.

name: Clusia
description: A plant genus of the family CLUSIACEAE. Members contain benzophenones.

name: Mammea
description: A plant genus of the family CLUSIACEAE. Members contain xanthones and BENZOPHENONES. The common name of Mamey is also used with POUTERIA.

name: Calystegia
description: A plant genus of the family CONVOLVULACEAE. Members contain calystegine and calystegins.

name: Convolvulus
description: A plant genus of the family CONVOLVULACEAE. The common name of morning glory also refers to IPOMOEA. The common name of bindweed also refers to IPOMOEA; CALYSTEGIA; or POLYGONUM.

name: Carex Plant
description: A plant genus of the family CYPERACEAE. The seed contains oligostilbenes (STILBENES).

name: Eleocharis
description: A plant genus of the family CYPERACEAE. Corm of Eleocharis species (e.g., Eleocharis dulcis) is edible and commonly referred to as water chestnut which sometimes also referred to fruits of unrelated plant genus TRAPA (e.g., invasive aquatic plant TRAPA NATANS).

name: Droseraceae
description: A plant family of the order Nepenthales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida, notable for leaves with sticky gland-tipped hairs that entrap insects.

name: Poult Enteritis Mortality Syndrome
description: An acute, transmissible, infectious disease associated with high MORTALITY and MORBIDITY in young turkeys (poults). It is characterized by DIARRHEA; ANOREXIA; growth depression, and immune dysfunction. The cause is unknown but astroviruses (AVASTROVIRUS) and coronaviruses (CORONAVIRUS, TURKEY) have been isolated from diseased poults and are thought to cause the enteritis and increased susceptibility to bacterial infections.

name: Ebenaceae
description: A small plant family of the order Ebenales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida. Members contain NAPHTHOQUINONES.

name: Elaeagnaceae
description: A plant family of the order Rhamnales, subclass Rosidae class Magnoliopsida. The plants have a characteristic silvery or rusty-colored sheen, caused by tiny distinctive scales. Flowers have a tubular structure of four sepals. Root nodules host the Frankia (ACTINOMYCETES) nitrogen-fixing symbionts.

name: Hippophae
description: A plant genus of the family ELAEAGNACEAE. Linoleic (18:2n-6) and alpha-linolenic acids (18:3n-3) comprised about 70% of seed oil fatty acids. This is unrelated to 'artificial sea buckthorn oil'. This genus does not belong to the buckthorn family (RHAMNACEAE).

name: Gaultheria
description: A plant genus of the family ERICACEAE. The common name of wintergreen is also used for PYROLA and snowberry is also used for SYMPHORICARPOS.

name: Eucommiaceae
description: A plant family of the order Eucommiales, subclass Hamamelidae, class Magnoliopsida (some botanists have classified this in the order Hamamelidales or Urticales). Eucomia is an elmlike tree of central and eastern China. Leaves are alternate; deciduous flowers are solitary and unisexual and lack petals and sepals. The male flowers have 6 to 10 stamens and female flowers have one ovary of two carpels, one of which aborts during development so the fruit (a dry, winged structure) contains only one seed. The latex is a source of RUBBER. Tochu tea is an aqueous extract of Eucommia ulmoides leaves and a popular beverage in Japan. (Mutat Res 1997 Jan 15;388(1):7-20).

name: Aleurites
description: A plant genus of the family EUPHORBIACEAE that is the source of tung oil and a phorbol diester (PHORBOL ESTERS).

name: Hippomane
description: A plant genus of the family EUPHORBIACEAE. The trees contain hippomanin A and the latex is a skin irritant.

name: Jatropha
description: A plant genus of the family EUPHORBIACEAE. Members contain jatrophone and other diterpenes.

name: Sapium
description: A plant genus of the family EUPHORBIACEAE that contains bukittinggine and PHORBOL ESTERS.

name: Chamaecrista
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE. Some species were reclassified from CASSIA and Senna.

name: Albizzia
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that contains julibroside (triterpenoid saponins).

name: Butea
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that contains butrin and isobutrin.

name: Castanospermum
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that contains castanospermines, swainsonine, and triterpenoid saponins.

name: Clitoria
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that contains ternatins (anthocyanins) and preternatins, antifungal proteins, stigmast-4-ene-3,6-dione, and clitoriacetal (ROTENONE).

name: Cyamopsis
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that is the source of guar gum.

name: Dolichos
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that contains LECTINS. Many members have been reclassified into other genera of the FABACEAE family.

name: Griffonia
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE. Members contain Griffonia simplicifolia agglutin-I and griffonin.

name: Laburnum
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE named after the drooping clusters of flowers.

name: Lupinus
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that is a source of SPARTEINE, lupanine and other lupin alkaloids.

name: Mimosa
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that contains kukulkanin, a CHALCONE.

name: Mucuna
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that is the source of mucuna gum.

name: Retinal Vasculitis
description: Inflammation of the retinal vasculature with various causes including infectious disease; LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS, SYSTEMIC; MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS; BEHCET SYNDROME; and CHORIORETINITIS.

name: Robinia
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that contains linarin (acaciin) and LECTINS.

name: Spartium
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that is a source of SPARTEINE. Do not confuse with Broom or Scotch Broom (CYTISUS) or Butcher's Broom (RUSCUS) or Desert Broom (BACCHARIS) or Brome (BROMUS).

name: Sphenostylis
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that contains LECTINS and raffinose oligosaccharides.

name: Tephrosia
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that contains tephrorin, tephrosone, and C-prenylflavonoids.

name: Tetrapleura
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE. Members contain molluscicidal triterpene glycosides (TRITERPENES).

name: Vicia
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that is widely used as ground cover and forage and known for the edible beans, VICIA FABA.

name: Vicia faba
description: A plant species of the genus VICIA, family FABACEAE. The edible beans are well known but they cause FAVISM in some individuals with GLUCOSEPHOSPHATE DEHYDROGENASE DEFICIENCY. This plant contains vicine, convicine, Vicia lectins, unknown seed protein, AAP2 transport protein, and Vicia faba DNA-binding protein 1.

name: Salicaceae
description: A plant family of the order MALPIGHIALES, superorder ROSANAE, class MAGNOLIOPSIDA. The leaves are alternate and simple, and staminate (male) flowers consist of one to several stamens; pistillate (female) flowers consist of a single-chambered ovary with several ovules that produce silky seeds.

name: Ryania
description: A plant genus of the family Salicaceae that is the source of RYANODINE.

name: Fumarioideae
description: The fumitory, or bleeding-heart plant family of the order Papaverales, subclass Magnoliidae, class Magnoliopsida. Flowers are bisexual, with two small sepals and four petals, one pistil and six stamens.

name: Corydalis
description: A plant genus of the family FUMARIOIDEAE (classified by some in PAPAVERACEAE) that contains isoquinoline alkaloids.

name: Fumaria
description: A plant genus of the family FUMARIOIDEAE that contains fumariline and other isoquinoline alkaloids.

name: Gentianella
description: A plant genus of the family GENTIANACEAE that contains nitiol (a C25 sesterterpenoid) & nitidasin.

name: Geraniaceae
description: A plant family of the order Geraniales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida.

name: Geranium
description: A plant genus of the family GERANIACEAE. Geranium is also used as a common name for PELARGONIUM.

name: Pelargonium
description: A plant genus of the family GERANIACEAE. The common name of geranium is also used for the GERANIUM genus.

name: Liquidambar
description: A plant genus of the family HAMAMELIDACEAE. The sap is a source of storax, which should not be confused with the similar named STYRAX genus.

name: Hippocastanaceae
description: A plant family of the order Sapindales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida.

name: Aesculus
description: A plant genus of the family HIPPOCASTANACEAE (or SAPINDACEAE by some) that contains antimicrobial protein 1 and escin. A. hippocastanum is used in folk medicine for treating chronic venous insufficiency.

name: Hippocrateaceae
description: A plant family of the order Celastrales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. The Hippocratea genus contains friedelanes, triterpenoid quinone, and hippocrateine I.

name: Hydrocharitaceae
description: A plant family of the order Hydrocharitales, subclass ALISMATIDAE, class Liliopsida (monocotyledons).

name: Eriodictyon
description: A plant genus of the family HYDROPHYLLACEAE that has a characteristic strong smell.

name: Iris Plant
description: A plant genus of the family IRIDACEAE that contains IRIP, a type-1 ribosome-inactivating protein, and iridals (TRITERPENES).

name: Juglans
description: A plant genus of the family JUGLANDACEAE that provides the familiar walnut.

name: Carya
description: A plant genus of the family JUGLANDACEAE that bears edible nuts.

name: Krameriaceae
description: A plant family of the order Polygalales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida.

name: Agastache
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that contains tilianin, agastanol, and agastaquinone (a cytotoxic diterpenoid quinone).

name: Ajuga
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that contains cyasterone, ajugasterone, 20-hydroxyecdysone, 8-acetylharpagide (an iridoid glycoside).

name: Ballota
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that contains phenylpropanoids.

name: Coleus
description: A plant genus of the family Lamiaceae. The species of Coleus should be distinguished from PLECTRANTHUS BARBATUS - which is also known as Coleus forskohlii.

name: Hyptis
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that contains 5-methoxydehydropodophyllotoxin (a PODOPHYLLOTOXIN) and other LIGNANS.

name: Leonurus
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that contains leonurine.

name: Lycopus
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that contains rosmarinic acid and isopimarane diterpenoids and has been used in folk medicine for HYPERTHYROIDISM.

name: Melissa
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE. The common names of beebalm or lemonbalm are also used for MONARDA.

name: Mentha pulegium
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that contains pulegone. Do not confuse with 'American false pennyroyal' (HEDEOMA).

name: Hedeoma
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that is closely related to the European pennyroyal (MENTHA PULEGIUM).

name: Mentha spicata
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE having characteristic flavor.

name: Monarda
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE. The common names of beebalm or lemonbalm are also used for MELISSA. The common name of bergamot is also used for Citrus bergamia (CITRUS).

name: Ocimum
description: A plant genus of the family Lamiaceae which occurs in tropical and warm temperate regions worldwide. It includes the aromatic herb OCIMUM BASILICUM (Sweet Basil) and the MEDICINAL PLANT Ocimum tenuiflorum (Holy Basil).

name: Origanum
description: A plant genus of the family Lamiaceae that is the source of familiar seasonings, oregano and marjoram.

name: Orthosiphon
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that contains pimarane-type diterpenes. Several species of Orthosiphon are also called Java tea.

name: Perilla
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that is a source of perilla alcohol and the oil is rich in alpha-linolenic acid (alpha-18:3).

name: Perilla frutescens
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that is an ingredient of Banxia Houpu (DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL).

name: Phlomis
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that contains phlorigidosides, iridoid glucosides and megastigmane glycosides.

name: Plectranthus
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that contains eudesmane sesquiterpenes and antimicrobial abietane diterpenoids.

name: Prunella
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE. Members contain TRITERPENES. Heal all is another common name.

name: Satureja
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE used to flavor food.

name: Scutellaria
description: A plant genus of the family Lamiaceae used in folk medicine.

name: Scutellaria baicalensis
description: A plant species of the genus Scutellaria, family LAMIACEAE, that contains skullcap flavone and is used in CHINESE HERBAL DRUGS.

name: Sideritis
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that contains isoscutellarein-7-O-(allosyl(1-2)glucoside).

name: Stachys
description: A plant genus of the family LAMIACEAE that has a characteristic odor.

name: Teucrium
description: A plant genus of the family Lamiaceae. Members contain teuscordonin. There have been reports of hepatotoxicity by this genus.

name: Zoster Sine Herpete
description: HERPES ZOSTER but without eruption of vesicles. Patients exhibit the characteristic pain minus the skin rash, sometimes making diagnosis difficult.

name: Cryptocarya
description: A plant genus of the family LAURACEAE. Members contain cryptofolione, caryachine, grandisin and other compounds. Some PEUMUS species have been reclassified as CRYPTOCARYA.

name: Lecythidaceae
description: A plant family of the order Lecythidales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida.

name: Barringtonia
description: A plant genus of the family Lecythidaceae. Members contain nasimalun A and B (neo-clerodane diterpenoids).

name: Bertholletia
description: A plant genus of the family Lecythidaceae which is the source of edible Brazil nuts.

name: Polygonatum
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae. Members contain benzoquinones, steroidal saponin, and ribosome-inactivating proteins.

name: Maianthemum
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae. The cluster of flowers at the end of the stalk distinguishes this plant from true Solomon's seal (POLYGONATUM), which has flowers that grow along the stem.

name: Alstroemeria
description: A plant genus of the family Alstroemeriaceae. Members contain allergens, tuliposide A and tulipalin A.

name: Anemarrhena
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae. Members contain anemarans (POLYSACCHARIDES), hinokiresinol, mangiferin (a xanthone), and timosaponin (a steroidal saponin).

name: Camassia
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae that contains steroidal SAPONINS and should not be confused with death camas (ZIGADENUS).

name: Convallaria
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae that contains CARDIAC GLYCOSIDES.

name: Cordyline
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae that contains spirostanol & furostanol SAPONINS.

name: Crinum
description: A plant genus of the family Amaryllidaceae that contains ALKALOIDS.

name: Curculigo
description: A plant genus of the family Hypoxidaceae that contains curculin and cycloartane saponins.

name: Dracaena
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae. The common name of dragon's blood is also used for CROTON and Daemonorops (ARECACEAE).

name: Fritillaria
description: A plant genus of the family LILIACEAE. Members of this genus produce imperialine, a steroidal alkaloid which acts at muscarinic receptors.

name: Hemerocallis
description: A plant genus of the family ASPHODELACEAE. Members contain steroidal saponins.

name: Hosta
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae. Members contain steroidal saponins.

name: Hyacinthus
description: A plant genus of the family Hyacinthaceae (Asparagaceae). Do not confuse with water hyacinth (EICHHORNIA).

name: Liriope Plant
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae. Members contain ruscogenin. Do not confuse with the Liriope jellyfish (CNIDARIA).

name: Plasmodesmata
description: Membrane-like channels of cytoplasm connecting adjacent plant cells. Plasmodesmata connect through pores in the CELL WALL and associate with the CYTOSKELETON machinery. They are essential for intercellular transport and communication.

name: Lycoris
description: A plant genus of the family Amaryllidaceae. Members contain radiatine, vittatine, haemanthamine, lycorenine, dihydrolycorine, lycorine, lycoricidinol and lycoricidine.

name: Narcissus
description: A plant genus of the family Amaryllidaceae. Members contain ungiminorine and LECTINS.

name: Ophiopogon
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae. Members contain steroidal glycosides and provide an ingredient of shengmaisan (DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL).

name: Ornithogalum
description: A plant genus of the family LILIACEAE that contains cholestane glycosides (CHOLESTANES).

name: Ruscus
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae. This should not be confused with Broom or Scotch Broom (CYTISUS) or Desert Broom (BACCHARIS) or Spanish Broom (SPARTIUM) or Brome (BROMUS).

name: Sansevieria
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae that contains steroidal SAPONINS.

name: Scilla
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae. Members contain the cardiotonic PROSCILLARIDIN. The common name of squill is also used for DRIMIA.

name: Trillium
description: A plant genus of the family Melanthiaceae that is a short plant with a distinct whorl of 3 broad leaves.

name: Tulipa
description: A plant genus of the family LILIACEAE. Members contain tuliposides and tulipalins and have been associated with allergic contact dermatitis in florists.

name: Drimia
description: A plant genus of the family Asparagaceae that contains bufadienolides (BUFANOLIDES). The common name of squill is also used for SCILLA.

name: Zigadenus
description: A plant genus of the family Melanthiaceae that is fatally toxic to grazing animals. The name is similar to another plant genus CAMASSIA.

name: Gelsemium
description: A plant genus of the family LOGANIACEAE (classified by some botanists as Gelsemiaceae). The sometimes used common name of trumpet flower is also used for DATURA.

name: Strychnos
description: A plant genus of the family LOGANIACEAE (classified by some botanists as Strychnaceae).

name: Strychnos nux-vomica
description: A plant genus of the genus STRYCHNOS, family LOGANIACEAE that is the source of STRYCHNINE.

name: Cynomorium
description: A plant genus of the family BALANOPHORACEAE. Members contain stigmastanes and ursanes (TRITERPENES) and lignan glucopyranosides (LIGNANS).

name: Capparaceae
description: A plant family of the order Capparales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida, that are mostly herbs and shrubs growing in warm arid regions. Several produce GLUCOSINOLATES.

name: Capparis
description: A plant genus of the family CAPPARACEAE that contains mabinlin, a sweet protein.

name: Cleome
description: A plant genus of the family CAPPARACEAE that contains cleogynol and 15alpha-acetoxycleomblynol (dammaranes) and 1-epibrachyacarpone (a triterpene), and ISOTHIOCYANATES.

name: Gleditsia
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE that contains gleditsiosides (triterpenoid SAPONINS).

name: Lythrum
description: A plant genus of the family LYTHRACEAE that contains ALKALOIDS. Common name loosestrife refers to members Lythrum (purple loosestrife) and LYSIMACHIA (e.g., yellow loosestrife).

name: Cuphea
description: A plant genus of the family LYTHRACEAE. Members contain lauric acid and cuphiin.

name: Lagerstroemia
description: A plant genus of the family LYTHRACEAE. Members contain lagertannin and have hypoglycemic effects.

name: Lawsonia Plant
description: A plant genus of the family LYTHRACEAE that is the source of henna and has cytotoxic activity.

name: Woodfordia
description: A plant genus of the family LYTHRACEAE. Members contain woodfordins.

name: Magnolia
description: A plant genus of the family MAGNOLIACEAE. The germacranolide sesquiterpene lactones costunolide, parthenolide, and costunolide diepoxide have been isolated from the leaves. Bark contains honokiol and magnolol. Parts are an ingredient of Banxia Houpo Tang.

name: Liriodendron
description: A plant genus of the family MAGNOLIACEAE. Members include hardwood trees of eastern North America with distinct large tuliplike flowers.

name: Banisteriopsis
description: A plant genus of the family MALPIGHIACEAE which includes an Amazonian psychoactive plant that contains the beta-carboline harmine and N,N-dimethyltryptamine.

name: Galphimia
description: A plant genus of the family MALPIGHIACEAE. G. glauca is the source of 'Galphimia glauca extract' and contains 'galphimine B' and tetragalloylquinic acid.

name: Althaea
description: A plant genus of the family MALVACEAE known for mucilaginous roots. The common names of hollyhock and mallow are also used for other genera of MALVACEAE.

name: Hibiscus
description: A plant genus of the family MALVACEAE. Members contain CITRIC ACID; MALATES; ANTHOCYANINS; FLAVONOIDS; GLYCOSIDES; DIETARY FIBER; and LIGNANS. Hibiscus sabdariffa is common constituent of HERBAL TEAS. Hibiscus cannabinus is a source of hemp fiber for TEXTILES.

name: Melia
description: A plant genus of the family MELIACEAE. Members contain meliavolkinin, melianin C and limonoids.

name: Melia azedarach
description: A plant species of the genus MELIA, family MELIACEAE, which is toxic to insects. The name is very similar to Melia azadirachta (AZADIRACHTA).

name: Cedrela
description: A plant genus of the family MELIACEAE. Members contain cedrelanolide.

name: Azadirachta
description: A plant genus of the family MELIACEAE. Members contain azadirachtin A (a limonoid commonly referred to as azadirachtin) and other TRITERPENES. They have been used in PESTICIDES. The old name of Melia azadirachta is very similar to a related plant, MELIA AZEDARACH.

name: Aglaia
description: A plant genus of the family MELIACEAE. Members contain lariciresinol, pregnanes, insecticidal rocaglamide derivatives and other compounds.

name: Menispermum
description: A plant genus of the family MENISPERMACEAE. Members contain dauricine and other ALKALOIDS.

name: Cyclea
description: A plant genus of the family MENISPERMACEAE. Members contain bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloids.

name: Cocculus
description: A plant genus of the family MENISPERMACEAE. Members contain sinococuline, coccuvine and other ALKALOIDS.

name: Cissampelos
description: A plant genus of the family MENISPERMACEAE. Members contain eletefine (a stephaoxocane alkaloid) and tropoloisoquinoline and protoberberine ALKALOIDS.

name: Stephania
description: A plant genus of the family MENISPERMACEAE. Members contain cycleanine.

name: Area Postrema
description: A small, rounded eminence on each side of the FOURTH VENTRICLE, which receives nerve fibers from the SOLITARY NUCLEUS; SPINAL CORD; and adjacent areas of the MEDULLA OBLONGATA. The area postrema lies outside the BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER and its functions include acting as an emetic chemoreceptor.

name: Stephania tetrandra
description: A plant species of the genus STEPHANIA, family MENISPERMACEAE, that contains tetrandrine and bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloids.

name: Tinospora
description: A plant genus of the family MENISPERMACEAE. Members have been used in AYURVEDIC MEDICINE. Hypoglycemic effect has been reported.

name: Peumus
description: A plant genus of the family MONIMIACEAE. Members contain boldine ALKALOIDS. Some PEUMUS species have been reclassified as CRYPTOCARYA.

name: Antiaris
description: A plant genus of the family MORACEAE. Members have been used as an arrow poison.

name: Artocarpus
description: A plant genus of the family MORACEAE. Puag-haad extract, from A. lakoocha, contains STILBENES and related 4-substituted RESORCINOLS.

name: Broussonetia
description: A plant genus of the family MORACEAE. Members contain PYRROLIDINES.

name: Maclura
description: A plant genus of the family MORACEAE. Members contain maclurin, antifungal chalcones, and other compounds.

name: Morus
description: A plant genus of the family MORACEAE that is widely planted for shade.

name: Myrica
description: A plant genus of the family MYRICACEAE. Members contain myricanol. The common name of bayberry is similar to the name barberry which is used for BERBERIS and MAHONIA.

name: Myoporaceae
description: A plant family of the order Scrophulariales, subclass Asteridae, class Magnoliopsida.

name: Myoporum
description: A plant genus of the family MYOPORACEAE. Members contain dehydrongaione, deisopropylngaione, dehydromyodesmone and other furanoid sesquiterpene essential oils. It is the source of Ngaio oil and ngaione.

name: Ardisia
description: A plant genus of the family MYRSINACEAE. Members contain ardisiacrispins (oleanane triterpenoid saponins), ardicrenin, and cyclamiretin.

name: Embelia
description: A plant genus of the family MYRSINACEAE. Members contain embelin.

name: Feijoa
description: A plant genus of the family MYRTACEAE that is cultivated for the edible fruit, which is different from the ordinary guava (PSIDIUM).

name: Psidium
description: A plant genus of the family MYRTACEAE that bears an edible fruit and contains guavin B and quercetin glycosides.

name: Kunzea
description: A plant genus of the family MYRTACEAE. The common name of tea tree more often refers to MELALEUCA or LEPTOSPERMUM.

name: Leptospermum
description: A plant genus of the family MYRTACEAE. The common name of tea tree is also used for MELALEUCA and KUNZEA.

name: Melaleuca
description: A plant genus of the family MYRTACEAE. M. alternifolia foliage is a source of TEA TREE OIL. The common name of tea tree also refers to LEPTOSPERMUM or KUNZEA. M. vindifolia is a source of niaouli oil. M. cajuputi and M. leucadendra are sources of cajuput oil.

name: Myrtus
description: A plant genus of the family MYRTACEAE. Members contain PHYTOHEMAGGLUTININS.

name: Nelumbonaceae
description: A plant family of the order Nymphaeales, subclass Magnoliidae, class Magnoliopsida. They are aquatic plants.

name: Nelumbo
description: A plant genus of the family NELUMBONACEAE. The common name lotus is also used for other plants such as the WATER-LILY, which they resemble, and the unrelated genus Lotus (LOTUS). Nelumbo produce the edible lotus nuts.

name: Nuphar
description: A plant genus of the family NYMPHAEACEAE. Members contain sesquiterpene thioalkaloids.

name: Nyssa
description: A plant genus of the family Nyssaceae. Named for the water nymph from classical mythology, these species grow in moist habitats and are tolerant of flooding.

name: Olacaceae
description: A small plant family of the order Santalales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida.

name: Forsythia
description: A plant genus of the family OLEACEAE. Members contain suspensaside.

name: Olea
description: A plant genus of the family Oleaceae. The olive fruit is the source of OLIVE OIL.

name: Ligustrum
description: A plant genus of the family OLEACEAE. Oleuropein, a phenolic secoiridoid glycoside, is found in the leaves.

name: Jasminum
description: A plant genus of the family OLEACEAE. Members contain secoiridoid glucosides and this is the source of oil of jasmine.

name: Fraxinus
description: A plant genus of the family OLEACEAE. Members contain secoiridoid glucosides.

name: Syringa
description: A plant genus of the family OLEACEAE. Oleuropein has been identified in the stem bark.

name: Clarkia
description: A plant genus, of the family ONAGRACEAE, which is the subject of genetic studies. The floral aroma is attributed to benzenoid esters and benzyl acetate.

name: Oenothera
description: A plant genus of the family ONAGRACEAE. Members contain oenotheins.

name: Oenothera biennis
description: A plant species, of the genus OENOTHERA, family ONAGRACEAE, that is the source of evening primrose oil.

name: Epilobium
description: A plant genus of the family ONAGRACEAE. The common name of fireweed is also used with other plants.

name: Dendrobium
description: A plant genus of the family ORCHIDACEAE that contains dihydroayapin (COUMARINS) and phenanthraquinones.

name: Gastrodia
description: A plant genus of the family ORCHIDACEAE which depends on the fungus Armillaria mellea to complete its life cycle. It is an ingredient of Zhenxuanyin (DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL).

name: Vanilla
description: A plant genus of the family ORCHIDACEAE that is the source of the familiar flavoring used in foods and medicines (FLAVORING AGENTS).

name: Orobanchaceae
description: The broom-rape plant family of the order Lamiales.

name: Cistanche
description: A plant genus of the family OROBANCHACEAE. Members contain phenylethanoid glycosides.

name: Orobanche
description: A plant genus of the family OROBANCHACEAE. Lacking chlorophyll, they are nonphotosynthetic parasitic plants. The common name is similar to Broom or Scotch Broom (CYTISUS) or Butcher's Broom (RUSCUS) or Desert Broom (BACCHARIS) or Spanish Broom (SPARTIUM) or Brome (BROMUS).

name: Pandanaceae
description: A plant family of the order Pandanales, subclass Arecidae, class Liliopsida (monocotyledons).

name: Argemone
description: A plant genus of the family PAPAVERACEAE that contains isoquinoline alkaloids.

name: Eschscholzia
description: A plant genus of the family PAPAVERACEAE that contains benzo[c]phenanthridine alkaloids.

name: Sanguinaria
description: A plant genus of the family PAPAVERACEAE, a species of which is the source of sanguinarine extract used in MOUTHWASHES.

name: Passifloraceae
description: A plant family of the order Violales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida that are herbaceous or woody vines, shrubs, and trees, mostly of warm regions. Many have tendrils in leaf axils. Leaves are alternate. Flowers have 3-5 sepals, petals and stamens. Nearly all species have seeds that bear a fleshy appendage called an aril.

name: Harpagophytum
description: A plant genus of the family PEDALIACEAE. Members contain harpagoside.

name: Sesamum
description: A plant genus of the family PEDALIACEAE that is the source of the edible seed and SESAME OIL.

name: Tagetes
description: A plant genus of the family ASTERACEAE. The common name of marigold is also used for CALENDULA.

name: Piper
description: A plant genus of the family PIPERACEAE that includes species used for spicy and stimulating qualities.

name: Agropyron
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The common name of wheatgrass is also used for other plants in the family.

name: Agrostis
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE.

name: Piper betle
description: A plant genus of the family PIPERACEAE that is indigenous in the Indian Malay region and cultivated in Madagascar, and the West Indies. It contains chavibetol, chavicol and cadinene. The leaf is chewed as a stimulant, antiseptic and sialogogue. The common name of betel is also used for ARECA.

name: Andropogon
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The common name of bluestem is also used for other plants in this family. Andropogon nardus has been reclassified as CYMBOPOGON nardus and Andropogon zizanioides as Chrysopogon zizanioides.

name: Bambusa
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. Young shoots are eaten in Asian foods while the stiff mature stems are used for construction of many things. The common name of bamboo is also used for other genera of Poaceae including Phyllostachys, SASA, and Dendrocalamus.

name: Bromus
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The name is similar to Broom or Scotch Broom (CYTISUS) or Butcher's Broom (RUSCUS) or Desert Broom (BACCHARIS) or Spanish Broom (SPARTIUM).

name: Cenchrus
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The common name of buffelgrass is also used for PENNISETUM.

name: Coix
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The seed is used in folk medicine (DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL).

name: Cymbopogon
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE which is a source of citronella oil and lemongrass oil.

name: Cynodon
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that is considered a lawn grass by some and a weed by others. It contains allergen Cyn d 7.

name: Dactylis
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that contains allergen Dac g I.

name: Digitaria
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that many people consider to be a weed.

name: Echinochloa
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that is grown mainly as a hay crop.

name: Eleusine
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. Finger millet or raggee (E. coracana) is an important food grain in southern Asia and parts of Africa.

name: Elymus
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The common name of wild rye is used with some other grasses.

name: Eragrostis
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE.

name: Festuca
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The common name of fescue is also used with some other grasses.

name: Holcus
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that contains Hol l 1 and Hol l 5 allergens.

name: Paspalum
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that is used for forage.

name: Pennisetum
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The seed is one of the millets used in EDIBLE GRAIN. It contains vitexin. The common name of buffelgrass is also used for CENCHRUS.

name: Phalaris
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE.

name: Phleum
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that contains the Phl p 4 allergen.

name: Poa
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE that contains the Poa p Ia allergen and allergen C KBGP.

name: Saccharum
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE widely cultivated in the tropics for the sweet cane that is processed into sugar.

name: Sasa
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. Folin is the water-soluble extract from Sasa albomarginata. Sasa kurinensis is an ingredient of Sho-ju-sen, a Japanese herbal medicine.

name: Polygala
description: A plant genus of the family POLYGALACEAE that contains onjisaponins, xanthones, pyrones, and benzophenones. The name is similar to other snakeroots such as ASARUM; SANICULA; ARISTOLOCHIA; AGERATINA; and others.

name: Securidaca
description: A plant genus of the family POLYGALACEAE that contains securiosides and indole alkaloids.

name: Eriogonum
description: A plant genus of the family POLYGONACEAE.

name: Rumex
description: A plant genus of the family POLYGONACEAE that contains patientosides and other naphthalene glycosides.

name: Pontederiaceae
description: A plant family of the order Liliales, subclass Liliidae, class Liliopsida (monocotyledons). Most species are perennials, native primarily to tropical America. They have creeping rootstocks, fibrous roots, and leaves in clusters at the base of the plant or borne on branched stems. The fruit is a capsule containing many seeds, or a one-seeded winged structure.

name: Eichhornia
description: A plant genus of the family PONTEDERIACEAE that is used as a biological filter for treating wastewater.

name: Potamogetonaceae
description: A plant family of the order Najadales, subclass Alismatidae, class Liliopsida (monocotyledons).

name: Portulaca
description: A plant genus of the family PORTULACACEAE.

name: Anagallis
description: A plant genus of the family PRIMULACEAE that contains anagallosides, which are molluscacidal triterpenoid saponins.

name: Cyclamen
description: A plant genus of the family PRIMULACEAE that contains triterpenoid saponins.

name: Primula
description: A plant genus of the family PRIMULACEAE. It can cause CONTACT DERMATITIS. SAPONINS have been identified in the root.

name: Pyrolaceae
description: A plant family of the order Ericales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida.

name: Pyrola
description: A plant genus of the family PYROLACEAE. The common name of wintergreen is more often used for GAULTHERIA.

name: Aconitum
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Members contain a number of diterpenoid alkaloids including: aconitans, hypaconitine, ACONITINE, jesaconitine, ignavine, napelline, and mesaconitine. The common name of Wolfbane is similar to the common name for ARNICA.

name: Actaea
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE.

name: Adonis
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Members contain cardenolide oligoglycosides such as adoniside, adonisidum and alepposide.

name: Nigella
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE.

name: Hajdu-Cheney Syndrome
description: Rare, autosomal dominant syndrome characterized by ACRO-OSTEOLYSIS, generalized OSTEOPOROSIS, and skull deformations.

name: Nigella damascena
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. The name is similar to giant fennel (FERULA), true fennel (FOENICULUM), and dog fennel (ANTHEMIS).

name: Nigella sativa
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE that contains alpha-hederin, a triterpene saponin in the seeds, and is the source of black seed oil.

name: Delphinium
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Members contain ACONITINE and other diterpenoid alkaloids.

name: Anemone
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE that contains triterpene saponins. The root of Anemone raddeana is the source of a Chinese folk medicine, zhu jie xian fu. The common name of liverwort is also used with other plants. This genus is unrelated to SEA ANEMONES.

name: Aquilegia
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE that contains aquiledine, isoaquiledine and cycloartane-type glycosides.

name: Cimicifuga
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE that contains triterpenoid saponins. Remifemin from C. racemosa is used to suppress LUTEINIZING HORMONE. It is reclassified by some to ACTAEA. The common name of black snakeroot is also used with ASARUM and SANICULA.

name: Gestational Trophoblastic Disease
description: A group of diseases arising from pregnancy that are commonly associated with hyperplasia of trophoblasts (TROPHOBLAST) and markedly elevated human CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN. They include HYDATIDIFORM MOLE, invasive mole (HYDATIDIFORM MOLE, INVASIVE), placental-site trophoblastic tumor (TROPHOBLASTIC TUMOR, PLACENTAL SITE), and CHORIOCARCINOMA. These neoplasms have varying propensities for invasion and spread.

name: Hemorrhagic Septicemia, Viral
description: A systemic infection of various salmonid and a few nonsalmonid fishes caused by Viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (see NOVIRHABDOVIRUS),

name: Cynara
description: A plant genus of the family ASTERACEAE.

name: Cynara scolymus
description: A plant species of the genus CYNARA, family ASTERACEAE. The flower bud is the familiar artichoke eaten as a vegetable.

name: Dahlia
description: A plant genus of the family ASTERACEAE that contains antifungal plant defensin.

name: Coreopsis
description: A plant genus of the family ASTERACEAE that contains phenyl propanoids.

name: Pulsatilla
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Members contain cernuosides and other oleanane and hederagenin saponins.

name: Ranunculus
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE that contains protoanemonin, anemonin, and ranunculin.

name: Semiaquilegia
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE that contains griffonilide, lithospermoside, and magnoflorine.

name: Thalictrum
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Members contain isoquinoline alkaloids and triterpene glycosides.

name: Xanthorhiza
description: A plant genus of the family RANUNCULACEAE. Members contain isoquinoline alkaloids.

name: Resedaceae
description: A plant family of the order Capparales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida. It is a small family of herbs and shrubs. Some produce GLUCOSINOLATES.

name: Ceanothus
description: A plant genus of the family RHAMNACEAE. Root nodules host the Frankia (ACTINOMYCETES) nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

name: Colubrina
description: A plant genus of the family RHAMNACEAE. Members contain antifungal jujubogenin saponins.

name: Choriocarcinoma, Non-gestational
description: A highly malignant CHORIOCARCINOMA derived from the non-placental origin such as the totipotent cells in the TESTIS, the OVARY, and the PINEAL GLAND. It produces high levels of CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN and can metastasize widely through the bloodstream to the lungs, brain, liver, bone, and other viscera by the time of diagnosis.

name: Rhamnus
description: A plant genus of the family RHAMNACEAE. This genus is often called buckthorn but should not be confused with HIPPOPHAE or KARWINSKIA. Some RHAMNUS species have been reclassified into this genus. F. purshiana bark is cascara sagrada. Members contain frangulanin, frangulin, and anthraquinones such as EMODIN.

name: Karwinskia
description: A plant genus of the family RHAMNACEAE that contains tullidinol (toxin T-544) and peroxisomicine (toxin T-514). It is sometimes called buckthorn but should not be confused with other plants called that.

name: Ziziphus
description: A plant genus of the family RHAMNACEAE. Members contain nummularogenin (a spirostane) and is the source of an edible fruit.

name: Connaraceae
description: A plant family of the order ROSALES, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida that are tropical plants. The flowers are usually bisexual and have 5 sepals and petals; 5 or 10 stamens; and 1, 4, or usually 5 separate, one-chambered, female ovule-bearing structures (carpels).

name: Kalanchoe
description: A plant genus of the family CRASSULACEAE. Members contain bryophyllins (also called bryotoxins) which are bufadienolides (BUFANOLIDES) that have insecticidal activity.

name: Sedum
description: A plant genus of the family CRASSULACEAE. Some species in this genus are called stonecrop which is also a common name for RHODIOLA.

name: Grossulariaceae
description: A plant family of the order ROSALES, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida. They are deciduous woody shrubs with alternate leaves. The flowers are in terminal racemes with 5 petals and 5 stamens.

name: Ribes
description: Also known as currant, ribes is a member of the family GROSSULARIACEAE. Oil extracted from the seeds contain GAMMA-LINOLENIC ACID.

name: Hydrangea
description: A plant genus of the family HYDRANGEACEAE. Members contain hydrangenol, thunberginols, hydramacrosides A and B, and secoiridoid glucosides.

name: Agrimonia
description: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE that has been used in folk treatment of diabetes. Members contain agrimoniin (TANNINS).

name: Alchemilla
description: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE. Members contain esculetin and QUERCETIN.

name: Eriobotrya
description: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE that is the source of an edible fruit. Members contain TRITERPENES.

name: Filipendula
description: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE. Members contain TANNINS.

name: Fragaria
description: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE known for the edible fruit.

name: Geum
description: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE. Members contain TRITERPENES.

name: Potentilla
description: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE. Members contain procyanidins and TANNINS.

name: Pyrus
description: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE known for the edible fruit.

name: Quillaja
description: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE whose members produce SAPONINS.

name: Pyracantha
description: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE widely cultivated as a prickly hedge with bright red berries. Members contain pyracrenic acid (a lupane triterpenoid).

name: Spiraea
description: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE. Members contain prunioside, spiramine and other diterpene alkaloids.

name: Sanguisorba
description: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE. Members contain sanguiin.

name: Sorbus
description: A plant genus of the family ROSACEAE.

name: Saxifragaceae
description: The saxifrage plant family of the order SAXIFRAGALES, class Magnoliopsida. The leaves are alternate and sometimes deeply lobed or form rosettes. The flowers have both male and female parts and 4 or 5 sepals and petals; they are usually in branched clusters. The fruit is a capsule with many seeds.

name: Heuchera
description: A plant genus of the family SAXIFRAGACEAE with dark green round or heart-shaped leaves and tiny flowers.

name: Delegation, Professional
description: The process of assigning duties to a subordinate with lesser qualifications.

name: Integrons
description: DNA elements that include the component genes and insertion site for a site-specific recombination system that enables them to capture mobile gene cassettes.

name: Personnel Delegation
description: To entrust to the care or management of another, to transfer or to assign tasks within an organizational or administrative unit or structure

name: Nested Genes
description: Genes whose entire sequences are contained within other genes.

name: Galium
description: A genus of herbaceous annual and perennial plants in the family RUBIACEAE.

name: Gardenia
description: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members contain genepin, from which geniposide is obtained for use as a crosslinking agent in ADHESIVES, and 3-caffeoyl-4-sinapoylquinic acid.

name: Hamelia
description: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE that has a name very similar to another plant genus, HAMAMELIS.

name: Hedyotis
description: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members contain anthraquinones and iridoids. H. diffusa is used in DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL.

name: Mitragyna
description: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members contain antimalarial (ANTIMALARIALS) and analgesic (ANALGESICS) indole alkaloids.

name: Morinda
description: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members contain iridoid glycosides and ANTHRAQUINONES.

name: Oldenlandia
description: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Some species are used as an ingredient in Chinese and African traditional medicines. Members contain kalata B1, a macrocyclic peptide.

name: Pausinystalia
description: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members produce YOHIMBINE.

name: Psychotria
description: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members contain psychotridine and brachycerine (indole alkaloids).

name: Uncaria
description: A plant genus of the family RUBIACEAE. Members contain uncarine and other cytotoxic and hypotensive oxindole alkaloids.

name: Casimiroa
description: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE. The fruit is edible and the seed has cardiovascular activity.

name: Citrus aurantiifolia
description: A plant species of the genus CITRUS, family RUTACEAE that provides the familiar lime fruit. Its common name of lime is similar to the limetree (TILIA).

name: Citrus paradisi
description: A plant species of the genus CITRUS, family RUTACEAE that produces the familiar grapefruit. There is evidence that grapefruit inhibits CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP3A4, resulting in delayed metabolism and higher blood levels of a variety of drugs.

name: Citrus sinensis
description: A plant species of the genus CITRUS, family RUTACEAE that provides the familiar orange fruit which is also a source of orange oil.

name: Isochores
description: Large regions of the GENOME that contain local similarities in BASE COMPOSITION.

name: Evodia
description: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE which is used in Chinese medicine (DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL). Evodiamine and other quinazoline alkaloids (QUINAZOLINES) are obtained from the fruit of E. ruticarpa.

name: Murraya
description: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE. Members contain murrayanine, koenine, isomahanine, kwangsine, siamenol, murrayafoline A, murrayaquinone A and other cytotoxic carbazolequinones.

name: Phellodendron
description: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE. Members contain BERBERINE, indolopyridoquinazoline and other ALKALOIDS and limonoids.

name: Pilocarpus
description: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE that is the natural source of PILOCARPINE.

name: Poncirus
description: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE. Members contain ponfolin, a coumarin (COUMARINS).

name: Ruta
description: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE. Members contain quinoline alkaloids.

name: Zanthoxylum
description: A plant genus of the family RUTACEAE. Some members of Zanthoxylum are reclassified from ELEUTHEROCOCCUS, Melicope, and EVODIA. The twigs are used as dental brushing sticks (TOOTHBRUSHING). Most plants that are called Fagara have been reclassified as Zanthoxylum, however some Fagara were reclassified to MELICOPE (also in the Rutacea family) or to GLEDITSIA (a genus in the FABACEAE family).

name: Populus
description: A plant genus of the family SALICACEAE. Balm of Gilead is a common name used for P. candicans, or P. gileadensis, or P. jackii, and sometimes also used for ABIES BALSAMEA or for COMMIPHORA.

name: Salix
description: A plant genus of the family Salicaceae. Members contain salicin, which yields SALICYLIC ACID.

name: Salvadoraceae
description: A plant family of the order Celastrales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida, a small family growing in the tropics. Members contain piperidine alkaloids and GLUCOSINOLATES.

name: Pyrularia
description: A plant genus of the family SANTALACEAE. Members contain thionin toxin, which shouldn't be confused with thionine.

name: Santalum
description: A plant genus of the family SANTALACEAE which is the source of sandalwood oil.

name: Blighia
description: A plant genus of the family SAPINDACEAE. Members contain hypoglycins and ackee oil.

name: Litchi
description: A plant genus of the family SAPINDACEAE that bears sweet fruits. Unusual fatty acids such as cyclopropanoic fatty acids have been identified in the seeds.

name: Paullinia
description: A plant genus of the family SAPINDACEAE. The seed of P. cupana is the source of guarana powder which contains 4% CAFFEINE.

name: Sapindus
description: A plant genus of the family SAPINDACEAE that contain SAPONINS.

name: Madhuca
description: A plant genus of the family SAPOTACEAE that is the source of mahua oil. Members contain oleanene triterpenoid saponins.

name: Manilkara
description: A plant genus of the family SAPOTACEAE that bears sweet fruit.

name: Mimusops
description: A plant genus of the family SAPOTACEAE. Members contain triterpenoid saponins. Latex from bark incisions is processed into gutta balata.

name: Palaquium
description: A plant genus of the family SAPOTACEAE. Latex from bark incisions is processed into GUTTA-PERCHA.

name: Pouteria
description: A plant genus of the family SAPOTACEAE. Members contain triterpenes. Some species in this genus are called mamey which is also a common name for MAMMEA.

name: Synsepalum
description: A plant genus of the family SAPOTACEAE. Members contain miraculin (also spelled mieraculin), a sweet protein.

name: Saururaceae
description: A plant family of the order Piperales, subclass Magnoliidae class Magnoliopsida. Members contain sauristolactam, and aristololactam BII.

name: Kadsura
description: A plant genus of the family SCHISANDRACEAE used in folk medicine in a manner similar to SCHISANDRA. Members contain KADSURENONE and KADSURIN.

name: Schisandra
description: A plant genus of the family Schisandraceae which contain schisandrins (Russian) which are also called gomisins (Japanese) or wuweizins (Chinese). Compounds produced by this genus are very similar in composition and use to that of the related KADSURA plant.

name: Antirrhinum
description: A plant genus of the family Plantaginaceae. Members contain DEFICIENS PROTEIN.

name: Craterostigma
description: A plant genus of the order Lamiales, family Linderniaceae.

name: Euphrasia
description: A plant genus of the family Orobanchaceae used in FOLK REMEDIES for the eyes.

name: Linaria
description: A plant genus of the family Plantaginaceae. Members contain linarin (also called acaciin).

name: Mimulus
description: A plant genus of the family Phrymaceae. Members contain 6-geranylflavanones and mimulone.

name: Picrorhiza
description: A plant genus of the family Plantaginaceae. Members contain scrosides (CINNAMATES) and phenylethanoid glycoside. P. kurrooa is the source of picroliv (a purified iridoid glycoside fraction from the roots having hepatoprotective, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties).

name: Pedicularis
description: A plant genus of the family Orobanchaceae. Members contain phenylpropanoid glycosides and iridoids.

name: Penstemon
description: A plant genus of the family Plantaginaceae. Members contain phenylpropanoid and iridoid glycosides.

name: Veronica
description: A plant genus of the family Plantaginaceae. Members contain bis-sesquiterpene and iridoid glucosides.

name: Verbascum
description: A plant genus of the family Scrophulariaceae.

name: Scrophularia
description: A plant genus of the family SCROPHULARIACEAE. Members contain iridoids.

name: Rehmannia
description: A plant genus of the family Rehmanniaceae. Members contain catapol, rehmannin and ALKALOIDS.

name: Ailanthus
description: A plant genus of the family SIMAROUBACEAE. Members contain ailantinols and other quassinoids.

name: Brucea
description: A plant genus of the family SIMAROUBACEAE. Members contain bruceosides and bruceanols (quassinoids). The astringent seeds have been used to treat dysentery in southeastern Asia.

name: Picrasma
description: A plant genus of the family SIMAROUBACEAE. Members contain javanicins, picrasinoside and other quassinoids.

name: Quassia
description: A plant genus of the family SIMAROUBACEAE. Members contain quassinoids. Quassia simarouba has been reclassified as SIMAROUBA.

name: Simarouba
description: A plant genus of the family SIMAROUBACEAE. Members produce quassinoids.

name: Smilax
description: A plant genus of the family SMILACACEAE. Members contain smiglasides (phenylpropanoid glycosides) and steroidal saponins. Commercially it is sometimes adulterated with HEMIDESMUS, which would affect experimental results. Drinks called sarsaparilla and root beer have been prepared from the Smilaz ornata (Jamaican sarsaparilla) and SASSAFRAS.

name: Atropa
description: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE which contain SOLANACEOUS ALKALOIDS including ATROPINE which is named after this genus.

name: Cestrum
description: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain steroidal saponins and cause CALCINOSIS in grazing livestock due to high levels of 1 ALPHA,25-DIHYDROXYVITAMIN D3.

name: Datura
description: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain TROPANES. The common name of trumpet flower is also sometimes used for GELSEMIUM.

name: Duboisia
description: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE that is a source of SCOPOLAMINE and other TROPANES.

name: Hyoscyamus
description: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE which contains TROPANES.

name: Lycium
description: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain CEREBROSIDES and SCOPOLETIN.

name: Petunia
description: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain steroidal glycosides.

name: Physalis
description: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain physalin and withangulatin.

name: Solanum
description: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain SOLANACEOUS ALKALOIDS. Some species in this genus are called deadly nightshade which is also a common name for ATROPA BELLADONNA.

name: Solanum melongena
description: A plant species of the genus SOLANUM, family SOLANACEAE. The fruit is a large, egg-shaped berry, varying in color from dark purple to red, yellowish, or white. The leaves are large and ovate. The flowers are pendant, violet, and two inches across.

name: Solanum nigrum
description: A plant species of the genus SOLANUM, family SOLANACEAE that contains steroidal glycosides.

name: Withania
description: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE. Members contain withanolides. Withania somnifera is the source of ashwagandha and aswal.

name: Muscle Cells
description: Mature contractile cells, commonly known as myocytes, that form one of three kinds of muscle. The three types of muscle cells are skeletal (MUSCLE FIBERS, SKELETAL), cardiac (MYOCYTES, CARDIAC), and smooth (MYOCYTES, SMOOTH MUSCLE). They are derived from embryonic (precursor) muscle cells called MYOBLASTS.

name: Sterculia
description: A plant genus of the family STERCULIACEAE. S. urens is the source of KARAYA GUM which is sometimes called Indian tragacanth, which is different from the true TRAGACANTH which comes from ASTRAGALUS GUMMIFER.

name: Styrax
description: A plant genus of the family STYRACACEAE. Sap of these Asian trees are a source of a balsam (BALSAMS). This styrax balsam is 3/4 coniferyl benzoate, 1/8 free BENZOIC ACID, along with benzyl cinnamate, vanillin, and TRITERPENES.

name: Tamaricaceae
description: A plant family of the order Violales, subclass Dilleniidae, class Magnoliopsida.

name: Daphne
description: A plant genus of the family THYMELAEACEAE. They are evergreen shrubs much cultivated in garden borders and rock gardens in mild climates. Members contain mezerein, flavonoids, and COUMARINS such as daphnetin and daphnin.

name: Wikstroemia
description: A plant genus of the family THYMELAEACEAE. Members contain daphnoretin and wikstroelides and daphnane-type DITERPENES.

name: Corchorus
description: A plant genus of the family TILIACEAE. Members contain cycloartane saponins and CARDENOLIDES.

name: Grewia
description: A plant genus of the family TILIACEAE. Members contain lupeol and betulin TRITERPENES.

name: Myocytes, Cardiac
description: Striated muscle cells found in the heart. They are derived from cardiac myoblasts (MYOBLASTS, CARDIAC).

name: Tilia
description: A plant genus of the family TILIACEAE. Some species in this genus are called Limetree which is nearly the same as the common name for lime (CITRUS AURANTIIFOLIA). Some people are allergic to the POLLEN.

name: Triumfetta
description: A plant genus of the family TILIACEAE. The common name of burweed is also used for AMSINCKIA. Triumfetta semitriloba is considered a noxious weed.

name: Myoblasts, Cardiac
description: Precursor cells destined to differentiate into cardiac myocytes (MYOCYTES, CARDIAC).

name: Tropaeolaceae
description: A plant family of the order Geraniales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida.

name: Tropaeolum
description: A plant genus of the family TROPAEOLACEAE. The common nasturtium is a plant that grows 2.4-3.6 m (8-12 feet) tall and has funnel-shaped flowers that are commonly yellow-orange with red spots or stripes and have a long spur that contains sweet nectar. Some species in this genus are called watercress which is also a common name for RORIPPA and NASTURTIUM.

name: Myocytes, Smooth Muscle
description: Non-striated, elongated, spindle-shaped cells found lining the digestive tract, uterus, and blood vessels. They are derived from specialized myoblasts (MYOBLASTS, SMOOTH MUSCLE).

name: Myoblasts, Smooth Muscle
description: Precursor cells destined to differentiate into smooth muscle myocytes (MYOCYTES, SMOOTH MUSCLE).

name: Typhaceae
description: A plant family of the order Typhales, subclass Commelinidae, class Liliopsida (monocotyledons) that contains a single genus, Typha, that grows worldwide.

name: Boehmeria
description: A plant genus of the family URTICACEAE. Members contain cryptopleurine, beta-sitosterol, daucosterol and 19 alpha-hydroxyursolic acid.

name: Parietaria
description: A plant genus of the family URTICACEAE which is the most common cause of pollinosis in Mediterranean countries. It is the source of 'allergen Par o I' and of Pollinex used for DESENSITIZATION, IMMUNOLOGIC.

name: Nardostachys
description: A plant genus of the family VALERIANACEAE. Nardostachysin, nardostachin, nardosinone, valeranone, and patchoulene have been found in this genus. Nardostachys jatamansi is classified by some as Valeriana jatamansi.

name: Patrinia
description: A plant genus of the family VALERIANACEAE. Members contain ursolic acid and oleanolic acid glycosides, sulfapatrinosides (triterpenoid glycosides), and patriscabrol (iridolactone).

name: Valerianella
description: A plant genus of the family VALERIANACEAE. It is sometimes called goosefoot cornsalad but should not be confused with true goosefoot (CHENOPODIUM).

name: Avicennia
description: A plant genus of the family Acanthaceae. Members contain NAPHTHOQUINONES. Black mangroves (common name for the genus) are distinguished from other mangroves by their spike-like aerial roots called pneumatophores that project from the soil or water surrounding the plants.

name: Callicarpa
description: A plant genus of the family Lamiaceae. Members contain clerodane DITERPENES and callicarpone.

name: Clerodendrum
description: A plant genus of the family Lamiaceae. Inerminosides (iridoid glycosides); colebroside A; STEROIDS; STEROLS; terpenoid glucosides; and abietane DITERPENES have been found in this genus.

name: Lantana
description: A plant genus of the family VERBENACEAE. Members contain lantadene and other TRITERPENES.

name: Lippia
description: A plant genus of the family VERBENACEAE. Lippsidoquinone; TRITERPENES; SESQUITERPENES; and THYMOL have been found in this genus. Plant extracts have cytotoxic activity. It is sometimes called Mexican oregano but that confuses it with real oregano (ORIGANUM).

name: Verbena
description: A plant genus of the family VERBENACEAE. Members contain verbenachalcone (dimeric dihydrochalcone), iridoids, and phenylethanoids.

name: Viola
description: A plant genus of the family VIOLACEAE. Some species in this genus are called bouncing bet which is a common name more often used with SAPONARIA OFFICINALIS. Members contain macrocyclic peptides.

name: Ampelopsis
description: A plant genus of the family VITACEAE. Members contain momordin and SITOSTEROLS.

name: Cissus
description: A plant genus of the family VITACEAE. Cissus rufescence gum is considered comparable to TRAGACANTH.

name: Winteraceae
description: A plant family of the order Magnoliales, subclass Magnoliidae, class Magnoliopsida. The wood lacks water-conducting cells but has acrid sap. The leaves are gland-dotted, leathery, and smooth-margined. The flowers are small, in clusters, with two to six sepals, petals in two or more series, several stamens, and one to several carpels.

name: Drimys
description: A plant genus of the family WINTERACEAE. They have leathery, elliptic-shaped leaves; red-tinged shoots; and jasmine-scented, cream-colored, 8- to 12-petaled, 2.5-centimeter (1-inch) flowers in clusters.

name: Pseudowintera
description: A plant genus of the family WINTERACEAE. Members contain polygodial.

name: Marantaceae
description: A plant family of the order ZINGIBERALES, subclass Zingiberidae, class Liliopsida.

name: Heliconiaceae
description: A plant family of the order ZINGIBERALES, subclass Zingiberidae, class Liliopsida.

name: Strelitziaceae
description: A plant family of the order ZINGIBERALES, subclass Zingiberidae, class Liliopsida. Some species in this genus are called bird-of-paradise (Strelitzia reginae) which is also a common name for CAESALPINIA and Heliconia (HELICONIACEAE).

name: Alpinia
description: A plant genus of the family ZINGIBERACEAE. Members contain galangin, yakuchinone-A, and diarylheptanoids.

name: Balanites
description: A plant genus of the family ZYGOPHYLLACEAE. Feruloyltyramine, balanitoside (a furostanol glycoside), and cytostatic steroidal saponins have been found in this genus. B. aegyptiaca fruit water extract is traditionally used as an anthelmintic in the Sudan.

name: Guaiacum
description: A plant genus of the family ZYGOPHYLLACEAE. GUAIAC is obtained from G. officinale or G. sanctum. Some species in this genus are called lignum vitae which is also a common name for other trees.

name: Larrea
description: A plant genus of the family ZYGOPHYLLACEAE. It is sometimes called chaparral but that is a generic word which is used with a number of other plants. Members contain NORDIHYDROGUAIARETIC ACID.

name: Peganum
description: A plant genus of the family ZYGOPHYLLACEAE. HARMALINE and other ALKALOIDS, phenylpropanoids, and TRITERPENES have been found in plants of this genus.

name: Tribulus
description: A plant genus of the family ZYGOPHYLLACEAE. Members contain steroidal saponins. Ingestion by grazing animals causes PHOTOSENSITIVITY DISORDERS called geeldikkop (yellow thick head) in South Africa.

name: Zygophyllum
description: A plant genus of the family ZYGOPHYLLACEAE. Members contain SAPONINS.

name: Myoblasts
description: Embryonic (precursor) cells of the myogenic lineage that develop from the MESODERM. They undergo proliferation, migrate to their various sites, and then differentiate into the appropriate form of myocytes (MYOCYTES, SKELETAL; MYOCYTES, CARDIAC; MYOCYTES, SMOOTH MUSCLE).

name: Wisteria
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE. Members contain wistarin, wisteria lectin and wistariasaponin.

name: Myoblasts, Skeletal
description: Precursor cells destined to differentiate into skeletal myocytes (MYOCYTES, SKELETAL).

name: Canavalia
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE. Canavalia ensiformis is the source of CONCANAVALIN A.

name: Chromosomes, Plant
description: Complex nucleoprotein structures which contain the genomic DNA and are part of the CELL NUCLEUS of PLANTS.

name: Cycadopsida
description: A class of vascular seed plants also known as gymnosperms in the subdivision spermatophytina. They have large cones and pinnate leaves. Examples are pines, spruces, cedars and sequoias.

name: Zamiaceae
description: A plant family of the order Cycadales, class Cycadopsida, division CYCADOPHYTA.

name: Cephalotaxus
description: A plant genus of the family TAXACEAE, order Pinales, class Pinopsida, division TRACHEOPHYTA. Members contain homoharringtonine.

name: Cryptomeria
description: A plant genus of the family CUPRESSACEAE which produce POLLEN that is a major ALLERGEN.

name: Cunninghamia
description: A plant genus of the family TAXODIACEAE. Members contain DITERPENES.

name: Sequoia
description: A plant genus of the family CUPRESSACEAE known for tall trees with coastal distribution in California and Oregon. Related giant sequoia is SEQUOIADENDRON GIGANTEUM and are found in the Sierra Mountain range of California.

name: Sequoiadendron
description: A plant genus of the family CUPRESSACEAE known for giant trees like the tall SEQUOIA redwoods.

name: Taxodium
description: A plant genus of the family CUPRESSACEAE. Members contain taxodione and taxodone, which are diterpenoid quinone methide tumor inhibitors.

name: Taxaceae
description: A plant family of the order Pinales, class Pinopsida, division TRACHEOPHYTA.

name: Dryopteridaceae
description: The wood fern plant family of the order Polypodiales, class Filicopsida, division Pteridophyta.

name: Dryopteris
description: A plant genus of the family DRYOPTERIDACEAE. Members contain aspidin and filicic acid.

name: Polystichum
description: A plant genus of the family DRYOPTERIDACEAE.

name: Polypodium
description: A plant genus of the family POLYPODIACEAE. Members contain polypodoside.

name: Pteris
description: A plant genus of the family PTERIDACEAE. Members contain entkaurane DITERPENES. The name is similar to bracken fern (PTERIDIUM).

name: Satellite Cells, Skeletal Muscle
description: Elongated, spindle-shaped, quiescent myoblasts lying in close contact with adult skeletal muscle. They are thought to play a role in muscle repair and regeneration.

name: Dennstaedtiaceae
description: The bracken fern plant family of the order Polypodiales, class Filicopsida, division Pteridophyta.

name: Pteridium
description: A plant genus of the family DENNSTAEDTIACEAE. Members contain ptaquiloside, braxin A1, and braxin B. The name is similar to brake fern (PTERIS).

name: Huperzia
description: A plant genus of the family LYCOPODIACEAE. Members contain huperzine, one of the CHOLINESTERASE INHIBITORS.

name: Lycopodium
description: A plant genus of the family LYCOPODIACEAE. Members contain ALKALOIDS. Lycopodium oil is obtained from L. clavatum.

name: Selaginellaceae
description: A plant family of the order Selaginellales, class Lycopodiopsida, division Lycopodiophyta, subkingdom TRACHEOPHYTA. Members contain bilobetin. The rarely used common name of resurrection plant is mainly used with CRATEROSTIGMA.

name: Immunity, Herd
description: The state of a community in which a significant proportion of its population becomes immune to an infectious disease, and the risk of person-to-person transmission decreases. Individuals who are not immune and susceptible are indirectly protected because ongoing disease spread is very small.

name: Cotton Fiber
description: A TEXTILE fiber obtained from the pappus (outside the SEEDS) of cotton plant (GOSSYPIUM).

name: Tuberculosis Vaccines
description: Vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent or treat TUBERCULOSIS.

name: Erysimum
description: A plant genus of the family BRASSICACEAE. Some members contain CARDIAC GLYCOSIDES.

name: Caragana
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE. Members contain STILBENES.

name: Scopolia
description: A plant genus of the family SOLANACEAE after which the compound SCOPOLAMINE got its name.

name: Alangiaceae
description: A plant family of the order Cornales, subclass Rosidae, class Magnoliopsida, consisting of slow-growing evergreen trees common in tropical forests of south India and Burma. Members contain tetrahydroisoquinoline-monoterpene and iridoid glycosides.

name: Eurotiales
description: An order of fungi in the phylum ASCOMYCOTA characterized by the presence of well defined peridia and cleistothecial asci. Notable anamorphs (mitosporic forms) of Eurotiales include PENICILLIUM and ASPERGILLUS.

name: Cordyceps
description: A genus of ascomycetous fungi (ASCOMYCOTA), family Clavicipitaceae, order HYPOCREALES, that grows by infecting insect larvae or mature insects with spores that germinate often before the cocoon is formed.

name: Biomimetics
description: An interdisciplinary field in materials science, ENGINEERING, and BIOLOGY, studying the use of biological principles for synthesis or fabrication of BIOMIMETIC MATERIALS.

name: Adult Children
description: Children who have reached maturity or the legal age of majority.

name: Advance Care Planning
description: Discussions with patients and/or their representatives about the goals and desired direction of the patient's care, particularly end-of-life care, in the event that the patient is or becomes incompetent to make decisions.

name: Monascus
description: A genus in the family Monascaceae, order EUROTIALES. One species, Monascus purpureus, has multiple uses in traditional Chinese medicine (MEDICINE, CHINESE TRADITIONAL).

name: Casuistry
description: A method of ETHICAL ANALYSIS that emphasizes practical problem solving through examining individual cases that are considered to be representative; sometimes used to denote specious argument or rationalization. Differentiate from casuistics, which is the recording and study of cases and disease.

name: Codes of Ethics
description: Systematic statements of principles or rules of appropriate professional conduct, usually established by professional societies.

name: Committee Membership
description: The composition of a committee; the state or status of being a member of a committee.

name: Commodification
description: The social process by which something or someone comes to be regarded and treated as an article of trade or commerce.

name: Sinomenium
description: A plant genus of the family MENISPERMACEAE. Members contain sinomenine, caffeine, 1,7-dimethylxanthine, and other ALKALOIDS.

name: Emericella
description: A genus in the family Trichocomaceae, order EUROTIALES. The anamorph is ASPERGILLUS.

name: Buddleja
description: A plant genus of the family SCROPHULARIACEAE. Members contain mimengoside B, verbascoside, and phenylethanoids.

name: Litsea
description: A plant genus of the family LAURACEAE. Members contain laurotetanine and other APORPHINES.

name: Comprehension
description: The act or fact of grasping the meaning, nature, or importance of; understanding. (American Heritage Dictionary, 4th ed) Includes understanding by a patient or research subject of information disclosed orally or in writing.

name: Talaromyces
description: A fungal genus in the family Trichocomaceae, order EUROTIALES, characterized by loose hyphal fruiting bodies containing spherical asci. Anamorphs include PENICILLIUM and PAECILOMYCES.

name: Ganoderma
description: A genus of fungi in the family Ganodermataceae, order POLYPORALES, containing a dimitic hyphal system. It causes a white rot and is a wood decomposer. Ganoderma lucidum (REISHI) is used in traditional Chinese medicine (MEDICINE, CHINESE TRADITIONAL).

name: Confucianism
description: A school of thought and set of moral, ethical, and political teachings usually considered to be founded by Confucius in 6th-5th century B.C. China. (from Cambridge Dictionary of Philosophy, 1995)

name: Cinnamomum aromaticum
description: A plant species of the genus CINNAMOMUM that contains CINNAMATES and has been used in traditional Chinese medicine (DRUGS, CHINESE HERBAL).

name: Consensus
description: General agreement or collective opinion; the judgment arrived at by most of those concerned.

name: Sperm Midpiece
description: The middle piece of the spermatozoon is a highly organized segment consisting of MITOCHONDRIA, the outer dense fibers and the core microtubular structure.

name: Consent Forms
description: Documents describing a medical treatment or research project, including proposed procedures, risks, and alternatives, that are to be signed by an individual, or the individual's proxy, to indicate his/her understanding of the document and a willingness to undergo the treatment or to participate in the research.

name: Dehumanization
description: The process by which a person or group of persons comes to be regarded or treated as lacking in human qualities.

name: Contracts
description: Agreements between two or more parties, especially those that are written and enforceable by law (American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language, 4th ed). It is sometimes used to characterize the nature of the professional-patient relationship.

name: Setaria Plant
description: A plant genus of the family POACEAE. The small pointed seeds are grown for hay in North America and western Europe and important as food in China and other Asian countries.

name: Ethics, Research
description: The moral obligations governing the conduct of research. Used for discussions of research ethics as a general topic.

name: Directed Tissue Donation
description: Tissue, organ, or gamete donation intended for a designated recipient.

name: Duty to Recontact
description: The ethical and/or legal obligation of a health provider or researcher to communicate with a former patient or research subject about advances in research relevant to a treatment or to a genetic or other diagnostic test provided earlier, or about proposed new uses of blood or tissue samples taken in the past for another purpose.

name: Eastern Orthodoxy
description: The name given to the religion of the body of modern churches, including among others the Greek and Russian Orthodox, that is derived from the church of the Byzantine Empire, adheres to the Byzantine rite, and acknowledges the honorary primacy of the patriarch of Constantinople. (from American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language, 4th ed)

name: Oxytropis
description: A plant genus of the family FABACEAE. Members contain SWAINSONINE.

name: Vicia sativa
description: A plant species of the genus VICIA, family FABACEAE. The seed is used for food and contains THIOCYANATES such as prunasin, cyanoalanine, cyanogen, and vicine.

name: Foot Joints
description: The articulations extending from the ANKLE distally to the TOES. These include the ANKLE JOINT; TARSAL JOINTS; METATARSOPHALANGEAL JOINT; and TOE JOINT.

name: Ethics Consultation
description: Services provided by an individual ethicist (ETHICISTS) or an ethics team or committee (ETHICS COMMITTEES, CLINICAL) to address the ethical issues involved in a specific clinical case. The central purpose is to improve the process and outcomes of patients' care by helping to identify, analyze, and resolve ethical problems.

name: Friends
description: Persons whom one knows, likes, and trusts.

name: Shear Strength
description: The internal resistance of a material to moving some parts of it parallel to a fixed plane, in contrast to stretching (TENSILE STRENGTH) or compression (COMPRESSIVE STRENGTH). Ionic crystals are brittle because, when subjected to shear, ions of the same charge are brought next to each other, which causes repulsion.

name: Genetic Determinism
description: The theory that human CHARACTER and BEHAVIOR are shaped by the GENES that comprise the individual's GENOTYPE rather than by CULTURE; ENVIRONMENT; and individual choice.

name: Genetic Services
description: Organized services to provide diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of genetic disorders.

name: Government Regulation
description: Exercise of governmental authority to control conduct.

name: Information Dissemination
description: The circulation or wide dispersal of information.

name: Intention
description: What a person has in mind to do or bring about.

name: Interdisciplinary Communication
description: Communication, in the sense of cross-fertilization of ideas, involving two or more academic disciplines (such as the disciplines that comprise the cross-disciplinary field of bioethics, including the health and biological sciences, the humanities, and the social sciences and law). Also includes differences in patterns of language usage in different academic or medical disciplines.

name: Euphausiacea
description: An order of pelagic, shrimplike CRUSTACEA. Many consume ZOOPLANKTON and a few are predacious. Many antarctic species, such as Euphausia superba, constitute the chief food of other animals.

name: Anostraca
description: An order of CRUSTACEA comprised of shrimp-like organisms containing body trunks with at least 20 segments. The are commonly used as aquarium food.

name: Jehovah's Witnesses
description: Members of a religious denomination founded in the United States during the late 19th century in which active evangelism is practiced, the imminent approach of the millennium is preached, and war and organized government authority in matters of conscience are strongly opposed (from American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language, 4th ed).
