These domains, also found in Apc3, Apc6, and Apc8, have been shown to mediate protein-protein interactions, suggesting that Apc7 may assist in coordinating the juxtaposition of the catalytic and substrate recognition module subunits relative to coactivators and APC-C inhibitors.

name: Apc8 Subunit, Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
description: A highly conserved subunit of the anaphase-promoting complex (APC-C) containing multiple 34-amino-acid tetratricopeptide repeats. These domains, also found in Apc3, Apc6, and Apc7, have been shown to mediate protein-protein interactions, suggesting that Apc8 may assist in coordinating the juxtaposition of the catalytic and substrate recognition module subunits relative to coactivators and APC-C inhibitors.

name: Apc10 Subunit, Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
description: Apc10 is necessary for coactivator-dependent substrate recognition by the anaphase-promoting complex-cyclosome. It binds the Apc2 subunit, which is a part of the catalytic core, and interacts with coactivators Cdh1 or Cdc20 to recruit substrates to the complex.

name: Apc11 Subunit, Anaphase-Promoting Complex-Cyclosome
description: Together with the Apc2 subunit, forms the catalytic core of the E3 ubiquitin ligase, anaphase-promoting complex-cyclosome. It has a RING H2 domain which interacts with the cullin domain of Apc2. Apc11 also interacts with the E2 ubiquitin ligases involved in APC-C ubiquitination reactions.

name: Cdc20 Proteins
description: Highly conserved proteins that specifically bind to and activate the anaphase-promoting complex-cyclosome, promoting ubiquitination and proteolysis of cell-cycle-regulatory proteins. Cdc20 is essential for anaphase-promoting complex activity, initiation of anaphase, and cyclin proteolysis during mitosis.

name: Cdh1 Proteins
description: Cdh1 is an activator of the anaphase-promoting complex-cyclosome and is involved in substrate recognition. It associates with the complex in late MITOSIS from anaphase through G1 to regulate activity of CYCLIN-DEPENDENT KINASES and to prevent premature DNA replication.

name: Trichomes
description: Hair-like extensions on specialized epidermal surfaces of plants which protect against damage from insects, animals, light degradation and fungal infection. Trichomes may also occur on certain unicellular EUKARYOTES.

name: O'nyong-nyong Virus
description: A species of ALPHAVIRUS causing a measles-like acute febrile rash illness. It is closely related to the Chikungunya virus and Igbo Ora viruses.

name: Aggregatibacter
description: A genus of PASTEURELLACEAE. Members are nonmotile, Gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic rods or coccobacilli. Its members are X factor (HEMIN) independent and variably dependent on V factor (NAD).

name: Aggregatibacter aphrophilus
description: A species of Gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic spherical or rod-shaped bacteria indigenous to oral cavity and pharynx. It is associated with BACTERIAL ENDOCARDITIS; and MENINGITIS.

name: Aggregatibacter segnis
description: A species of Gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic pleomorphic rod-shaped often filamentous bacteria in the genus of AGGREGATIBACTER found in the oral cavity. It is associated with DENTAL PLAQUE; and BACTERIAL ENDOCARDITIS.

name: Phytochemicals
description: A broad range of biologically active compounds which occur naturally in plants having important medicinal and nutritional properties.

name: Secondary Metabolism
description: A physiochemical process which occurs in a wide range of organisms which unlike BASAL METABOLISM is not required for or essential to short-term survivability but to long-term general well-being of the organism.

name: Connectin
description: A giant elastic protein of molecular mass ranging from 2,993 kDa (cardiac), 3,300 kDa (psoas), to 3,700 kDa (soleus) having a kinase domain. The amino- terminal is involved in a Z line binding, and the carboxy-terminal region is bound to the myosin filament with an overlap between the counter-connectin filaments at the M line.

name: Prescription Drug Diversion
description: The transfer of prescription drugs from legal to illegal distribution and marketing networks.

name: Chlorofluorocarbons, Ethane
description: A group of ethane-based halogenated hydrocarbons containing one or more fluorine and chlorine atoms.

name: Bromochlorofluorocarbons
description: A series of hydrocarbons containing BROMINE; CHLORINE and FLOURINE.

name: Biological Ontologies
description: Structured vocabularies describing concepts from the fields of biology and relationships between concepts.

name: Nestin
description: A type VI intermediate filament protein expressed mostly in nerve cells where it is associated with the survival, renewal and mitogen-stimulated proliferation of neural progenitor cells.

name: Sulfonylurea Receptors
description: ATP-BINDING CASSETTE PROTEINS that are highly conserved and widely expressed in nature. They form an integral part of the ATP-sensitive potassium channel complex which has two intracellular nucleotide folds that bind to sulfonylureas and their analogs.

name: Matrilin Proteins
description: PROTEOGLYCANS-associated proteins that are major components of EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX of various tissues including CARTILAGE; and INTERVERTEBRAL DISC structures. They bind COLLAGEN fibers and contain protein domains that enable oligomer formation and interaction with other extracellular matrix proteins such as CARTILAGE OLIGOMERIC MATRIX PROTEIN.

name: Cartilage Oligomeric Matrix Protein
description: Major component of chondrocyte EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX of various tissues including bone, tendon, ligament, SYNOVIUM and blood vessels. It binds MATRILIN PROTEINS and is associated with development of cartilage and bone.

name: Mad2 Proteins
description: Mad2 is a component of the spindle-assembly checkpoint apparatus. It binds to and inhibits the Cdc20 activator subunit of the anaphase-promoting complex, preventing the onset of anaphase until all chromosomes are properly aligned at the metaphase plate. Mad2 is required for proper microtubule capture at KINETOCHORES.

name: Separase
description: Separase is a caspase-like cysteine protease, which plays a central role in triggering ANAPHASE by cleaving the SCC1/RAD21 subunit of the cohesin complex. Cohesin holds the sister CHROMATIDS together during METAPHASE and its cleavage results in chromosome segregation.

name: Geminin
description: Geminin inhibits DNA replication by preventing the incorporation of MCM complex into pre-replication complex. It is absent during G1 phase of the CELL CYCLE and accumulates through S, G2,and M phases. It is degraded at the metaphase-anaphase transition by the ANAPHASE-PROMOTING COMPLEX-CYCLOSOME.

name: Securin
description: Securin is involved in the control of the metaphase-anaphase transition during MITOSIS. It promotes the onset of anaphase by blocking SEPARASE function and preventing proteolysis of cohesin and separation of sister CHROMATIDS. Overexpression of securin is associated with NEOPLASTIC CELL TRANSFORMATION and tumor formation.

name: Hypertriglyceridemic Waist
description: A screening phenotype consisting of both elevated WAIST CIRCUMFERENCE and elevated fasting TRIGLYCERIDES level.

name: Multifunctional Enzymes
description: Molecules that contain multiple active sites which are used to catalyze more than one enzymatic reaction. Proteins in this class generally contain multiple active sites within a single peptide chain and may also contain more than one enzymatically active subunit. They are distinguished from MULTIENZYME COMPLEXES in that their subunits are not found as distinct enzymes.

name: Preexisting Condition Coverage
description: Insurance coverage of a physical or mental health condition, disability, or illness existing before health insurance is applied for or enrolled in.

name: Intrinsically Disordered Proteins
description: Functional proteins that do not have unique, stable, folded, three-dimensional native structures or that possess non-ordered regions under physiological conditions. They are characterized by extraordinary structural flexibility and plasticity, which enable them to adopt different conformations in response to different stimuli or different interactions.

name: ATP Binding Cassette Transporter 1
description: A superfamily of integral ATP-binding cassette membrane proteins whose expression pattern is consistent with a role in lipid (cholesterol) efflux. It is implicated in TANGIER DISEASE, characterized by accumulation of cholesteryl ester in various tissues.

name: Non-Nutritive Sweeteners
description: Chemical additives, such as aspartame, saccharin, and sucralose, that give a sweet taste to foods without contributing significant calories or promoting tooth decay. They are generally much sweeter than sucrose.

name: Microbiota
description: The full collection of microbes (bacteria, fungi, virus, etc.) that naturally exist within a particular biological niche such as an organism, soil, a body of water, etc.

name: MEF2 Transcription Factors
description: Activating transcription factors of the MADS family which bind a specific sequence element (MEF2 element) in many muscle-specific genes and are involved in skeletal and cardiac myogenesis, neuronal differentiation and survival/apoptosis.

name: Torpor
description: A state of decreased activity in animals characterized by depressed metabolism, reduced body temperature, and low sensitivity to external stimuli.

name: Genome, Microbial
description: The genetic complement of a microorganism as represented in its DNA or in some microorganisms its RNA.

name: Genes, Microbial
description: The functional hereditary units of a microorganism.

name: Healthy Volunteers
description: Persons with no known significant health problems who are recruited to participate in research to test a new drug, device, or intervention as controls for a patient group. (from http://clinicalcenter.nih.gov/recruit/volunteers.html, accessed 2/14/2013)

name: Spike Glycoprotein, Coronavirus
description: A class I viral fusion protein that forms the characteristic spikes, or peplomers, found on the viral surface that mediate virus attachment, fusion, and entry into the host cell. During virus maturation, it is cleaved into two subunits: S1, which binds to receptors in the host cell, and S2, which mediates membrane fusion.

name: Hazardous Waste Sites
description: Sites where HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES are deposited. Some have facilities for safely storing, processing, and recycling these waste products.

name: Ankle Fractures
description: Fractures of any of the bones of the ANKLE.

name: Patient Harm
description: A measure of PATIENT SAFETY considering errors or mistakes which result in harm to the patient. They include errors in the administration of drugs and other medications (MEDICATION ERRORS), errors in the performance of procedures or the use of other types of therapy, in the use of equipment, and in the interpretation of laboratory findings and preventable accidents involving patients.

name: Senior Centers
description: Community centers for older adults and providers of resources for the community. In addition to providing services and activities for older adults that reflect the community's diversity, they link participants with resources offered by other agencies.

name: Human Trafficking
description: Recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring or receipt of persons, by means of the threat or use of force or other forms of coercion, of abduction, of fraud, of deception, of the abuse of power or of a position of vulnerability or of the giving or receiving of payments or benefits to achieve the consent of a person having control over another person, for the purpose of exploitation. (UN. Protocol to prevent, suppress and punish trafficking in persons, especially women and children, supplementing the United Nations convention against transnational organized crime. General Assembly resolution 55/25. United Nations General Assembly, 2000)

name: Streptomyces rimosus
description: An actinomycete best known as the producer of the commercially important antibiotic OXYTETRACYCLINE.

name: Levalbuterol
description: The R-isomer of albuterol.

name: 3-Phosphoinositide-Dependent Protein Kinases
description: Highly conserved protein-serine threonine kinases that phosphorylate and activate a group of AGC protein kinases, especially in response to the production of the SECOND MESSENGERS, phosphatidylinositol 3,4,-biphosphate (PtdIns(3,4)P2) and phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-triphosphate (PtdIns(3,4,5)P3).

name: Type B Personality
description: Behavior pattern characterized by a generally calm and even-tempered demeanor. Emotionally, such personality types show less frequent irritation, anger, hostility, and aggression than Type A individuals. (from International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences, 2008, p. 223)

name: Type D Personality
description: Behavior pattern characterized by negative emotionality, an inability to express emotions, and social isolation, which has been linked to greater cardiovascular disease and increased mortality. (from International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences, 2008, p. 217)

name: Hospital Medicine
description: The branch of medicine concerned with the delivery of comprehensive medical care to hospitalized patients. Practitioners include physicians and non-physician providers who engage in clinical care, teaching, research, or leadership in the field of general hospital medicine.(from http://www.hospitalmedicine.org/AM/Template.cfm?Section=Hospitalist_Definition)

name: Vitamin K Epoxide Reductases
description: OXIDOREDUCTASES which mediate vitamin K metabolism by converting inactive vitamin K 2,3-epoxide to active vitamin K.

name: Chemically-Induced Disorders
description: Disorders caused by the intentional or unintentional ingestion or exposure to chemical substances such as PHARMACEUTICAL PREPARATIONS; NOXAE; and PESTICIDES.

name: Drug-Related Side Effects and Adverse Reactions
description: Disorders that result from the intended use of PHARMACEUTICAL PREPARATIONS. Included in this heading are a broad variety of chemically-induced adverse conditions due to toxicity, DRUG INTERACTIONS, and metabolic effects of pharmaceuticals.

name: Ambulance Diversion
description: The practice of redirecting ambulances and patients seeking urgent care from one emergency department to others for various reasons such as overcrowding and shortage of skilled staff.

name: Drug Trafficking
description: The illegal acquisition, sale, production, transport, movement, and distribution of controlled substances such as narcotics.

name: Tobacco Use
description: Use of TOBACCO (Nicotiana tabacum L) and TOBACCO PRODUCTS.

name: Herbals as Topic
description: Works about books, articles or other publications on herbs or plants describing their medicinal value.

name: Gasotransmitters
description: Endogenously produced lipid-soluble gaseous molecules which function as neurotransmitters and signal mediators targeting ION CHANNELS and transporters.

name: Nutritive Sweeteners
description: Any agent that adds not only sweet taste but some energy value to food. They include natural sugars such as SUCROSE; FRUCTOSE; and GALACTOSE; and certain SUGAR ALCOHOLS.

name: Hyperpolarization-Activated Cyclic Nucleotide-Gated Channels
description: A subgroup of cyclic nucleotide-regulated ION CHANNELS of the superfamily of pore-loop cation channels that are opened by hyperpolarization rather than depolarization. The ion conducting pore passes SODIUM, CALCIUM, and POTASSIUM cations with a preference for potassium.

name: Fatty Acid Synthases
description: Enzymes that catalyze the synthesis of FATTY ACIDS from acetyl-CoA and malonyl-CoA derivatives.

name: NAD (+) and NADP (+) Dependent Alcohol Oxidoreductases
description: Oxidoreductases that act on the CH-OH group of donors with NAD (+) or NADPH (+) as acceptors.

name: 3-Oxoacyl-(Acyl-Carrier-Protein) Reductase
description: A 3-oxoacyl reductase that has specificity for ACYL CARRIER PROTEIN-derived FATTY ACIDS.

name: Orexin Receptors
description: G-protein-coupled NEUROPEPTIDE RECEPTORS that have specificity for OREXINS and play a role in appetite control, and sleep-wake cycles. Two principle receptor types exist, each having a specificity for OREXIN A and OREXIN B peptide subtypes.

name: Checkpoint Kinase 2
description: Enzyme activated in response to DNA DAMAGE involved in cell cycle arrest. The gene is located on the long (q) arm of chromosome 22 at position 12.1. In humans it is encoded by the CHEK2 gene.

name: Filamins
description: A family of crosslinking filament proteins encoded by distinct FLN genes. Filamins are involved in cell adhesion, spreading, and migration, acting as scaffolds for over 90 binding partners including channels, receptors, intracellular signaling molecules and transcription factors. Due to the range of molecular interactions, mutations in FLN genes result in anomalies with moderate to lethal consequences.

name: Sequestering Agents
description: Compounds that bind to and reduce the biological availability of a chemical or pharmaceutical agent.

name: Workplace Violence
description: Threatened or actual attempt to harm others at place of employment.

name: Hepcidins
description: Forms of hepcidin, a cationic amphipathic peptide synthesized in the liver as a prepropeptide which is first processed into prohepcidin and then into the biologically active hepcidin forms, including in human the 20-, 22-, and 25-amino acid residue peptide forms. Hepcidin acts as a homeostatic regulators of iron metabolism and also possesses antimicrobial activity.

name: Solute Carrier Family 12, Member 1
description: Na-K-Cl transporter in the ASCENDING LIMB OF LOOP OF HENLE. It mediates active reabsorption of sodium chloride and is inhibited by LOOP DIURETICS such as FUROSEMIDE; and BUMETANIDE. Mutations in the gene encoding SLC12A1 are associated with a BARTTER SYNDROME.

name: Solute Carrier Family 12, Member 3
description: Na-Cl cotransporter in the convoluted segments of the DISTAL KIDNEY TUBULE. It mediates active reabsorption of sodium and chloride and is inhibited by THIAZIDE DIURETICS.

name: Solute Carrier Family 12, Member 2
description: Na-K-Cl transporter ubiquitously expressed. It plays a key role in salt secretion in epithelial cells and cell volume regulation in nonepithelial cells.

name: Solute Carrier Family 12, Member 4
description: K-Cl cotransporter ubiquitously expressed with higher expression levels in ERYTHROCYTES of ANEMIA, SICKLE CELL. It mediates active potassium and chloride cotransport across the plasma membrane and contributes to cell volume homeostasis

name: Etiolation
description: Physical changes in the growth patterns of a plant brought on by sustained absence of light. These changes are characterized by lengthened internodes which produce long weak stems, fewer leaves, and pale yellow color (chlorosis). The physiological basis for etiolation is induction of the phytohormone, AUXIN.

name: Receptor, Metabotropic Glutamate 5
description: A type I G protein-coupled receptor mostly expressed post-synaptic pyramidal cells of the cortex and CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM.

name: Peripherins
description: Type III intermediate filament proteins expressed mainly in neurons of the peripheral and CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEMS. Peripherins are implicated in neurite elongation during development and axonal regeneration after injury.

name: Histocompatibility Antigen H-2D
description: A component of the murine major histocompatibility complex class I family. It contains one Ig-like C1-type domain and functions in processing and presentation of exogenous peptide antigens to the immune system.

name: Protein Kinase C beta
description: PKC beta encodes two proteins (PKCB1 and PKCBII) generated by alternative splicing of C-terminal exons. It is widely distributed with wide-ranging roles in processes such as B-cell receptor regulation, oxidative stress-induced apoptosis, androgen receptor-dependent transcriptional regulation, insulin signaling, and endothelial cell proliferation.

name: Myxovirus Resistance Proteins
description: Interferon-induced DYNAMIN-like GTP-binding proteins localized in the cytoplasm, nuclear pore complex and nucleus. They play a role in antiviral defense and immunity.

name: Hand Sanitizers
description: Preparations used as alternatives or supplements to hand washing with soap and water to destroy microorganisms and prevent transmission of pathogens. The active ingredient may be ETHANOL; 1-PROPANOL; or POVIDONE-IODINE in a gel, foam, or liquid solution.

name: Myeloid Cell Leukemia Sequence 1 Protein
description: A member of the myeloid leukemia factor (MLF) protein family with multiple alternatively spliced transcript variants encoding different protein isoforms. In hematopoietic cells, it is located mainly in the nucleus, and in non-hematopoietic cells, primarily in the cytoplasm with a punctate nuclear localization. MLF1 plays a role in cell cycle differentiation.

name: Death-Associated Protein Kinases
description: A family of calcium/calmodulin-dependent PROETIN-SERINE-THREONINE KINASES. They are ubiquitously expressed in adult and embryonic mammalian tissues, and their functions are tightly related to the early stages of eukaryotic programmed cell death.

name: S100 Calcium Binding Protein beta Subunit
description: A calcium-binding protein that is 92 AA long, contains 2 EF-hand domains, and is concentrated mainly in GLIAL CELLS. Elevation of S100B levels in brain tissue correlates with a role in neurological disorders.

name: alpha7 Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor
description: A member of the NICOTINIC ACETYLCHOLINE RECEPTOR subfamily of the LIGAND-GATED ION CHANNEL family. It consists entirely of pentameric α7 subunits expressed in the CNS, autonomic nervous system, vascular system, lymphocytes and spleen.

name: Ubiquitin-Specific Proteases
description: Members of the peptidase C19 family which regulate signal transduction by removing UBIQUITIN from specific protein substrates via a process known as deubiquitination or deubiquitylation.

name: Selenic Acid
description: A strong dibasic acid with the molecular formula H2SeO4. Included under this heading is the acid form, and inorganic salts of dihydrogen selenium tetraoxide.

name: Osmoregulation
description: The response of cells in sensing a difference in OSMOTIC PRESSURE between the inside and outside of the cell. This response includes signaling from osmotic sensors to activate transcription factors, which in turn regulate the expression of osmocompensatory genes, all functioning to maintain CELL VOLUME and the water concentration inside the cells.

name: Selenium Oxides
description: Inorganic compounds formed through the oxidation of selenium.

name: Allografts
description: Tissues, cells, or organs transplanted between genetically different individuals of the same species.

name: Autografts
description: Transplant comprised of an individual's own tissue, transferred from one part of the body to another.

name: Heterografts
description: Tissues, cells or organs transplanted between animals of different species.

name: Bone-Patellar Tendon-Bone Grafts
description: A bone-patellar tendon graft used for fixation of the ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT during surgical reconstruction of the knee.

name: Composite Tissue Allografts
description: A graft consisting of multiple tissues, such as muscle, bone, nerve, vasculature, and skin, comprising a functional unit for reconstructive purposes.

name: Isografts
description: Tissues, cells or organs transplanted between genetically identical individuals, i.e. members of the same species with identical histocompatibility antigens, such as monozygotic twins, members of the same inbred strain, or members of a hybrid population produced by crossing certain inbred strains.

name: SLC4A Proteins
description: Bicarbonate transporters that move BICARBONATE IONS in exchange of CHLORIDE IONS or SODIUM IONS across membranes. They regulate acid-base HOMEOSTASIS, cell volume and intracellular pH. Members include CHLORIDE-BICARBONATE ANTIPORTERS (SLC4A1, 2, 3, and 9); SODIUM-COUPLED BICARBONATE TRANSPORTERS (SLC4A4 and 5, 7, 8 and 10); and a sodium borate cotransporter (SLC4A11 protein).

name: Cardiovascular Nursing
description: A specialty concerned with the nursing care of patients suffering from disorders of the CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM as well as those identified as at risk for adverse cardiac or vascular events.

name: Nephrology Nursing
description: A nursing specialty involving the care of patients with or at risk for KIDNEY DISEASES.

name: Critical Care Nursing
description: A nursing specialty that deals specifically with the care of patients who are critically ill.

name: Home Health Nursing
description: A nursing specialty in which skilled nursing care is provided to patients in their homes by registered or licensed practical NURSES. Home health nursing differs from HOME NURSING in that home health nurses are licensed professionals, while home nursing involves non-professional caregivers.

name: Basal Bodies
description: Structures which form the base of FLAGELLA and CILIA. They contain nine triplets of MICROTUBULES that are arranged around the periphery and that serve as the nucleation center for AXONEME assembly.

name: Diapause, Insect
description: Seasonal suspension of insect growth development. It can be either induced by environmental cues (e.g., PHOTOPERIOD) or as a facultative part of the life cycle in order to time development with seasonal changes.

name: Nutritionists
description: Persons specially trained in NUTRITION SCIENCES.

name: Diarylquinolines
description: A class of quinoline compounds defined by the presence of two aromatic ring structures which are attached via a side chain to carbon 3 of the qunolinyl structure. The two aromatic moieties are typically NAPTHALENE and BENZENE. Several compounds in this class are used as ANTITUBERCULAR AGENTS.

name: Nurses, Public Health
description: Nurses whose goal is to improve health and quality of life in a population or community through the prevention and treatment of disease and other physical and mental health conditions, the surveillance of cases and health indicators, and the promotion of healthy behaviors through public education and awareness.

name: Wakefulness-Promoting Agents
description: A specific category of drugs that prevent sleepiness by specifically targeting sleep-mechanisms in the brain. They are used to treat DISORDERS OF EXCESSIVE SOMNOLENCE such as NARCOLEPSY. Note that this drug category does not include broadly-acting central nervous system stimulants such as AMPHETAMINES.

name: Nurses, Community Health
description: Nurses whose work combines elements of both primary care nursing and public health practice and takes place primarily outside the therapeutic institution. Primary nursing care is directed to individuals, families, or groups in their natural settings within communities.

name: Hyoscyamine
description: The 3(S)-endo isomer of atropine.

name: Rural Nursing
description: A branch of nursing requiring generalist training with specialty knowledge in crisis assessment and management in all subdisciplines of nursing. Rural nursing practices often include geographical and social distance concepts in delivery of health care.

name: Enclomiphene
description: The trans or (E)-isomer of clomiphene.

name: Zuclomiphene
description: The cis or (Z)-isomer of clomiphene.

name: Racemethionine
description: A preparation of METHIONINE that includes a mixture of D-methionine and L-methionine isomers.

name: Parish Nursing
description: A nursing specialty involving programs designed to bring wholeness and healing to a particular faith community through addressing the health needs of body, mind, and spirit. They are coordinated by registered NURSES and may involve HEALTH EDUCATION and counseling, facilitation, referral, PATIENT ADVOCACY, and health care plan interpretation, as influenced and defined by the unique needs of the congregation.

name: Dexmethylphenidate Hydrochloride
description: A methylphenidate derivative, DOPAMINE UPTAKE INHIBITOR and CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM STIMULANT that is used in the treatment of ATTENTION DEFICIT HYPERACTIVITY DISORDER.

name: Nurses, International
description: Nurses who provide nursing care in countries other than the ones in which they received their training.

name: Pediatric Nurse Practitioners
description: Registered nurses with graduate degrees in nursing who provide care to pediatric patients who are acutely or critically ill.

name: International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health
description: The World Health Organization's classification categories of health and health-related domains. The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) consists of two lists: a list of body functions and structure, and a list of domains of activity and participation. The ICF also includes a list of environmental factors.

name: Family Nurse Practitioners
description: Registered nurses with graduate degrees in nursing who provide care to patients of all age levels, and who focus their efforts on the health care needs of the entire family.

name: Levofloxacin
description: The L-isomer of Ofloxacin.

name: Racepinephrine
description: A racemic mixture of d-epinephrine and l-epinephrine.

name: Vocal Cord Dysfunction
description: A disorder characterized by an intermittent abnormal VOCAL CORDS movement toward the midline during inspiration or expiration resulting in upper AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION.

name: Triple Negative Breast Neoplasms
description: Breast neoplasms that do not express ESTROGEN RECEPTORS; PROGESTERONE RECEPTORS; and do not overexpress the NEU RECEPTOR/HER-2 PROTO-ONCOGENE PROTEIN.

name: Neurokinin-1 Receptor Antagonists
description: Compounds that inhibit or block the activity of NEUROKININ-1 RECEPTORS.

name: Dexrazoxane
description: The (+)-enantiomorph of razoxane.

name: Lansoprazole
description: A 2,2,2-trifluoroethoxypyridyl derivative of timoprazole that is used in the therapy of STOMACH ULCERS and ZOLLINGER-ELLISON SYNDROME. The drug inhibits H(+)-K(+)-EXCHANGING ATPASE which is found in GASTRIC PARIETAL CELLS. Lansoprazole is a racemic mixture of (R)- and (S)-isomers.

name: Dexlansoprazole
description: The R-isomer of lansoprazole that is used to treat severe GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE.

name: Retrocaval Ureter
description: A rare congenital abnormality resulting in the URETER passing dorsal to and being obstructed by the INFERIOR VENA CAVA.

name: Rabeprazole
description: A 4-(3-methoxypropoxy)-3-methylpyridinyl derivative of timoprazole that is used in the therapy of STOMACH ULCERS and ZOLLINGER-ELLISON SYNDROME. The drug inhibits H(+)-K(+)-EXCHANGING ATPASE which is found in GASTRIC PARIETAL CELLS.

name: Ammonium Compounds
description: Inorganic compounds that include a positively charged tetrahedral nitrogen (ammonium ion) as part of their structure. This class of compounds includes a broad variety of simple ammonium salts and derivatives.

name: Atrial Remodeling
description: Long-term changes in the electrophysiological parameters and/or anatomical structures of the HEART ATRIA that result from prolonged changes in atrial rate, often associated with ATRIAL FIBRILLATION or long periods of intense EXERCISE.

name: Ammonium Hydroxide
description: The hydroxy salt of ammonium ion. It is formed when AMMONIA reacts with water molecules in solution.

name: Influenza A Virus, H7N9 Subtype
description: A subtype of INFLUENZA A VIRUS with the surface proteins hemagglutinin 7 and neuraminidase 9. This avian origin virus was first identified in humans in 2013.

name: Nocebo Effect
description: An adverse effect occurring with a medical treatment that is not attributable to the actions of the treatment.

name: Portion Size
description: The amount of a particular food one chooses to eat at a single meal. It is different from SERVING SIZE, which is a reference amount of food as defined by an authoritative source, such as the Food Guide Pyramid devised by the UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE.

name: Serving Size
description: A reference measure of food used to identify the calorie and nutrient content in a particular amount of that food. It is defined by an authoritative source, such as the Food Guide Pyramid devised by the UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE. It is different from PORTION SIZE, which is the amount of food one chooses to eat at a single meal.

name: Immunity, Heterologous
description: The immunological phenomenon by which exposure to some organisms or vaccines can profoundly alter the host's response to subsequent exposure to unrelated (heterologous) organisms or vaccines.

name: Clinical Laboratory Services
description: Organized services provided by MEDICAL LABORATORY PERSONNEL for the purpose of carrying out CLINICAL LABORATORY TECHNIQUES used for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease.

name: Desoxycorticosterone Acetate
description: The 21-acetate derivative of desoxycorticosterone.

name: Teratogenesis
description: The formation of CONGENITAL ABNORMALITIES.

name: Lorajmine
description: A monochloroacetyl derivative of ajmaline. It is a class Ia antiarrhythmic agent that is rapidly hydrolyzed to ajmaline by plasma and tissue esterases.

name: Veterinary Sports Medicine
description: The field of veterinary medicine concerned with PHYSICAL FITNESS of animals in sports (horse racing, dog racing, etc.) and the diagnosis and treatment of sports injuries in animals.

name: Physical Conditioning, Human
description: Diet modification and physical exercise to improve the ability to carry out daily tasks and perform physical activities.

name: Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-Proline Dioxygenases
description: Dioxygenase enzymes that specifically hydroxylate a PROLINE residue on the HYPOXIA-INDUCIBLE FACTOR 1, ALPHA SUBUNIT. They are OXYGEN-dependent enzymes that play an important role in mediating cellular adaptive responses to HYPOXIA.

name: Prolyl-Hydroxylase Inhibitors
description: Compounds that inhibit the action of HYDROXYLASES that act on PROLINE to form HYDROXYPROLINE.

name: Phospholipase A2 Inhibitors
description: Compounds that inhibit or block the activity of a PHOSPHOLIPASE A2 enzyme.

name: Urological Agents
description: Drugs used in the treatment of urological conditions and diseases such as URINARY INCONTINENCE and URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS.

name: Bunolol
description: A nonselective beta-adrenoceptor antagonist used in the treatment of glaucoma.

name: Dysbiosis
description: Changes in quantitative and qualitative composition of MICROBIOTA. The changes may lead to altered host microbial interaction or homeostatic imbalance that can contribute to a disease state often with inflammation.

name: Anticholinergic Syndrome
description: Adverse drug effects associated with CHOLINERGIC ANTAGONISTS. Clinical features include TACHYCARDIA; HYPERTHERMIA; MYDRIASIS, dry skin and dry mucous membranes, decreased bowel sounds and urinary retention in peripheral anticholinergic syndrome; and HALLUCINATIONS; PSYCHOSES; SEIZURES; and COMA in central anticholinergic syndrome.

name: Transfusion Medicine
description: The area of hematology that is concerned with the transfusion of blood and blood components, and in prevention and treatment of adverse effects from BLOOD TRANSFUSION errors.

name: Prolyl Hydroxylases
description: Enzymes that specifically hydroxylate PROLINE residues on proteins.

name: Alcohol Abstinence
description: Non-consumption of ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES.

name: Temperance Movement
description: Social effort most active in the 19th and early 20th centuries dedicated to promoting moderation or complete abstinence in the use of ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES.

name: Sports for Persons with Disabilities
description: Activities or games played by PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES, usually requiring physical effort or skill. The activities or games may be specifically created or based on existing sports, with or without modifications, to meet the needs of persons with physical or intellectual disabilities.

name: Mindfulness
description: A psychological state of awareness, the practices that promote this awareness, a mode of processing information and a character trait. As a therapy mindfulness is defined as a moment-to-moment awareness of one's experience without judgment and as a state and not a trait.

name: Mesopotamia
description: Ancient land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, corresponding to modern-day Iraq and partly NE Syria, SE Turkey and smaller parts of SW Iran. It is considered to be the cradle of civilization in the West. Bronze Age Mesopotamia included Sumer and the Akkadian, Babylonian and Assyrian empires (from http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/mesopotamia )

name: Ethnic Violence
description: Violence or other hostile behavior arising when an ethnic group either feels itself under threat, or where it seeks to assert its superiority or dominance over other groups.

name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy
description: Contextually focused form of cognitive behavioral psychotherapy that uses MINDFULNESS and behavioral activation to increase patients' psychological flexibility in areas such as ability to engage in values-based, positive behaviors while experiencing difficult thoughts, emotions, or sensations.

name: Air Travel
description: Travel by means of an airplane, helicopter, or balloon.

name: Teach-Back Communication
description: Providing the patient, family or others information, and then allowing them to take an action or restate the information in their own words. The clinician prefaces communications with a statement framed to show the clinician has the burden of effective communication rather than the patient.

name: Asia, Northern
description: A subregion of Asia, consisting of Asian portion of Russia.

name: Tatarstan
description: Political subdivision of eastern RUSSIA located within Europe. It lies between the Volga River and the Kama River, and extends east to the Ural mountains.

name: Safety-net Providers
description: Providers that by mandate or mission organize and deliver a significant level of health care and other health-related services to the uninsured, Medicaid recipients, and other vulnerable patients.

name: Organ Trafficking
description: Criminal activity that occurs in three broad categories. Firstly, cases where traffickers force or deceive the victims into giving up an organ. Secondly, there are cases where victims formally or informally agree to sell an organ and are cheated because they are not paid for the organ or are paid less than the promised price. Thirdly, vulnerable persons are treated for an ailment, which may or may not exist and thereupon organs are removed without the victim's knowledge.

name: Web Browser
description: Software application for retrieving, presenting and traversing information resources on the World Wide Web.

name: Dataset
description: Works consisting of organized collections of data, which have been stored permanently in a formalized manner suitable for communication, interpretation, or processing.

name: Observational Study
description: A work that reports on the results of a clinical study in which participants may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions, but the investigator does not assign participants to specific interventions (as in an interventional study).

name: Psychotherapy, Psychodynamic
description: Forms of PSYCHOTHERAPY falling within or deriving from the psychoanalytic tradition, that view individuals as reacting to unconscious forces (e.g., motivation, drive), that focus on processes of change and development, and that place a premium on self understanding and making meaning of what is unconscious.

name: Social Determinants of Health
description: The circumstances in which people are born, grow up, live, work, and age, as well as the systems put in place to deal with illness. These circumstances are in turn shaped by a wider set of forces: economics, social policies, and politics (http://www.cdc.gov/socialdeterminants/).

name: Disaster Victims
description: Persons adversely effected by DISASTERS, occurrences that result in property damage, deaths, and/or injuries to a community.

name: Diagnostic Uses of Chemicals
description: Chemicals administered to patients in order to diagnose or study the pathology of medical conditions, diseases, or syndromes.

name: Tick Bites
description: The effects, both local and systemic, caused by the bites of TICKS.

name: Hospice and Palliative Care Nursing
description: A nursing specialty concerned with care of patients facing serious or life-threatening illnesses. The goal of palliative nursing is to prevent and relieve suffering, and to support the best possible quality of life for patients and their families. Hospice nursing is palliative care for people in their final stages of life.

name: British Virgin Islands
description: A British overseas territory, part of the British West Indies, lying about 60 miles east of Puerto Rico. Tortola is the main island, other islands include Virgin Gorda, Jost Van Dyke and Anegada.

name: Pragmatic Clinical Trial
description: A type of clinical study designed to evaluate the effectiveness of interventions in real-world health system practice.

name: Scorpion Stings
description: The effects, both local and systemic, caused by the bite of SCORPIONS.

name: Hope
description: Belief in a positive outcome.

name: Antihyperkalemic Agents
description: Compounds used to lower excessive POTASSIUM levels in the body.

name: Acetaldehyde Dehydrogenase Inhibitors
description: Compounds that bind to and inhibit the enzymatic activity of acetaldehyde dehydrogenases.

name: Acetylcholine Release Inhibitors
description: Compounds that block release of the neurotransmitter ACETYLCHOLINE.

name: Steroid Synthesis Inhibitors
description: Compounds that bind to and inhibit enzymes involved in the synthesis of STEROIDS.

name: Glycoside Hydrolase Inhibitors
description: Compounds that inhibit or block the activity of GLYCOSIDE HYDROLASES such as ALPHA-AMYLASES and ALPHA-GLUCOSIDASES.

name: Amylin Receptor Agonists
description: Compounds that stimulate the activity of AMYMIN RECEPTORS. Included under this heading is the endogenous form of ISLET AMYLOID POLYPEPTIDE and synthetic compounds that mimic its effect.

name: Antidiuretic Hormone Receptor Antagonists
description: Endogenous compounds and drugs that inhibit or block the activity of ANTIDUIRETIC HORMONE RECEPTORS.

name: beta-Lactamase Inhibitors
description: Endogenous substances and drugs that inhibit or block the activity of BETA-LACTAMASES.

name: Bradykinin B2 Receptor Antagonists
description: Compounds and drugs that inhibit ligand binding or cellular signaling by BRADYKININ B2 RECEPTORS.

name: Calcineurin Inhibitors
description: Compounds that inhibit or block the PHOSPHATASE activity of CALCINEURIN.

name: Calcium Chelating Agents
description: Substances that bind to and sequester CALCIUM ions.

name: Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase I Activators
description: Substances and drugs that stimulate the synthesis or increase the activity of CARBAMOYL PHOSPHATE SYNTHETASE I. Drugs in this class of compounds have been used to treat the genetic disorder, CARBAMOYL-PHOSPHATE SYNTHASE I DEFICIENCY DISEASE.

name: Catechol O-Methyltransferase Inhibitors
description: Compounds and drugs that inhibit or block the activity of CATECHOL O-METHYLTRANSFERASE enzymes. Drugs in this class are used in management of central nervous system disorders such as PARKINSON DISEASE.

name: Travel Nursing
description: A type of nursing practice involving licensed professional nurses who travel to work in temporary nursing positions.

name: CCR5 Receptor Antagonists
description: Compounds and drugs that inhibit or block the activity of CCR5 RECEPTORS.

name: Chloride Channel Agonists
description: A class of drugs that stimulate chloride ion influx through cell membrane channels.

name: Licensed Practical Nurses
description: Health personnel who do not hold professional degrees or credentials, but have completed training and are licensed to provide routine patient care under the direction of registered nurses and physicians.

name: Cystine Depleting Agents
description: Compounds and drugs that react with CYSTINE and convert it into a compound that can be more easily metabolized or intracellularly transported. Drugs in this class have been used to treat CYSTINOSIS.

name: Aromatic Amino Acid Decarboxylase Inhibitors
description: Compounds and drugs that block or inhibit the enzymatic action of AROMATIC AMINO ACID DECARBOXYLASES. Pharmaceutical agents in this category are used in conjunction with LEVODOPA in order to slow its metabolism.

name: Demulcents
description: Compounds that form soothing films on the surface of MUCOUS MEMBRANES. They are generally used as agents to protect the integrity of internal EPITHELIUM.

name: Ornithine Decarboxylase Inhibitors
description: Substances and drugs that inhibit or block the activity of ORNITHINE DECARBOXYLASE.

name: Palliative Medicine
description: A branch of medicine concerned with preventing and relieving the suffering of patients in any stage of disease. Its focus is on comprehensive care and improving the quality of all areas of the patient's life.

name: Dopamine D2 Receptor Antagonists
description: Compounds and drugs that bind to and inhibit or block the activation of DOPAMINE D2 RECEPTORS.

name: Endothelin Receptor Antagonists
description: Compounds and drugs that bind to and inhibit or block the activation of ENDOTHELIN RECECPTORS.

name: Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis
description: A method of disease prevention (abbreviated PrEP) which involves the administration of drugs to at-risk persons who have not been exposed to the disease-causing agent.

name: Endothelin A Receptor Antagonists
description: Compounds and drugs that bind to and inhibit or block the activation of ENDOTHELIN A RECECPTORS.

name: Endothelin B Receptor Antagonists
description: Compounds and drugs that bind to and inhibit or block the activation of ENDOTHELIN B RECEPTORS.

name: Ephemeroptera
description: An Order of aquatic INSECTS comprising about 2,500 species worldwide. It is the only insect group with two flying stages, each with relatively large forewings. The immature stage called naiad or nymph lasts one year in fresh water, and the adult stage is shortlived, lasting from a few minutes to a few days, depending on the species. The Ephemeroptera includes mayflies (also called shadflies)

name: Lipedema
description: Disorder of adipose tissue characterized by symmetric and bilateral enlargement of the lower extremities due to abnormal deposition of SUBCUTANEOUS FAT often in obese women. It is associated with HEMATOMA, pain and may progress to secondary LYMPHEDEMA which is known as lipolymphedema.

name: Animal Culling
description: Selection and removal of individuals from a population or group. Culling is a common strategy with livestock and wildlife, used to control and eradicate diseases or pests, control population size, select for desired genetic characteristics, and maximize economic profit.

name: Zeaxanthins
description: Carotenoids found in fruits and vegetables. Zeaxanthin accumulates in the MACULA LUTEA.

name: Viral Fusion Protein Inhibitors
description: Drugs that are designed to block the action of VIRAL FUSION PROTEINS and prevent VIRUSES from entering the cell.

name: Nicolau Syndrome
description: An uncommon complication of INTRAMUSCULAR INJECTION leading to variable degrees of necrosis of skin and underlying tissue.

name: Cellular Reprogramming
description: A process where fully differentiated or specialized cells revert to pluripotency or a less differentiated cell type.

name: Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy
description: Acute neurological dysfunction during severe SEPSIS in the absence of direct brain infection characterized by systemic inflammation and BLOOD BRAIN BARRIER perturbation.

name: Pregnancy, Interstitial
description: A type of ectopic pregnancy in which the extrauterine EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occurs in the portion of the FALLOPIAN TUBE that traverses the muscular wall of the uterus.

name: Bradykinin Receptor Antagonists
description: Compounds and drugs that inhibit ligand binding or cellular signaling by BRADYKININ RECEPTORS.

name: Bradykinin B1 Receptor Antagonists
description: Compounds and drugs that inhibit ligand binding or cellular signaling by BRADYKININ B1 RECEPTORS.

name: Pregnancy, Angular
description: A rare type of abnormal pregnancy in which EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occurs at a lateral angle of the UTERUS, medial to the uterotubal junction and the ROUND LIGAMENT OF UTERUS.

name: Estrogen Receptor Antagonists
description: Compounds and drugs that bind to and block or inhibit the activation of ESTROGEN RECEPTORS.

name: Pregnancy, Ovarian
description: A type of pregnancy in which EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occurs in an OVARY instead of in the uterine cavity.

name: Pregnancy, Cornual
description: A type of pregnancy in which the EMBRYO IMPLANTATION occurs in the horn of the UTERUS instead of in the uterine cavity, i.e. at the junction of the uterus and one of the FALLOPIAN TUBES.

name: Extracellular Traps
description: Extracellular structure primarily composed of CHROMATIN and associated PROTEASES.

name: Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus
description: A coronavirus first reported in the summer of 2012 in a pneumonia patient in SAUDI ARABIA. It is related to SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME-RELATED CORONAVIRUS. MERS-CoV has an estimated incubation period of 12 days and symptoms include renal failure and severe acute pneumonia with often fatal outcome.

name: Transfusion Reaction
description: Complications of BLOOD TRANSFUSION. Included adverse reactions are common allergic and febrile reactions; hemolytic (delayed and acute) reactions; and other non-hemolytic adverse reactions such as infections and adverse immune reactions related to immunocompatibility.

name: Culturally Competent Care
description: Health care services that are respectful of and responsive to the health beliefs, practices and cultural and linguistic needs of diverse patients. The provider and the patient each bring their individual learned patterns of language and culture to the health care experience which must be transcended to achieve equal access and quality health care.

name: Frankincense
description: Resin exudate from certain trees of the genus BOSWELLIA in the BURSERACEAE family.

name: Serogroup
description: A set of variants within a species of microorganisms that are antigenically, closely related. With bacteria, a serogroup refers to a group that shares a common antigen.

name: Acute-On-Chronic Liver Failure
description: Sudden liver failure in the presence of underlying compensated chronic LIVER DISEASE (e.g., LIVER CIRRHOSIS; HEPATITIS; and liver injury and failure) due to a precipitating acute hepatic insult.

name: Corneal Injuries
description: Damage or trauma inflicted to the CORNEA by external means.

name: Morphological and Microscopic Findings
description: Morphological findings useful in differentiation and classification of results in CYTODIAGNOSIS and related techniques.

name: Atypical Squamous Cells of the Cervix
description: Morphological abnormalities of the cervical EPITHELIUM, usually revealed in PAP SMEAR, which do not meet the criteria for squamous CERVICAL INTRAEPITHELIAL NEOPLASIA or SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMAS of the CERVIX . It may be a sign of infection with certain types of human papillomavirus (HPV).or sign of a benign (not cancer) growth, such as a cyst or polyp or, in menopausal women, of low hormone levels. More testing, such as HPV test, may be needed.

name: Squamous Intraepithelial Lesions of the Cervix
description: A cytological test finding often from PAP SMEARS that shows abnormal lesions of SQUAMOUS EPITHELIAL CELLS of the CERVIX. It is a diagnostic criterion used in the Bethesda System for UTERINE CERVICAL NEOPLASMS and represents the PAP TEST result that is abnormal. Although squamous intraepithelial lesions test result does not mean UTERINE CERVICAL NEOPLASMS it requires follow-ups (e.g., HPV DNA TESTS; and COLPOSCOPY).

name: Adenocarcinoma in Situ
description: A lesion with cytological characteristics associated with invasive adenocarcinoma but the tumor cells are confined to the GLANDULAR EPITHELIAL CELLS of origin. Adenocarcinoma in situ of the CERVIX and the LUNG are the most common.

name: Children's Health Insurance Program
description: Federal program, enacted in 1997, for the funding of children's health insurance coverage at the state level for low-income families, affording them effective protection against erosions in employer sponsored coverage.

name: Circuit-Based Exercise
description: Alternating sets of exercise that work out different muscle groups and that also alternate between aerobic and anaerobic exercises, which, when combined together, offer an overall program to improve strength, stamina, balance, or functioning.

name: Lubricant Eye Drops
description: Ophthalmic solutions that include LUBRICANTS and WETTING AGENTS such as POLYETHYLENE GLYCOL; HYPROMELLOSE; GLYCEROL; PROPYLENE GLYCOL. They are used to treat conditions caused by deficient tear production such as DRY EYE SYNDROME.

name: Hypromellose Derivatives
description: Polymeric compounds that contain repeating units of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose. The properties of hypromellose polymers can vary greatly and are defined by their molecular weight, the percentage of hydroxyl groups, the percentage of hydroxypropyl groups, and viscosity measurements. They are found a broad variety of commercial products such as FOOD ADDITIVES; EXCIPIENTS; and LUBRICANTS.

name: Macular Pigment
description: A yellow pigment that accumulates in the MACULA LUTEA. It is composed of LUTEIN, meso-zeaxanthin, and ZEAXANTHIN.

name: Cryptoxanthins
description: Mono-hydroxylated xanthophylls formed from the hydroxylation of BETA-CAROTENE. Isomers include: beta-cryptoxanthin, alpha-cryptoxanthin, and zeinoxanthin. The alpha- and beta-cryptoxanthin are provitamin A precursors.

name: Factor Xa Inhibitors
description: Endogenous factors and drugs that inhibit or block the activity of FACTOR XA.

name: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder
description: A condition in which a woman suffers from severe depression, irritability, and tension before MENSTRUATION. Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) may involve a wide range of physical or emotional symptoms, which are more severe and debilitating than those seen with premenstrual syndrome (PMS), and which include at least one mood-related symptom. Symptoms usually stop when, or shortly after, menstruation begins.

name: Practice Management, Veterinary
description: The organization and operation of the business aspects of a veterinary practice.

name: Lysholm Knee Score
description: An instrument used to assess the results of rehabilitation from knee injuries, especially those requiring ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT RECONSTRUCTION. It measures recovery of knee joint function based on ACTIVITIES OF DAILY LIVING.

name: Dasyproctidae
description: A family of Central and South American plant-eating rodents comprising the agoutis (Dasyprocta) and acouchis (Myoprocta). They look similar to guinea pigs (CAVIA) but are larger and have longer legs. Their fur is reddish or dark brown.

name: Cuniculidae
description: A family of large (20 to 30 inches long) plant eating rodents found in Central and South America. They are nearly tailless and have chunky bodies, dark brown fur with spotted lines along their sides and back, with stout legs and hind limbs that are longer than the forelimbs, and a large, square head with short ears.

name: Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococci
description: Strains of the genus Enterococcus that are resistant to the antibiotic VANCOMYCIN. The enterococci become resistant by acquiring plasmids carrying genes for VANCOMYCIN RESISTANCE.

name: Drug Liberation
description: Release of drugs from DOSAGE FORMS into solution.

name: Subcutaneous Absorption
description: The uptake of substances via the SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE.

name: Absorption, Physiological
description: Uptake of substances by the body, tissues, or cells. The uptake may occur by various forms of BIOLOGICAL TRANSPORT or by simple DIFFUSION.

name: Oral Mucosal Absorption
description: Uptake of substances into the body via the mucosal surfaces (MUCOUS MEMBRANE) of the oral cavity.

name: Gastrointestinal Absorption
description: Uptake of substances via the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT.

name: Gastric Absorption
description: Uptake of substances via the stomach.

name: Intramuscular Absorption
description: Uptake of substances via muscle tissue.

name: Ocular Absorption
description: Uptake of substances by tissues of the eye.

name: Nasal Absorption
description: Uptake of substances through the nasal mucosa.

name: Respiratory Tract Absorption
description: Uptake of substances via the RESPIRATORY SYSTEM.

name: Rectal Absorption
description: Uptake of substances from the RECTUM.

name: Metabolic Side Effects of Drugs and Substances
description: Specific effects of drugs and substances on metabolic pathways such as those occurring through the CYTOCHROME P-450 ENZYME SYSTEM. These include effects that often result in DRUG INTERACTIONS; FOOD-DRUG INTERACTIONS; and HERB-DRUG INTERACTIONS.

name: Cytochrome P-450 Enzyme Inhibitors
description: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 ENZYMES.

name: Renal Reabsorption
description: The reuptake of water, ELECTROLYTES, and other substances by the KIDNEY to the blood supply.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP1A2 Inhibitors
description: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP1A2.

name: Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease
description: Fatty liver finding without excessive ALCOHOL CONSUMPTION.

name: Familial Primary Pulmonary Hypertension
description: Familial or idiopathic hypertension in the PULMONARY CIRCULATION which is not secondary to other disease.

name: Intestinal Reabsorption
description: The re-uptake of substances in the intestines after their prior absorption from the intestines into the PORTAL SYSTEM and reintroduction into the intestines as substances accumulated in the BILE.

name: Peritoneal Absorption
description: Uptake of substances from the PERITONEAL CAVITY.

name: Hernias, Diaphragmatic, Congenital
description: Protrusion of abdominal structures into the THORAX as a result of embryologic defects in the DIAPHRAGM often present in the neonatal period. It can be isolated, syndromic, non-syndromic or be a part of chromosome abnormality. Associated pulmonary hypoplasia and PULMONARY HYPERTENSION can further complicate stabilization and surgical intervention.

name: Rhinitis, Allergic
description: An inflammation of the NASAL MUCOSA triggered by ALLERGENS.

name: Chikungunya Fever
description: An acute infection caused by a mosquito-borne alphavirus CHIKUNGUNYA VIRUS characterized by RASH; FEVER; JOINT PAINS; CONJUNCTIVITIS; MENINGOENCEPHALITIS; LYMPHOPENIA; and THROMBOCYTOPENIA.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP1B1
description: A cytochrome P450 aryl hydrocarbon hydroxylase that has specificity for ESTROGENS which it converts into 4-hydroxy estrogens. CYP1B1 has been shown to be physiologically important for FETAL DEVELOPMENT with mutations in the CYP1B1 gene resulting in congenital forms of GLAUCOMA and Peter's anomaly.

name: Cerebrospinal Fluid Leak
description: Discharge of cerebrospinal fluid through a hole through the skull bone most commonly draining from the nose (CEREBROSPINAL FLUID RHINORRHEA) or the ear (CEREBROSPINAL FLUID OTORRHEA).

name: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo
description: Idiopathic recurrent VERTIGO associated with POSITIONAL NYSTAGMUS. It is associated with a vestibular loss most often with OTOCONIA dislodge but without other neurological or auditory signs. Unlike in LABYRINTHITIS and VESTIBULAR NEURONITIS, inflammation in the ear is not observed.

name: Myotonin-Protein Kinase
description: Serine/threonine protein kinase responsible for various SKELETAL MUSCLE functions; HEART CONDUCTION SYSTEM activity; calcium HOMEOSTASIS; calcium uptake by SARCOPLASMIC RETICULUM and SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY. It is encoded by the DMPK gene and its abnormal EXPANDED TRINUCLEOTIDE REPEAT of CTG in the 3'-UTR is associated with MYOTONIC DYSTROPHY 1.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2A6
description: A cytochrome P450 enzyme that has specificity for the 7-hydroxylation of coumarin.

name: Absorption, Radiation
description: The uptake or transfer of energy from RADIATION.

name: Thyroid Carcinoma, Anaplastic
description: An aggressive THYROID GLAND malignancy which generally occurs in IODINE-deficient areas in people with previous thyroid pathology such as GOITER. It is associated with CELL DEDIFFERENTIATION of THYROID CARCINOMA (e.g., FOLLICULAR THYROID CARCINOMA; PAPILLARY THYROID CANCER). Typical initial presentation is a rapidly growing neck mass which upon metastasis is associated with DYSPHAGIA; NECK PAIN; bone pain; DYSPNEA; and NEUROLOGIC DEFICITS.

name: Mesenteric Ischemia
description: Ischemic tissue injury produced by insufficient perfusion of intestinal tissue by the MESENTERIC CIRCULATION (i.e., CELIAC ARTERY; SUPERIOR MESENTERIC ARTERY; INFERERIOR MESENTERIC ARTERY; and MESENTERIC VEINS). It can progress from ISCHEMIA; EDEMA; and GANGRENE of the bowel wall to PERITONITIS and cardiovascular collapse.

name: Renal Elimination
description: The discharge of substances from the blood supply via the URINARY TRACT.

name: Vitamin D3 24-Hydroxylase
description: A cytochrome P-450 enzyme that has specificity for CHOLECALCIFEROL (Vitamin D3). It hydroxylates the molecule at carbon position 24.

name: Hepatobiliary Elimination
description: The removal of substances from the blood supply via the LIVER and BILIARY TRACT.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2B6 Inhibitors
description: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2B6.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C8 Inhibitors
description: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2C8.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C9 Inhibitors
description: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2C9.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C19 Inhibitors
description: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2C19.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2D6 Inhibitors
description: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2D6.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2E1 Inhibitors
description: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2E1.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP3A Inhibitors
description: Drugs and compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP3A.

name: Cytochrome P-450 Enzyme Inducers
description: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 ENZYMES.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP1A2 Inducers
description: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP1A2.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2B6 Inducers
description: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2B6.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C8 Inducers
description: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2C8.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C19 Inducers
description: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2C19.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C9 Inducers
description: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2C9.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2D6 Inducers
description: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2D6.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2E1 Inducers
description: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP2E1.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP3A Inducers
description: Drugs and compounds that induce the synthesis of CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP3A.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2B6
description: A cytochrome P450 enzyme subtype that oxidizes a diverse array of XENOBIOTICS. The expression of CYP2B6 varies widely between individuals which is due to the high rate of GENETIC POLYMORPHISMS. Examples of drugs metabolized by CYP2B6 include BUPROPION; efavirenz; CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE; and MEPERIDINE.

name: Malformations of Cortical Development, Group I
description: Cortical malformations secondary to abnormal neuronal and glial CELL PROLIFERATION or APOPTOSIS in NEUROGENESIS. This group includes congenital MICROCEPHALIES; MICROLISSENCEPHALIES, megalencephalies, HEMIMEGALENCEPHALIES and cortical dysplasias with balloon cells.

name: Malformations of Cortical Development, Group III
description: Cortical malformations secondary to abnormal cortical maturation after CELL MIGRATION in NEUROGENESIS. This group includes injury to the cortex during later stages of cortical development such as POLYMICROGYRIA and focal cortical dysplasias.

name: Hemimegalencephaly
description: Rare MALFORMATIONS OF CORTICAL DEVELOPMENT, GROUP I characterized by the enlargement of one side of the brain. It is associated with seizures, partial paralysis, and mental retardation.

name: Polymicrogyria
description: Heterogeneous disorders of cortical malformation characterized by excessive and small fused gyri and shallow sulci of the CORTEX with abnormal cortical lamination. It is considered a malformation secondary to abnormal post-migrational development of the neurons during cerebral cortical development and is associated with EPILEPSY and learning difficulties.

name: Schizencephaly
description: Cortical malformations characterized by grey matter-lined cleft or cyst that extends from the EPENDYMA often to the PIA MATER outer surface. The grey matter that lines the cleft is often POLYMICROGYRIA. It is associated with developmental delay, motor disturbance and seizures.

name: Porencephaly
description: Cortical malformations characterized by white matter-lined cleft or cyst associated with ISCHEMIA and hemorrhagic insults. Symptoms include delayed growth and development, HYPOTONIA; SEIZURES; SPASTIC HEMIPLEGIA and MACROCEPHALY; MICROCEPHALY; or HYDROCEPHALUS. Mutations in the genes encoding COLLAGEN TYPE IV are associated with familial types.

name: Common Data Elements
description: Data elements that are common to multiple data sets across different studies.

name: Glossoptosis
description: Posterior displacement of the TONGUE toward the PHARYNX. It is often a feature in syndromes such as in PIERRE ROBIN SYNDROME and DOWN SYNDROME and associated with AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION during sleep (OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNEAS).

name: Broca Area
description: Functional neuroanatomical region of the inferior frontal gyrus consisting of pars opercularis and pars triangularis. It is important in SPEECH and LANGUAGE production. Injuries to Broca area are associated with BROCA APHASIA and APRAXIA.

name: Limbic Lobe
description: The medial surface of the cerebral hemisphere around the brain stem.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C8
description: A liver microsomal cytochrome P450 hydroxylase that oxidizes a broad spectrum of substrates including STEROIDS, FATTY ACIDS, and XENOBIOTICS. Examples of pharmaceutical substrates for CYP2C8 include; PACLITAXOL; torsemide; and; AMODIAQUINE

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C9
description: A cytochrome P-450 subtype that has specificity for acidic XENOBIOTICS. It oxidizes a broad range of important clinical drugs that fall under the categories of NONSTEROIDAL ANTI-INFLAMMATORY AGENTS; HYPOGLYCEMIC AGENTS; ANTCOAGULANTS; and DIURETICS.

name: Limonene Hydroxylases
description: Members of the P-450 enzyme family that take part in the hydroxylation of limonene.

name: Cytochrome P-450 CYP2C19
description: A cytochrome P-450 enzyme subtype that oxidizes several important groups of drugs including many PROTON PUMP INHIBITORS and ANTICONVULSANTS.

name: Euterpe
description: A genus in the family Arecaceae. They are a source of ACAI BERRIES.

name: Phoeniceae
description: Tribe of palms in the subfamily Coryphoideae, family Arecaceae.

name: Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome
description: An hereditary hemolytic uremic syndrome associated with variations in the gene that encodes COMPLEMENT FACTOR H, or the related proteins CFHR1 and CFHR3. Disease often progresses to CHRONIC KIDNEY FAILURE without the prodromal symptoms of ENTEROCOLITIS and DIARRHEA that characterize typical hemolytic uremic syndrome.

name: Activation, Metabolic
description: The conversion of an exogenous substance by a biological system resulting in the production on an active metabolite.

name: Lennox Gastaut Syndrome
description: A childhood-onset epilepsy syndrome.

name: Delay Discounting
description: The tendency to devalue an outcome as a function of its temporal delay or probability of achievement. It can be evaluated in a psychological paradigm that involves the choice between receiving a smaller immediate reward or a larger delayed reward, and may be used to provide a measure of impulsive behavior.

name: Salivary Elimination
description: The discharge of substances from the blood supply via diffusion into the SALIVA from the ORAL MUCOSA or from the SALIVARY GLANDS.

name: Xenophobia
description: Intense or irrational dislike or fear of anything that is strange or foreign, particularly of people who are strangers or foreigners. It is an attitudinal orientation of hostility against non-natives in a given population that includes attitudes, prejudices and behavior that reject, exclude or vilify persons, based on the perception that they are outsiders or foreigners to the community, society or national identity.

name: Prepulse Inhibition
description: A neurophysiological phenomenon in which the response to a startling stimulus (pulse) is decreased when a weaker prestimulus (prepulse) precedes it closely in time. It is used as an operational measure of sensorimotor gating.

name: Respiratory Sinus Arrhythmia
description: A naturally occurring variation in heart rate that occurs during a BREATHING cycle, where the time between heartbeats is shortened during inspiration and prolonged during expiration. It is not the same as SINUS ARRHYTHMIA, the disorder.

name: Ethnic Cleansing
description: Expulsion of a population from a given territory due to religious or ethnic discrimination, political, strategic or ideological considerations, or a combination of these.

name: Interoception
description: The perception of and sensitivity to stimuli originating inside of the body. It is a sense of the physiological condition of the entire body.

name: Wernicke Area
description: Functional region comprising posterior part of the SUPERIOR TEMPORAL GYRUS in the dominant cerebral hemisphere (see CEREBRAL DOMINANCE) and often portions of the PARIETAL LOBE. Along with BROCA AREA it is important in SPEECH and LANGUAGE processes. A lesion in the area is associated with WERNICKE APHASIA and CONDUCTION APHASIA.

name: Cerebellar Vermis
description: A subregion of the CEREBELLAR CORTEX, located along the midsagittal plane of the CEREBELLUM.

name: Acalypha
description: Nettle-like plants in the subfamily Acalyphoideae. Acalypha is the largest genus in the Euphorbiaceae family.

name: Neuroscience Nursing
description: The nursing specialty focusing on the needs of patients with dysfunction of the NERVOUS SYSTEM.

name: Congenital Microtia
description: Malformation of external portion of EAR AURICLE.

name: Voriconazole
description: A triazole antifungal agent that specifically inhibits STEROL 14-ALPHA-DEMETHYLASE and CYTOCHROME P-450 CYP3A.

name: Zona Incerta
description: A region of the subthalamus located ventral to the THALAMUS and dorsal to the SUBTHALAMIC NUCLEUS.

name: Pontine Tegmentum
description: The dorsal region of pons bounded by the middle CEREBELLAR PEDUNCLES and the ventral part of the pons. It is continuous with the TEGMENTUM MESENCEPHALI and contains CEREBELLAR NUCLEI, lemnisci and RETICULAR FORMATION.

name: College Fraternities and Sororities
description: Local or national organizations of college students, primarily for social purposes, usually with secret initiations and rites and a name composed of two or three Greek letters.

name: Parabrachial Nucleus
description: A cell group in the pontine tegmentum surrounding the surfaces of the superior CEREBRAL PEDUNCLE of the PONS.

name: Oxalidaceae
description: Wood-sorrel family in the order Oxalidales. Some species of RUMEX (of the family POLYGONACEAE) also known by the common name of sorrels.

name: Averrhoa
description: Tropical trees in the family Oxalidaceae

name: Abducens Nucleus
description: A region in the PONTINE TEGMENTUM that is the nucleus of the ABDUCENS NERVE.

name: Facial Nucleus
description: A region in the pontine tegmentum that is the nucleus of the FACIAL NERVE.

name: Flower Essences
description: Aqueous extracts of flowers that are used in healing systems.

name: Monks
description: Members of a religious community of men typically living under vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience.

name: Nuns
description: Members of a religious community of women typically living under vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience.

name: Superior Olivary Complex
description: An auditory brainstem structure in the pontine tegmentum and a part of the olivary nucleus complex. It contains several nuclei associated with auditory localization and is a component of ascending and descending auditory pathways.

name: Trapezoid Body
description: A region in the pontine tegmentum containing nuclei and fibers associated with AUDITORY PATHWAYS.

name: Religious Personnel
description: Persons that live and work according to a religious vocation, or calling, to a consecrated or ordained life.

name: Barrington's Nucleus
description: A nucleus in the pons with exon projections to the sacral parasympathetic nucleus associated with bladder control.

name: Kolliker-Fuse Nucleus
description: A nucleus in the pons associated with RESPIRATION RATE control.

name: Middle Cerebellar Peduncle
description: WHITE MATTER consisting of a large bundle of paired fibers originating in the pontine nuclei in the pre pontis and the nucleus reticularis tegmenti pontis projecting to the contralateral cerebral cortex.

name: Oculomotor Nuclear Complex
description: A collection of nuclei in the midbrain tegmentum for the OCULOMOTOR NERVE fibers.

name: Edinger-Westphal Nucleus
description: Nucleus in the oculomotor nuclear complex associated with oculomotor activities and stress adaptation.

name: Pars Reticulata
description: A region in the substantia nigra located ventral and lateral to the PARS COMPACTA.

name: Pars Compacta
description: A region in the substantia nigra located dorsal to the PARS RETICULATA.

name: Cerebral Crus
description: Anterior portion of the cerebral peduncle which contains the motor tracts.

name: Tectospinal Fibers
description: A neural tract which connects the TECTUM MESENCEPHALI and the SPINAL CORD and is involved in head and eye movement coordination.

name: Nucleus Raphe Magnus
description: A nucleus located directly rostral to the NUCLEUS RAPHE OBSCURUS in the pontine part of the Raphe nuclei. Another pontine nucleus located directly rostral to the magnus nucleus is the nucleus raphe pontis.

name: Dorsal Raphe Nucleus
description: The dorsal region of the raphe nucleus which is a source of the SEROTONERGIC NEURONS innervating the TELENCEPHALON; DIENCEPHALON; MESENCEPHALON; and RHOMBENCEPHALON.

name: Nucleus Raphe Pallidus
description: A nucleus in the medullary Raphe nuclei located rostral to the NUCLEUS RAPHE OBSCURUS and caudal to the NUCLEUS RAPHE MAGNUS.

name: Nucleus Raphe Obscurus
description: A nucleus in the medullary Raphe nuclei located caudal to the NUCLEUS RAPHE PALLIDUS.

name: Cerebral Peduncle
description: Ventral portion of the mesencephalon including the MIDBRAIN TEGMENTUM; CRUS CEREBRI; and the PRETECTUM. It does not include tectum mesencephali and TROCHLEAR NERVE.

name: Ovarian Reserve
description: Capacity of the ovary to provide viable eggs.

name: Spatial Memory
description: Memory related to spatial information.

name: Spatial Learning
description: A process through which individuals encode information about their environmental CUES to facilitate SPATIAL NAVIGATION.

name: Spatial Navigation
description: Process by which organisms use various cues to develop a route to a destination and their ability to travel such a planned route.

name: Spatial Processing
description: Integration of spatial information perceived by visual and/or auditory CUES.

name: Rubus
description: A plant genus of the family Rosaceae whose members include blackberries and raspberries.

name: Optic Tract
description: Nerve fiber originating from the OPTIC CHIASM that connects predominantly to the LATERAL GENICULATE BODIES. It is the continuation of the VISUAL PATHWAY that conveys the visual information originally from the RETINA to the optic chiasm via the OPTIC NERVES.

name: Neurodevelopmental Disorders
description: These are a group of conditions with onset in the developmental period. The disorders typically manifest early in development, often before the child enters grade school, and are characterized by developmental deficits that produce impairments of personal, social, academic, or occupational functioning. (From DSM-5).

name: Hyperlactatemia
description: Increase in blood LACTATE concentration often associated with SEPTIC SHOCK; LUNG INJURY; SEPSIS; and DRUG TOXICITY. When hyperlactatemia is associated with low body pH (acidosis) it is LACTIC ACIDOSIS.

name: Karoshi Death
description: Sudden death from overwork, most often as a result of acute CARDIOVASCULAR STROKE.

name: Influenza A Virus, H10N8 Subtype
description: A subtype of INFLUENZA A VIRUS comprised of the surface proteins HEMAGGLUTININ 10 and NEURAMINIDASE 8. The H10N8 subtype usually infects domestic birds (POULTRY) but there have been some human infections reported.

name: Forests
description: An ecosystem dominated by trees and other woody vegetation.

name: Tundra
description: An ecosystem dominated by grasses, lichens, mosses, sedges and shrubs in cold landscapes or at high elevations where a layer of the ground remains perennially frozen (PERMAFROST).

name: Permafrost
description: Perennially frozen layer of soil below the surface in tundra.

name: Rainforest
description: Forests with high average annual rainfall.

name: Grassland
description: An ecosystem dominated by grasses (POACEAE) with few trees or shrubs.

name: Absorption, Physicochemical
description: The physical process of passing into, or being taken up or taken in by a substance.

name: Citrullus colocynthis
description: A plant species of the family CUCURBITACEAE distributed tropically and subtropically mainly in North Africa and Asia. It is a medicinal plant of TRADITIONAL MEDICINE and well known in ancient medicine as the wild gourd.

name: Toxicokinetics
description: The quantitation of the body's metabolism of toxic xenobiotic compounds, as measured by the plasma concentration of the toxicant at various time points.

name: Endothelial Progenitor Cells
